en: I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the god of sacrifice, the officiating priest,
the invoker, the bestower of the most abundant treasures.
Agni is worthy of praise by the ancient seers and indeed by those of the present day.
He shall bring the gods hither;
through Agni, may he obtain wealth and nourishment day by day—
wealth that is glorious and most rich in heroic sons.
O Agni, whatever sacrifice or rite you encompass on every side,
that alone goes to the gods.
Agni is the Hotṛ-priest, possessed of the insight of a seer, true, and most richly renowned.
May the god come with the gods. When, O Agni, you perform what is auspicious for the donor— that, O Aṅgiras, shall be true for you.
Day by day, O Agni, we approach you with our thought, O illuminator of the darkness,
bringing homage to you. To you who reign over the sacrifices, the radiant guardian of the cosmic order (ṛta), we come.
Increasing in your own abode,
O Agni, be easy of access to us as a father is to his son;
be with us for our well-being.
O Vāyu, come hither, O beautiful one; these Soma juices have been prepared for you.
Drink of them and hear our invocation.
O Vāyu, the singers praise you with hymns.
The Sutasomas, who know the days.
O Vāyu, your mingling speech goes forth to the donor,
far-reaching for the drinking of the soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, come hither with refreshments to these pressed juices;
for the drops long for you both. O Vāyu and Indra, you who possess abundant wealth, you take notice of the pressed juices.
Come hither, O you two; run quickly!
O Vāyu and Indra, come to the prepared place of the one who presses the soma;
come swiftly with this prayer, O heroes.
I invoke Mitra of purified will and Varuṇa, the destroyer of enemies,
as they perfect our prayer dripping with clarity.
By the Eternal Law, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who increase the Law and touch the Law.
You two have attained a lofty mental power.
O sages, Mitra and Varuṇa, our progenitors, wide-dwelling, you two bestow skillful and active dexterity.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor with swift hands, you who enjoy many things, bestow sacrificial food upon us.
O Aśvins, doers of many marvels, O heroes, [favor us] with powerful insight.
O wise ones, accept our songs!
O wonder-workers, Nāsatyas, for you the juices are pressed and the sacrificial grass is strewn;
come, O you whose path is red!
O Indra, come, O you of wondrous luster; these pressed juices long for you.
Purified by the fingers through the strainer, they flow.
O Indra, come, impelled by our prayer and urged on by the sages, to the one who has prepared the libation.
Come near to the sacred hymns of the worshipper;
O Indra, come swiftly to the sacred hymns, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, and take pleasure in the pressed juice of those who offer it.
O protectors, supporters of the people, all you gods, come hither;
you who give, come to the pressed juice of the donor.
O all you gods, crossers of the waters, come quickly to the pressed juice.
Like cows at their pastures,
may all the gods— those who possess the power of coming hither, who are free from malice and guile— enjoy the sacrifice, O bearers of the rite.

May Sarasvatī, the purifier, rich in prizes through her boons, desire our sacrifice— she who is wealthy in inspired thought. She is the impeller of true blessings, making manifest our well-wishing prayers.
Sarasvatī has established the sacrifice;
Sarasvatī, the great flood, makes it manifest with her signal; she rules over all inspired thoughts.
For our protection, day by day we invoke him who fashions beautiful forms, as one calls a good milch-cow for the milker.
O drinker of Soma, come to our libations and drink of the Soma.
The draughts of milk are the exhilaration of the wealthy one;
thus may we find your most intimate favors.
Do not overlook us; come hither!
Go away and ask the wise Indra, the unsubdued, who is better for your friends than you. And let our revilers say, "Depart from us to another!"
Offering worship to Indra alone—
may the people, O Wondrous One, call us fortunate and prosperous;
may we abide in the protection of Indra.
Bring this [soma] to the swift one, who is the glory of sacrifice and the delight of men;
flying, he gladdens his friend.
Having drunk of it, O Śatakratu, you became the slayer of the Vṛtras.
You have protected the prize-winner in the contests for booty.
O Śatakratu, we urge you on, the prize-winner, in these contests for booty,
O Indra, so that you may win riches.
He who is a great fountain of wealth, easy to cross over, the friend of the one who presses the soma—for that Indra, sing!
Come hither; sit down; sing forth unto Indra!
O friends, you who bring hymns of praise,
[serve] Indra at the pressed Soma— him who is most abundant among the many, the lord of all desirable things.
May he indeed be with us for our journey; may he come to us with wealth and with inspired wisdom;
may he come to us with spoils of war.
He whose two bay steeds no enemies can restrain in the clash of battles when they are harnessed.
Sing for that Indra;
these pressed juices flow pure for the drinker of the pressed, for his enjoyment— Soma-draughts mixed with curds.
O Indra, you were born at once grown strong for the drinking of the pressed juice, for preeminence, O wise one. O Indra, lover of songs, let the swift Soma drops enter into you.
May they be auspicious for you, the wise one.
O Śatakratu, the hymns of praise have magnified you; the sacrificial recitations have magnified you;
may our songs of praise magnify you.
May Indra, whose protection is imperishable, win for us this thousandfold booty,
in which all manly powers reside. O Indra, lover of songs, let not mortals do harm to our bodies.
The Lord wards off the weapon of death.
They harness the ruddy, bright one as he moves around those who stand still;
the lights shine in the sky.
They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on both sides— two ruddy, bold steeds that carry the hero.
Making a banner for one who had none, O men, you provide a form for one who was formless.
You were born together with the dawns;
then, according to your own nature, they brought you back again to the state of an embryo,
assuming names worthy of sacrifice.
O Indra, with those who break even what is firm and who bring [the sacrifice] from the cave,
you found the ruddy cows.
Like those seeking the gods according to their thought, our songs have reached the finder of wealth.
The great ones have praised the famous one.
For you shall be seen united with Indra, having come together with him who is fearless— both of you joyful and equal in splendor.
With blameless and radiant hosts, beloved by Indra, the sacrifice shines with power.
From there, O you who traverse the space, come hither from heaven or from the luminous realm above.
Upon him all songs of praise converge.
From here, or from heaven, or from the earthly realm, we seek bounty; or from Indra, the great space.
To Indra indeed the singers sing aloud; to Indra the chanters with their hymns;
Indra the voices have shouted after.
Indra alone is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled with them, yoked by a word.
Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is golden-hued.
Indra raised the sun high in the sky for far-reaching vision;
he split the mountain open with his rays.
O Indra, protect us in the contests for booty and in battles where thousands are won;
O Mighty One, with your mighty aids! We invoke Indra in the great contest for wealth, and we invoke Indra in the small one.
The wielder of the thunderbolt, our ally against the Vṛtras—
O showerer of blessings, O ever-conquering one, ward off that hostile vessel for us,
being irresistible toward us.
In every clash, those hymns which are superior belong to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
I find no adequate praise for him.
Like a bull among the herds, he drives the people forward by his might.
The sovereign, unassailable one, who alone rules over the peoples, over riches,
and over the five tribes— Indra.
We invoke Indra for you from every side, away from all other people;
may he be ours alone. O Indra, [grant] us winning wealth, that which is victorious and ever-conquering.
Bring the most excellent [aid] for our protection,
by which, aided by you, we may strike down with our fists and hold back the Vṛtras with our swift [chariot].
O Indra, protected by you, may we grasp the thunderbolt as a weapon;
may we completely conquer our rivals in battle. O Indra, with you as our ally, may we—through heroic archers—be victorious.
May we overcome those who attack us. Great is Indra, and let there be even greater majesty for the wielder of the thunderbolt;
his power is as vast as the sky.
The men who have sought refuge in you during the confusion for the winning of offspring,
or the inspired poets who are intent on their prayer—
[for them] that belly which drinks Soma most abundantly swells like the ocean.
The vast waters are like the palate; for thus his refreshing bounty is overflowing, great, and rich in cattle—
like a ripe branch for the donor.
For thus indeed are thy manifestations and thy aids for one like me, O Indra;
they are instantly present for the donor.
For thus indeed are his desirable things: the hymn of praise and the recitation of the *uktha* are to be celebrated.
For Indra, for the drinking of Soma. Come, O Indra, and exhilarate yourself with the food [of Soma] through all the Soma-pressings;
you are great, a helper by your might.
With this [soma], send him forth when it is pressed—the exhilarating one for Indra, the exhilarating one; the doer for the one who does all things.
O fair-jawed one, lord of all people, be exhilarated by these exhilarating hymns of praise.
They have accompanied you at the libations; O Indra, these songs have been poured forth toward you,
toward the bull, the lord, who delights in them.
Drive hither the wondrous and desirable gift, O Indra; let it be abundant and sufficient for you.
O Indra, impel us well toward that wealth, making us zealous.
O you of many glories,
bestow upon us, O Indra, great and wide renown, rich in cattle and in strength,
for all our life, imperishable.
Bestow upon us great renown and splendor that wins a thousandfold;
O Indra, grant us those nourishments borne on chariots.
Praising with songs the praiseworthy Indra, the lord of wealth, [we seek] the Lord of Wealth.
To the one who comes to the oblation for protection;
at every pressing, the praiser offers a great song of strength to Indra, the dweller in the home.
The singers of the *gāyatrī* chant thee; those who possess the *arkas* praise the *arka*.
O Lord of a hundred powers, the priests have raised thee up like a pole.
When thou didst ascend from ridge to ridge, thou didst perceive many deeds yet to be done.
Indra perceives that purpose; the bull moves with his herd.
Yoke, O Indra, your two long-maned, vigorous bay horses that fill out the girths. Then, O Soma-drinker, come to hear our songs.
Come, respond to our hymns with your voice; sing out and roar!
O Vasu, Indra, be with our prayer and increase our sacrifice.
An hymn worthy of praise has been recited for Indra, a strengthener for him who bestows many gifts.
May Śakra take delight in our pressed juices and in our friendship. We seek him for friendship, him for wealth, and him for heroic strength.
May that Śakra, Indra, indeed be able to help us, bestowing riches upon us.
O Indra, well-opened and free from dust is the glory bestowed by you;
open the stall of the cows and grant us wealth, O wielder of the stone.
For neither of the two worlds, heaven and earth, can contain you when you are enraged.
Win the sunlit waters; shake the cattle down for us.
O you whose ears are quick to hear, listen to my call; now indeed take to heart my songs.
O Indra, place this hymn of mine even closer than a companion.
For we know you as the most virile one, who hears our call in the contests for booty;
we invoke the aid of the most virile one, that which bestows thousands.
O Indra, son of Kuśika, come now and, being exhilarated, drink our pressed soma.
Prolong our life anew; make the seer a winner of a thousandfold wealth.
O lover of songs, may these hymns encompass you on every side. May these pleasing songs, increasing as you increase, be dear to you.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as vast as the ocean;
the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
O Indra, Lord of Might, through your friendship may we, possessing strength, never fear.
We cry out toward you, the conqueror who is never defeated. The many gifts of Indra do not fail; his aids are unfailing.
When he bestows wealth consisting of cattle as a bounty upon his praisers.
The breaker of forts, the youthful sage of immeasurable power was born;
Indra, the sustainer of every deed, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the much-praised one.
O driver of the chariot, you opened the cave of Vala, who possessed the cattle.
The gods, being urged on, took refuge in you without fear.
O hero, through your gifts I have come back, calling out to the river. O lover of songs, the poets who know this stood near you.
With your wondrous powers, O Indra, you overthrew the guileful Śuṣṇa. The wise know that deed of yours; extend their renown further.
Our hymns of praise have celebrated Indra, the ruler by his might.
He whose gifts are a thousand, or even more—
We choose Agni as our messenger, the all-knowing invoker,
the one of skillful wisdom for this sacrifice.
They ever invoke Agni, Agni, the lord of the people, with invocations—
the bearer of oblations, the one beloved by many.
O Agni, being born, bring the gods here for the one who has strewn the sacrificial grass.
You are our Hotṛ, worthy of praise.
Awaken them who desire you; O Agni, when you go on your mission as messenger, sit with the gods upon the sacrificial grass (barhis).
O you who are invoked with clarified butter, O radiant one, burn against the harmful ones;
O Agni, burn against those possessed by demons.
By means of fire is fire kindled—the sage, the master of the house, the youth.
The carrier of oblations, whose mouth is the sacrificial ladle—
praise Agni the sage at the sacrifice, whose laws are true,
the god who drives away disease.
O Agni, whoever, as a lord of oblations, honors you, the divine messenger—
be his protector. Whoever, possessing oblations, seeks to win over Agni for the feast of the gods.
O Purifier, be gracious to him!
O purifying, radiant Agni, bring the gods here to us,
to our sacrifice and our oblation.
Being thus praised with this newest song,
O Agni, bring us wealth and food accompanied by heroic sons, through your bright radiance and all our invocations of the gods.
Be pleased with this hymn of ours.
Well-kindled, O Agni, bring the gods here for us who offer the oblation;
O Purifier, as the Hotṛ priest, perform the sacrifice.
O Sage Tanūnapāt, make our sacrifice honey-sweet among the gods today, so that they may partake of it.
I invoke here the beloved Narāśaṃsa at this sacrifice.
Honey-tongued, prepared with oblations— O Agni, on your most comfortable chariot, being invoked, bring the gods hither;
you are the Hotṛ-priest appointed by Manu.
O wise ones, strew the sacrificial grass in due order, its back anointed with ghee,
where the vision of immortality is found.
Let the divine doors, which increase the cosmic order and flow with moisture, stand wide open.
For sacrifice today and now indeed;
Night and Dawn, the well-adorned ones, I invoke at this sacrifice to sit upon this sacred grass of ours.
I invoke those two fair-tongued divine Hotṛ-priests, the sages;
may they perform this sacrifice for us.
Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī—the three goddesses who bring bliss.
Let the guileless ones sit upon the sacrificial grass. Here I invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost, who possesses all forms; may he be ours alone.
O divine Lord of the Forest, release the oblation for the gods;
may the consciousness of the giver prevail. With the cry of *svāhā*, perform the sacrifice for Indra in the house of the sacrificer.
There I invoke the gods.
O Agni, come with all these gods to our offerings and songs for the drinking of Soma; come and perform the sacrifice.
The Kaṇvas have invoked you; O Sage, they sing your hymns.
O Agni, come hither with the gods! Indra and Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Mitra and Agni, Pūṣan, and Bhaga—[I invoke them].
The Ādityas and the host of Maruts—
your exhilarating, intoxicating drops are being brought forward,
the drops of honey resting within the vessels.
Seeking your aid, the Kaṇvas, having strewn the sacrificial grass, praise you;
they bring oblations and have prepared the offerings.
The steeds who carry you—whose backs are sprinkled with ghee, who are yoked by thought—are your bearers.
Bring the gods here for the drinking of the Soma;
O Agni, make those worshipful ones who increase the cosmic order accompanied by their wives;
O fair-tongued one, make them drink of the honeyed draught.
Those who are worthy of sacrifice, those who are to be praised— may they drink with their tongue the honeyed [soma] at the cry of *vaṣaṭ*, O Agni.
From the very realm of light of the sun, may all the gods who awaken at dawn [come hither].
The inspired priest shall bring [the offerings] here;
O Agni, with Indra and Vāyu, and with all [the gods], drink the Soma-mead according to the ordinances of Mitra.
O Agni, you are the Hotṛ appointed by Manu; you sit at the sacrifices. As such, perform this sacrifice for us.
Yoke, O God, the ruddy mares to your chariot—the bay and the red ones.
With them, O God, bring [the gods] hither.
O Indra, drink the Soma according to the season; let the exhilarating drops enter you, they whose home is there.
O Maruts, drink according to the season; purify the sacrifice from the office of the Potar. For you indeed are the bounteous givers.
O Gnas, favor our sacrifice; O Neṣṭar, drink according to the season.
For you, O Agni, are the bestower of treasures. Bring the gods here; seat them in the three wombs;
attend to them and drink according to the season.
O Indra, drink the Soma from the Brahmin’s gift according to the seasons;
for your friendship is invincible.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two uphold the power of the steadfast, which is difficult to overcome.
With the season you have approached the sacrifice. The givers of wealth, with pressing-stones in hand,
invoke the god at the sacrifice during the rites.
May the Giver of Wealth bestow upon us those riches that are renowned;
may we win them among the gods.
The Giver of Wealth desires to drink; offer the oblation and step forward!
From the office of the Neṣṭṛ, you are impelled by the seasons.
Since we worship you, the giver of wealth, with the fourth season, then indeed become a bestower of gifts for us.
O Aśvins, drink the honey-sweet draught, you who shine with fire and observe pure vows;
you who, by the season, carry the sacrifice. O benevolent one, by the season you are the leader of the sacrifice through the office of the Gārhapatya fire.
Sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
Let the bay steeds bring you hither, O Indra, the bull, to drink the Soma; O Indra, let those steeds with sun-like eyes bring you.
May these roasted grains dripping with ghee bring the two bay steeds here; may they bring Indra upon his most comfortable chariot.
We invoke Indra at dawn; we invoke Indra as the sacrifice proceeds.
Indra, for the drinking of the Soma!
Come to our pressed juice, O Indra, with your long-maned bay horses;
for we invoke you when the juice is pressed.
Come to this our hymn; come to this pressed libation.
Drink like a thirsty buffalo.
These Soma drops, the pressed juices, are upon the sacred grass.
Drink them for the sake of victory, O Indra!
May this foremost hymn of praise reach your heart as most healing;
then drink the pressed Soma.
Indra goes to every pressed libation for exhilaration;
the slayer of Vṛtra comes to drink the Soma.
O Śatakratu, fulfill this desire of ours with cattle and horses.
Let us, with attentive minds, praise you.
I choose for myself the protection of Indra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign kings. May they both be gracious to us who are such as we are.
For you two are indeed the ones who come for aid at the invocation of a sage such as I; you are the sustainers of the peoples.
O Indra and Varuṇa, satisfy us according to our desire with riches.
We pray to you both for that which is nearest; for yours indeed are the powers, and yours are the benevolent thoughts that bestow the prize of victory.
May we be among those who receive these gifts.
Indra is the lord of those who give a thousandfold; Varuṇa is the one to be praised. He becomes the praiseworthy power of the hymns.
Through the protection of these two, may we win and lay up [wealth].
And may there be a pouring forth [of wealth]. O Indra and Varuṇa, I invoke you both for wondrous bounty;
make us truly victorious.
O Indra and Varuṇa, now indeed, while our prayers desire to win you,
grant us protection.
O Indra and Varuṇa, may this excellent praise which I invoke reach you both.
The joint hymn which you two cause to prosper—
O *Brahmaṇaspati*, make the Soma-presser resound,
even as Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij.
He who is wealthy, who drives away disease, who finds riches, and increases prosperity— may he, the swift one, be with us.
Let not the curse of the stingy man, nor the malice of a mortal, reach us.
Protect us, O Brahmaṇaspati!
That hero indeed suffers no harm whom Indra and Brahmaṇaspati,
and Soma, impel as a mortal.
O Brahmaṇaspati, may you, O Soma, and Indra, and Dakṣiṇā, protect that mortal from distress.
The Lord of the Assembly, the wonderful one, the beloved and desirable friend of Indra.
I have sought for the gain of wisdom.
Without whom even the sacrifice of the wise man does not succeed, he promotes the application of our prayers.
Then he prospers in the performance of the oblation; he makes the sacrifice proceed forward, and the invocation goes to the gods.
I have beheld Narāśaṃsa, the most courageous and the most far-extending.
From heaven, [bring] to us the one who dwells in the seat and is eager for the sacrifice.
To this beautiful rite you are summoned for the protection of the cattle;
O Agni, come with the Maruts.
Neither god nor mortal surpasses your great power of will.
All the gods, free from guile, who know the great realm of space—
They who, fierce and unassailable by might, have sung their hymn of praise— them [I invoke]. They who, fierce and unassailable by might, have sung their hymn of praise— them [I invoke].
Those who are radiant, terrible in form, possessing excellent dominion, and destroyers of enemies;
those gods who sit in the luminous realm above the firmament in heaven.
RV_01.019.06.2 {37} ... RV_01.019.07.1 {37} Those who cause the mountains to sway across the surging ocean—
Those who extend [their power] with rays across the ocean by their might—
I pour forth for you the Soma-mead for the first draught.
RV 1.20.1.1: This hymn has been fashioned by the inspired poets for the sake of the divine race, through [the power of] the mouth.
RV 1.20.1.2: It has been made as the best bestower of jewels.

Those who for Indra fashioned with their mind the two bay steeds yoked by a word, have through their labors attained the sacrifice. They fashioned for the Nāsatyas a comfortable, all-encompassing chariot.
They fashioned the cow that milks at will; the *Ṛbhus*, seeking the straight path and possessing true mantras, made their aged parents young again through their skillful work.
Your exhilarating draughts have come together with Indra accompanied by the Maruts,
and with the Ādityas, the kings.
And that new cup of the divine Tvaṣṭṛ, which was fashioned—
O you who are fourfold and uncreated, bestow upon us treasures three times sevenfold for the one who presses the soma,
each one by means of our excellent praises.

The bearers have maintained [the sacrifice]; through their skillful action, they have obtained among the gods a share worthy of worship. Here I invoke Indra and Agni; we desire the hymn of praise for them both.
Those two, the greatest drinkers of Soma, [drink] the Soma;
those two, Indra and Agni, the men should praise at the sacrifices and adorn them;
sing to those two in Gāyatra hymns.

Those two who are the praises of Mitra, Indra and Agni, we invoke them for the drinking of the Soma, as Soma-drinkers, for the drinking of the Soma. Being mighty, we invoke them hither to this pressed libation.
Indra and Agni, come hither!
O Indra and Agni, you two great lords of the assembly, crush the demons!
Let the devourers be childless!
By that truth, remain awake upon the conscious station; O Indra and Agni, grant us protection.
Awaken the two Aśvins who yoke their chariot at dawn; let them come hither.
For the drinking of this Soma—
those two who possess excellent chariots, who are the best of charioteers, the two gods who touch the heavens— those Aśvins we invoke.
O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honey-sweet and full of truth, sprinkle the sacrifice. For nothing is far for you when you travel on your chariot.
O Aśvins, [come] to the house of the Soma-presser. For protection, I invoke Savitṛ, the golden-handed; he is the knower of the station of the gods.
Praise Savitṛ, the Son of the Waters, for his protection; we desire to follow his sacred laws.
We invoke him, the distributor of wonderful wealth and bounty.
To Savitar, who beholds men, [sing].
O friends, sit down; Savitar is now to be praised by us.
The giver of boons, he makes them beautiful.
O Agni, bring hither the wives of the gods who desire [the sacrifice],
and Tvaṣṭṛ for the drinking of the Soma.
O most youthful Agni, bring the divine women here for our protection, and Hotrā Bhāratī.
Bring Varūtrī and Dhiṣaṇā;
may the goddesses, the wives of the lords of men, with their great protection and shelter, come to us with their aid, their wings unbroken.
Hither I call Indrāṇī for our well-being, Varuṇānī,
and Agnāyī for the drinking of Soma. May the great Heaven and Earth bedew this sacrifice of ours.
May they nourish us with their sustenances. The inspired poets lick with their prayers the ghee-rich milk of those two in the fixed station of the Gandharva.
O Earth, be pleasant, thornless, and a place of rest for us;
grant us wide-spread shelter. From that place where Viṣṇu strode forth, may the gods protect us.
RV 1.22.16.2: By means of the seven abodes of the earth...
RV 1.22.17.1: Viṣṇu strode across this [universe]; in three places he planted his step; his footstep is gathered together in the dust.
RV 1.22.17.2: His footprint is gathered together in the dust.
Viṣṇu, the undeceivable guardian, strode forth his three steps,
thereby upholding the sacred laws. Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made manifest his ordinances.
The close and worthy friend of Indra. The wise ever behold that highest step of Viṣṇu, Like an eye fixed in the sky.
The inspired poets, ever-watchful and full of praise, kindle that highest step of Viṣṇu.
Strong are these Soma juices, pressed with milk; come hither!
O Vāyu, drink those [soma-drops] that have been set forth.
We invoke both gods, Indra and Vāyu, who touch the heavens,
for the drinking of this soma.
Indra and Vāyu, swift as thought, the inspired poets invoke for their protection;
the thousand-eyed lords of prayer. We invoke Mitra and Varuṇa to drink the Soma.
Born with purified skill, those two who by Truth increase Truth, the lords of the light of Truth—
those Mitra and Varuṇa I invoke.
May Varuṇa be our protector, and Mitra with all his aids;
may they both make us richly prosperous. We invoke Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, to drink the Soma.
In harmony with his troop, may he sprinkle [the offering].
O gods, the Marut hosts with Indra as their chief, whose gifts come from Pūṣan—
may you all hear my call.
Slay Vṛtra, O bounteous ones, with Indra as your powerful ally! Let not the malevolent man have power over us.
We invoke all the gods and the Maruts to drink the Soma.
For the sons of Pṛśni are indeed fierce;
like conquerors, the roar of the Maruts goes forth boldly when you go forth for glory, O heroes.
Born from the laughing lightning, may they protect us;
may the Maruts be gracious to us.
O Pūṣan, bring hither the one with the variegated sacrificial grass, the radiant sustainer of heaven.
Like one who finds a lost animal,
Pūṣan, the glowing king, has found him who was hidden and concealed in a cave,
he whose sacrificial grass is variegated.
And so may he, by means of the drops, impel the six yoked ones for me;
let him plow up barley with the cows as it were.
The waters go along their paths like sisters for those performing the sacrifice.
Mixing milk with honey— those waters which are near the sun, or with which the sun is joined— may they speed our sacrifice forward.
I invoke the divine waters where our cattle drink; an oblation is to be prepared for the rivers.
Within the waters is immortality, within the waters is healing, and there is also the praise of the waters.
O gods, you have become possessors of strength.
Soma has told me that within the waters are all healing remedies, as well as Agni, who brings welfare to all, and the waters themselves, which possess every medicine.
O Waters, bestow healing medicine as a protection for my body,
so that I may long behold the sun.
O Waters, carry away this and whatever else is evil within me.
Whatever offense I have committed against you, or whatever falsehood I have uttered;
today I have entered into the waters, we have united with their essence.
O Agni, come hither full of milk; endow me with splendor.
O Agni, unite me with splendor, unite me with progeny, and unite me with long life.
May the gods know me; may Indra know me along with the seers.
Whose now, of which among the immortals, shall we meditate upon the beloved name of the god?
Who will restore us to great Aditi, so that I may behold my father and my mother? We meditate upon the beloved name of the god Agni, the first of the immortals;
he shall restore us to great Aditi, so that I may behold my father and my mother.
O God Savitṛ, Lord of all desirable things, we ever seek a share from you, O giver of abundance.
For indeed, Bhaga, whoever thus exerts himself for you before the onset of reproach—
He has placed benevolence in his two hands.
May we, through your protection, rise up by the grace of Bhaga,
grasping the summit of wealth.
Neither thy dominion, nor thy power, nor thy wrath have even the birds that fly through the air attained;
nor have these waters that flow unceasingly, nor those who disregard the might of the wind. King Varuṇa, whose will is pure, establishes the top of the tree upright above the bottomless depth.
They flow downward; their base is above. May their banners be established within us.
For King Varuṇa has made a broad path for Sūrya to follow. He has provided feet to set down where there was no place, he who speaks away even that which pierces the heart.
O King, you have a hundred physicians and a thousand; let your benevolence be vast and profound.
Drive Nirṛti far away into the distance, and release us from whatever sin we have committed.
Those stars which are set on high and are seen at night—where indeed do they go by day?
The ordinances of Varuṇa are inviolable; the moon goes forth shining in the night.
I seek this of you with a prayer, praising you; for this the sacrificer prays with oblations.
O Varuṇa, be mindful of us here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life.
That indeed they call night, and that day; this very thought my heart reveals to me.
May King Varuṇa release us, he whom Śunaḥśepa, when seized, invoked.
For Śunaḥśepa, when seized and bound to three wooden posts, invoked the Āditya.
May King Varuṇa release him; may the wise, undeceived one loosen his bonds.
O Varuṇa, we appease your wrath with prostrations, with sacrifices, and with oblations.
O wise Asura, O King, ruling over us, loosen the sins we have committed.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us, loosen the lowermost, and loosen the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless within your sacred law for the sake of Aditi. For even as subjects [follow] you, O God Varuṇa, so do we fulfill your ordinance.
Day by day we pay homage to you.
Do not deliver us to the weapon or the blow of one who is angry, nor to the wrath of one who is enraged.
For the sake of your mercy, we would bind your mind with our songs, O Varuṇa, as a charioteer binds a straying horse.
For my prayers, free from anger, fly forth toward you for the sake of greater prosperity.
Like birds to their nests, [we come] to you.
When shall we bring the hero Varuṇa, who possesses the glory of sovereignty, near us— for his mercy— him who is far-seeing?
Like two longing lovers, they both pursue that same goal;
they do not falter for the donor who maintains his sacred vows—
he who knows the track of the birds flying through the mid-air.
He, the lord of the ocean, knows the ships. He, whose vows are firm, knows the twelve months rich in progeny;
he knows him who is born thereafter.
He knows the path of the wind, of the wide, lofty, and great one; he knows those who dwell above. Varuṇa, whose law is firm, has sat down in his dwellings.
Possessing excellent wisdom for the sake of universal sovereignty,
from there he, the discerning one, beholds all wonders—
both those already accomplished and those yet to be done.
May that Āditya of excellent wisdom make for us fair paths at all times;
may he prolong our lives.
Wearing his golden mantle, Varuṇa puts on his bright garment.
His spies have settled all around him—
him whom the deceivers of men do not wish to harm, nor the malevolent ones; no adversaries can overcome that god.
And he who has established incomparable glory among men,
even within our own bellies.
My prayers go forth like cattle toward their pastures.
Desiring him of far-reaching vision...
Let us now speak together again, since the honey has been brought to me;
like a Hotar-priest, you shall consume what is dear.
Behold now him who is visible to all; behold his chariot upon the earth!
May he take pleasure in these my songs.
O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation today and be gracious!
Seeking your aid, I call upon you.
O wise one, you rule over all, both heaven and earth;
as such, hear me on your journey.
Loosen the uppermost bond for us, untie the middle bond, and release the lower ones so that we may live.
Clothe yourself in garments, O worthy of sacrifice, O Lord of Strengths!
Sacrifice this our rite for us.
O most youthful Agni, as our desirable Hotṛ-priest, sit ever with our prayers and with heaven-reaching speech.
The father indeed offers sacrifice for his son,
the kinsman for his kinsman, and the excellent friend for his friend.
O destroyers of enemies, may Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman come to our sacred grass.
May they sit down like men;
O ancient Hotṛ, rejoice in this our friendship. Listen well to these songs of praise.
For whatever god after god we worship in this perpetual succession, in you alone is the oblation offered.
May he be dear to us, the lord of the people, the delightful and choice-worthy Hotṛ-priest.
We are dear with our own sacred fires;
for the gods, possessing their own sacred fires, have bestowed desirable wealth upon us. Possessing our own sacred fires, we meditate [upon them].
Then let there be mutual praises between us, both the immortals and the mortals.
O Agni, with all your fires, [accept] this sacrifice and this speech.
Grant us favor, O son of strength!
With homages, I shall praise you, Agni, like a prize-winning horse,
you who rule over the sacrifices.
May he indeed, our son of great power, whose stride is wide, the most gracious one,
the bounteous giver, be ours. May he protect us from afar and from near, from the mortal who intends evil against us.
Protect us always, O you who possess all life!
O Agni, announce this our newest song of praise among the gods, so that we may win gain.
Grant us a share in the highest spoils, and in those that are middling; bestow upon us wealth from the nearest source.
You are the distributor, O you of wondrous luster, present at the very edge of the river’s wave.
Immediately you flow for the donor.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty— he shall be the master of eternal refreshments.
O mighty one, no one at all can overcome him; his strength is worthy of renown. May he, who belongs to all people, be a conqueror through his steeds for the sake of booty.
May he be the winner [of wealth] through the inspired poets. O you who are awakened by praise, perform that for every clan worthy of sacrifice;
offer a beautiful hymn of praise to Rudra.
May he, the great one, free from pride, whose banner is smoke, and who is many-shining,
impel us toward wisdom and toward strength.
Like a wealthy lord of the people, may that divine banner hear us.
Through hymns, Agni is the one of great luster.
Homage to the great, homage to the small, homage to the young, and homage to the aged.
Let us sacrifice to the gods if we are able; O gods, may I not incur the reproach of those who are superior.
Where the broad-based pressing-stone stands upright for the sake of extracting the juice, O Indra,
there you have drunk repeatedly of the soma pressed by the mortar.
Where the two pressing-boards are fashioned like buttocks, [there you have drunk].
RV_01.028.03.1 {25} Where the woman learns the *apacyava* and the *upacyava*,
Where they bind the churning-stick like one who has harnessed reins, [there you go].
O *ulūkhala*...
For indeed, O mortar, though you are joined in every single house, [you are the best].
Here, speak most brilliantly, like the drum of those who sacrifice.
And indeed, O Lord of the Forest, the wind blows through your top;
therefore, O mortar, press out the Soma for Indra to drink.
The two who win the sacrifice, the best at winning booty, for they are held aloft;
like two bay horses, they devour the soma-juices.
O two Lords of the Forest, lofty ones, with the lofty pressers, [favor us] today.
For Indra, press the honeyed juice. Bring the remnant from the two vessels; pour the *soma* onto the filter;
place it upon the ox-hide.
For even though we are, O truthful Soma-drinkers,
as if unpraised, O Indra, do you indeed grant us hope for cattle, horses, and beautiful thousands, O Lord of abundant wealth!
O fair-cheeked one, Lord of spoils, O possessor of power, let your wondrous deed be manifest!
Lull them to sleep, O Indra; let those who look at each other with hostility fall asleep, never to wake again.
Let those enemies sleep, and let the bountiful ones, O Hero, awaken.
Crush the braying donkey, O Indra, who mocks you with such wickedness.
Let the *kuṇḍṛṇācī* fly far away from the forest like the wind. Strike down every shrieker; crush the *kṛkadāśva*.
Like those seeking booty, we call Indra hither, the Lord of a Hundred Powers, as we would a swift steed.
Pour out the most bountiful one with drops of Soma.
He who [drinks] a hundred of the pure ones, or a thousand of those mixed with grain—
let him flow forth like water down a slope.

When they come together for the sake of the impetuous exhilaration, indeed, within his belly he possesses a vast expanse like the ocean. This [Soma] of yours you strike down, like a pigeon to its nest.
You do not disregard that speech;
O Hero, Lord of bounties, you who are borne by songs, may there be for you abundant prosperity and truthful speech.
Stand up for our protection in this contest, O Śatakratu;
let us two speak together in the assemblies.
In every endeavor, in every battle, we invoke you, the most powerful one.
O friends, [call] Indra for our protection.
May he indeed come hither if he hears us, with his thousandfold aids and with strengths, to our invocation.
I call upon the hero of many powers, who dwells in the ancient abode,
whom your father of old invoked. O you who are invoked by many, we, possessing all desirable things, urge you on.
O Friend, O Vasu, for those who praise you;
O Soma-drinker, for us who possess beautiful jaws, we who are drinkers of Soma;
O Friend, wielder of the thunderbolt, for your friends.
O Soma-drinker, O friend, wielder of the thunderbolt, let it be so; act accordingly so that we may desire thy favor for our prosperity.
May there be for us, at the shared banquet with Indra, wealthy and abundant provisions.
May we, possessing food, rejoice through those [songs].
O Bold One, one like you, having come in person to the singers,
has indeed opened up [the way] for us as if between two wheels.
When you, O Śatakratu, come to the service of the singers according to their desire,
you open up [the wealth] with your powers as if it were a closed door.
Constantly has Indra won riches with his snorting, roaring, and panting [steeds].
May he, the wonder-worker, grant us a chariot of gold; may he, the winner, grant us gain for our winning. He has bestowed it upon us.
O Aśvins, come with your powerful chariot to this place rich in horses, cattle, and gold, O wonder-workers! For your immortal chariot, O wonder-workers, is yoked with a single team.
The Aśvins are driven upon the ocean;
on the summit of the unassailable one, you have guided the wheel of the chariot;
the other [wheel] travels around the sky.
O Uṣas, dear to all, what mortal may enjoy you, the immortal one?
To whom do you go, O radiant one? For we have meditated upon you from near and from afar.
Like a dappled, ruddy horse—
O Daughter of Heaven, come hither with those strengths of yours; bestow wealth upon us.
O Agni, you were the first Aṅgiras, the seer; as a god, you became the auspicious friend of the gods.
Under your ordinance, the Maruts—the wise ones, active through their insight, with glittering spears—were born.
O Agni, you, the best of the Aṅgirases, the sage, encompass the sacred law (*vrata*) of the gods.

Pervasive for the entire world, wise, born of two mothers, he lies down in many ways for the sake of the living man. O Agni, you first became manifest to Mātariśvan through your skillful wisdom for Vivasvat.
The two worlds, heaven and earth, trembled at the choosing of the Hotṛ-priest; O Lord of Great Wealth, you bore the burden and performed the sacrifice.
O Agni, you made the heaven roar for Manu; for the well-doing Purūravas, you, the greater doer of good, [acted].
When you are released from your parents by your own vigor, they led you forward from the first to the later [state] again.
O Agni, you are the bull who increases prosperity; you become worthy of renown for the one who raises the ladle.
He who understands the oblation and the cry of *vaṣaṭ*, you, O sole life-force, seek to win over the clans at the beginning.
O Agni, you deliver the man who follows a crooked path in the assembly, O far-seeing one, when he is in need.
He who, in the clash for heroes or in the pursuit of wealth, even with few men, strikes down many in the encounter.
O Agni, you establish that mortal in the highest immortality for glory day by day—
you who, being thirsty, create bliss for both races and provide nourishment for the patron.
O Agni, being praised, make us a glorious singer for the winning of riches.
May we succeed in our work with this new rite; O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!

O Agni, you who are blameless and watchful among the gods, dwell in the lap of your parents. Be the protector of our bodies and the guardian of the singer; as a bringer of prosperity, you bestow all wealth upon us.
O Agni, you are our guardian, you are our father; you are the creator of our strength, and we are your kinsmen.
Hundreds and thousands of riches come together unto you, the protector of the sacred law, the invincible one who possesses noble heroes.
O Agni, the gods made you the first living breath for the sake of life, the lord of the people of Nahuṣa.
They have made Iḷā the instructor of mankind, since the son of my father is born.
O Agni, O worshipful god, protect us—the patrons and our own bodies—with your guardians.
You are the savior of our children and grandchildren and of our cattle, watching over them unblinkingly in your sacred law.
O Agni, you are kindled as a four-eyed guardian for the sacrificer who is without a quiver;
you, who are to be offered oblations, protect him from the wolf so that he may be sustained, for even the lowly man’s prayer you favor with your mind.
O Agni, for the priest who praises you widely, you win that most desirable and supreme wealth.

Even for the needy, you are called the provident father; you instruct the simple one, being more wise than the wise in all directions. O Agni, you protect the man who offers the sacrificial fee on every side, like well-sewn armor.
He whose food is sweet, who makes his dwelling pleasant, and who performs the sacrifice of living beings—he is the very image of heaven.
O Agni, forgive this our transgression; forgive this path upon which we have traveled from afar.
You are the kinsman, the father, the guardian of those worthy of Soma; you are the refuge and the inspirer of mortals.
O pure Agni, Angiras, like Manu, like Aṅgiras, and like Yayāti, sit here in this dwelling as of old.
Come hither, bring the divine folk, seat them upon the sacred grass (*barhis*), and sacrifice to the beloved one.

O Agni, grow strong by this prayer (*brahman*), whether we have performed it for you through our skill or through our knowledge. And lead us toward greater prosperity; unite us with your benevolence that is rich in strength (*vāja*).
I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time.
He slew the serpent, he pierced the water-courses, and he cleft asunder the bellies of the mountains.
He slew the serpent resting upon the mountain; Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the roaring thunderbolt.
Like lowing cows, the flowing waters have gone straight down to the ocean.
Acting like a bull, he chose the Soma; at the Trikadruka rites, he drank of the pressed juice. Maghavan took up his missile, the thunderbolt; with it, he slew him, the first-born of the dragons.
When you, O Indra, slew the first-born of the great ones, and destroyed the magic of the deceivers along with their magic;
when you then brought forth the sun, the sky, and the dawn—since that time, truly, you have found no enemy.
Indra slew Vṛtra, the worst of Vṛtras, the shoulderless one, with his great thunderbolt, his mighty weapon.
Like a serpent whose limbs have been severed by a thunderbolt, he lies prostrate upon the earth.
Like a headstrong warrior who failed to fight, he challenged the great hero, the mighty crusher, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*.
He did not survive the onset of his weapons; shattered, the enemy of Indra was crushed to pieces.
Footless and handless, he challenged Indra; upon his back Indra struck him with his thunderbolt.
Vṛtra, the eunuch who sought to be a match for the bull, lay scattered in many places.
Like a broken reed, as he lies there, the waters flow over him, rising up to their will.

Even those whom Vṛtra encompassed with his might, of them the serpent became one whose head lay at the feet. Vṛtra’s mother was cast down; Indra brought down his deadly weapon upon her. The son was above, the father below; Dānu lies there like a cow with her calf.
The waters flow forth from the secret hiding place of Vṛtra, whose body was cast into the midst of the motionless, unsheltered mountain ridges; Indra’s enemy sank into long-lasting darkness.
The waters stood obstructed, having the Dāsa as their lord and the serpent as their guardian, like cows held captive by a Paṇi.
When the opening of the waters was covered, you struck down Vṛtra and threw it open.
O Indra, you became the horse’s tail when the god alone struck at you with his bolt. You won the cattle, O hero, you won the Soma, and you released the seven rivers to flow.
Neither lightning nor thunderbolt could resist him, nor the mist and the hailstorm that he scattered.
When Indra and Ahi fought, Maghavan emerged victorious over them all.
O Indra, whom did you see as a protector for Ahi when fear entered your heart after you had struck him down?
When he crossed the nine and ninety flowing rivers like a frightened falcon traversing the mists;
when Indra, the king of what has been settled and of what is yet to be, the wielder of the thunderbolt, went forth against the horned beast;
he alone rules as king over the peoples, encompassing them all as the felly surrounds the spokes.
Come hither, O seekers of cattle; may Indra increase our excellent providence.
Will he not, being free from debt, surely bring us the highest desire for this wealth of cattle? I fly toward him, the giver of wealth, the unassailable one, like a falcon toward its beloved nest.

Worshiping Indra with the highest hymns—he who is to be invoked by the praisers on his journey— He has fastened on his quivers with all his host; he drives away the cattle in battle, whomever he desires.
O Indra, bestowing abundant wealth, do not become a miser toward us, O you who have grown great!
For you have slain the wealthy Dasyu with your weapon, O Indra, moving alone yet accompanied by your powers.
From the wealth of the non-sacrificers they scattered in all directions; the Sanakas went unto their destruction.
Even their heads were cast down, O Indra, as they, not sacrificing, contended with those who offered sacrifice.
When you, O fierce Lord of the Bay Steeds, driver from heaven, blew away the lawless ones from both worlds;
then the blameless one’s armies sought to fight, and the Navagvas, the peoples, exerted themselves.
Like castrated bulls with virile weapons, they were cast out; through their proclamations, they turned toward Indra for guidance.
O Indra, you fought these weeping and laughing ones on the far side of the mid-air;
you burned the Dasyu down from the heights of heaven and protected the prayer of those who press the juice and offer praise.
Making a covering for the earth, they adorned themselves with gold and jewels.
Though urged on, they did not overcome Indra; he surrounded his spies with the sun.

When, O Indra, you by your greatness encompassed both heaven and earth on every side, then, O Indra, with those who possess sacred prayer (*brahman*), you blew away the Dasyu against those who did not think of him.

They who did not reach the limit of heaven or earth, nor overcame the Giver of Wealth with their magic powers—Indra, the bull, made the thunderbolt his ally; by means of light, he milked the cows out from the darkness.
Following his own nature, the waters flowed; he grew great in the midst of the navigable rivers.
With a concentrated mind and with his most powerful blow, Indra struck him down toward the heavens. Indra pierced the strongholds of Ilībiśa; he split apart Śuṣṇa, the horned one.
O Maghavan, according to your speed and according to your might, you slew the attacking enemy with your thunderbolt.
Successful, he has overcome his enemies; with his sharp bull, he shattered the fortresses. Indra struck Vṛtra with his thunderbolt, and being triumphant, he furthered his own purposeful thought.
O Indra, you protected Kutsa in whom you took delight; you aided the fighting bull Daśadyu.
The dust raised by his hooves reached the sky; Śvaitreya stood forth for the conquest of men.

O Maghavan, you protected the bull Śambara among the Tugryas; in the contest for the land, you won the white cow. Having stayed there for a long time, they made their wealth subject to those who act as enemies; you brought down their possessions.
O Aśvins, be mindful of us today; far-reaching indeed is your journey and your bounty.
For your bond is like a garment in winter; you are to be approached with reverence by the wise.
The three fellies on the honey-bearing chariot—all indeed know the longing for Soma. There are three supports fixed for grasping; thrice by night you travel, O Aśvins, and thrice by day.
On the same day, O you who conceal what is blameworthy, sprinkle the sacrifice thrice today with honey.
O Aśvins, thrice pour forth for us food rich in vigor at evening and at dawn.
Come three times to our dwelling, three times to the people who follow your law; thrice bestow your aid upon the well-disposed man, as if at the threefold sacrifice.
O Aśvins, bring us joy thrice; thrice pour out nourishments for us like inexhaustible streams.
O Aśvins, bring us wealth thrice; thrice in the assembly of the gods and thrice protect our prayers.
Thrice grant us prosperity and thrice grant us renown; thrice has the Daughter of the Sun mounted your three-seated chariot.
O Aśvins, bestow upon us thrice the celestial medicines, thrice the earthly, and thrice those from the waters.
O Lords of Splendor, bring threefold protection and well-being for my son, and grant him shelter.
O Aśvins, worthy of sacrifice, thrice every day you have traveled around the threefold earth for us.
O Nāsatyas, chariot-borne ones, from the far distance, come to our dwellings like the wind reaching its own resting places.
O Aśvins, thrice with the seven mother-rivers, three are the mixing-vessels; the oblation is prepared in three ways.
You guard the three earths above and the vault of heaven established by days and nights.

Where are the three wheels of your threefold chariot? Where are the three seats that share a common foundation? When is the harnessing of your vigorous donkey, by which you, O Nāsatyas, come to our sacrifice?
O Nāsatyas, come hither; the oblation is being offered. Drink the honeyed draught with your honey-drinking mouths.
For Savitṛ sends forth for you two, at the first flush of dawn, his wondrous, butter-rich chariot for the sake of Truth.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come here with the thirty-three gods to the drinking of the honeyed mead.
Prolong our lives; wipe away our sins; drive off our enemies; be our companions.
O Aśvins, on your three-wheeled chariot, bring hither to us wealth consisting of heroic sons. Hearing me, I call upon you for protection; be present for our increase in the winning of the prize.
I invoke Agni first for well-being; I invoke Mitra and Varuṇa here for protection.
I invoke Night, who brings rest to all that moves; I invoke the god Savitṛ for aid.
Moving through the dark expanse, establishing both the immortal and the mortal,
the god Savitṛ comes on his golden chariot, beholding all beings.
The god goes by the downward path, he goes by the upward path; the worshipful one goes with his two bright bay horses.
The god Savitar comes from afar, driving away all difficulties.
Enveloped in pearls, multiform, with golden pins, the worshipful and great chariot— Savitar, of wondrous luster, has mounted it, bestowing his power upon the dark regions.
The dark-hued, white-footed steeds have looked upon the people, drawing the chariot with its golden pole.
All the clans and all beings abide perpetually within the lap of the divine Savitṛ.
Three are the heavens of Savitṛ; two are his laps, and one is in the realm of Yama, where he dwells among the heroes.
They stand upon the immortal as upon the linchpin of a chariot. Let him who understands this declare it here.
The well-winged one has surveyed the mid-air; the Asura of deep vibration is a good leader.
Where now is the Sun? Who has perceived it? To which heaven has his ray extended?
He has illuminated the eight quarters of the earth, the three desert regions, and the seven rivers.
The golden-eyed god Savitar has arrived, bestowing desirable treasures upon the donor.
Savitar, the golden-handed, the all-beholding, moves between both heaven and earth.
He drives away disease, he impels the sun, and with his dark radiance he reaches unto the sky.
May the golden-handed Asura, the good leader, the very gracious and self-strong one, come hither;
driving away the *rakṣases* and the sorcerers, the god has stood firm, being praised at every twilight.
O Savitṛ, those paths of yours which are ancient, dustless, well-made, and in the mid-air—
By those easy paths, protect us today and speak for us, O God.
We entreat with well-spoken words Agni, the mighty one of many people, of the tribes that seek the gods— him whom others indeed also invoke.
Men have established Agni as the increaser of strength; bearing oblations, we shall worship you.
As such, be well-disposed toward us today, our protector here in battles, O worthy one.
We choose you as our messenger, the all-knowing invoker.

The flames of you, who are great, spread abroad; your rays touch the sky. O Agni, the gods—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—kindle you, the ancient messenger. That mortal who offers oblations to you, O Agni, wins all wealth through you.
You, O Agni, are the delightful Hotṛ, the lord of the household, and the messenger of the people.
In you are gathered all the firm laws which the gods have established.
In you alone, O auspicious and most youthful Agni, is every oblation offered.
Be well-disposed toward us today and in the future; sacrifice to the gods so that we may possess heroic strength.
Truly, those who offer homage sit near him, the self-ruling lord.
With oblations, men kindle Agni, having overcome all failures.
Slaying Vṛtra, they crossed over heaven and earth and the waters; they have made wide room for their dwelling.
May the Bull, invoked with oblations, become manifest in glory to Kaṇva; may the Steed neigh in the raids for cattle. Sit down together, for you are great; shine forth, O best invoker of the gods!
O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, O praised one, emit your ruddy, beautiful smoke.
You whom the gods established here for Manu as the best of sacrificers, O bearer of oblations;
you whom Kaṇva Medhyātithi [invoked], you whom Vṛṣan and Upastuta [invoked] as the winner of wealth.
The Agni whom Medhyātithi Kaṇva kindled from the Eternal Order (ṛta)—his flames have shone forth; we magnify that very Agni with these hymns.
O self-dependent one, fill us with wealth, for you, O Agni, possess kinship among the gods.
You rule over the glorious prize; have mercy on us, for you are great. Stand up erect for our protection, like the god Savitṛ.
Stand erect as the winner of the prize when we, with ointments and singers, call upon you.
Standing upright, protect us from distress with your banner; burn up every devouring fiend.
Raise us up so that we may move and live; find for us favor among the gods.
Protect us, O Agni, from the demon; protect us from the malice of the stingy enemy.
Protect us from the one who seeks to harm us, or from the one who wishes to slay us, O youngest god of great luster!
Like a club, strike down on all sides those who offer no oblations, O you with the flame-jaws, whoever would deceive us.
Let not that mortal who sharpens his weapons against us through the nights become our enemy and prevail over us.
Agni has won great heroic might; Agni has won prosperity for Kaṇva.
Agni protected Mitra and Medhyātithi; Agni protected Upastuta in the winning of booty.
Through Agni we call Turvaśa and Yadu from afar, even as we call upon Ugradeva.
Agni led Navavāstva, Bṛhadratha, and Turvīti as a force against the Dasyu.
Manu established you, O Agni, as a light for all people forever.
You shone forth, O Kaṇva, born of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*), strengthened by the people whom the tribes revere.
The brilliant, impetuous flames of Agni are terrible; they are not to be withstood.
Burn up the demon-possessing sorcerers at once, and every devouring fiend!
Your sporting host, the Maruts—unassailable and radiant upon their chariots—[is celebrated].
O Kaṇvas,
sing forth to him who was born with self-effulgence, together with spotted deer, spears, axes, and glittering ornaments.
As if right here one hears the cracking of the whips in their hands as they speak; on their journey, they display their wondrous power.
For your impetuous host, of brilliant splendor and mighty strength—
Sing forth the prayer bestowed by the gods;
praise the bull among the cows, the sporting host of Maruts,
who has grown strong upon the juice for the sake of its consumption.
Who among you, O heroes, shakers of heaven and earth, is the most exalted,
when you shake them like the hem of a garment?
At your approach, no mortal can withstand your fierce wrath;
even the mountain, the rocky peak, yields.
At whose marches the earth trembles with fear during their journeys, like an aged lord of the people.
For firm indeed is their birth, their vigor to emerge from the mother, since their strength is doubled accordingly.
These sons have raised their voices; they have extended the race-courses in their strides, lowing as they go knee-deep in the waters.
Even him, the long and broad offspring of the mist, the one who does not fail—
him they cause to move forth on their journeys.
O Maruts, whatever strength you possess, with it you have caused the people to tremble; you have caused the mountains to tremble.
When the Maruts go along, they speak together on the way;
does anyone hear them?
Come forth quickly with your swift steeds; there are offerings for you among the Kaṇvas.
Rejoice there indeed!
For there is indeed enough for your exhilaration; we truly belong to them, that we may live out the full span of life.
When indeed, O you for whom the sacred grass is trimmed, will you now take us up in your hands like a father who loves his son?
Where now, O you whose purpose is great, do you go, as if from heaven to earth? Where do your cows delight, as if in a pen?
Where, O Maruts, are your newest favors? Where are your blessings? And where are all your auspicious gifts?
O you whose mother is Pṛśni, if you were mortals,
your worshiper would be immortal.
Let not your singer be like a wild beast in a pasture that is unloved;
let him not go upon the path of Yama.
Let not Destruction, with her evil intent, strike us down further and further;
let her perish together with Thirst.
Truly, these fierce and impetuous sons of Rudra bring mist even across the desert, though there be no wind.
Like a lowing cow, the lightning bellows; like a mother following her calf, she follows when their rain has been released.
Even by day they create darkness with Parjanya, the bringer of water,
when they drench the earth.
Then, at the roar of the Maruts, every earthly dwelling shook;
all human beings trembled.
O Maruts, with your firm-hoofed steeds, travel along the bright,
river-banked paths with unwearied courses.
May your fellies be firm, may your chariots and horses be so; may your reins be well-fashioned.
Speak forth with a continuous song to praise Brahmaṇaspati;
[praise] Agni, who is beautiful to behold like Mitra.
Measure out the hymn; let it spread from your mouth like Parjanya;
sing the song worthy of praise.
Worship the host of Maruts— the brilliant, praiseworthy, and hymn-singing one—
so that they may be increased for us here.
When you thus cast forth your measure like a flame from afar—
by whose wisdom, O Maruts, by whose form, to whom do you go, and whom, O shakers?
May your weapons be firm for driving away the foe, and strong for resisting the attack.
May your power be most praiseworthy; let it not belong to the wily mortal.
When you strike down what is firm, O heroes, and whirl about what is heavy,
you pass through the trees of the earth and through the regions of the mountains.
For no enemy of yours has been found in heaven, nor upon the earth, O destroyers of foes. O Rudras, may your power remain with your offspring; it is not to be assailed even now.
They cause the mountains to tremble; they rend asunder the lords of the forest.
O Maruts, you have come forth like those intoxicated with wine—O gods, together with your entire host.
You have harnessed the spotted deer to your chariots; the ruddy steed draws as a leader.
Even the earth has listened to your coming, and mortal men were struck with fear.
O Rudras, we quickly choose your protection for the sake of our offspring;
come now to us with your aid as in the past, even for the trembling Kaṇva.
O Maruts, whatever terrifying thing sent by you or sent by mortals assails us,
drive it away with your might, drive it away with your strength, and drive it away with your protections.
For you, O wise ones who are worthy of sacrifice, have bestowed the Kaṇva in its entirety.
O Maruts, come to us with your aids that are not incomplete, like lightning bringing rain.
O bounteous givers, you sustain power that is never-failing; O shakers, your strength is never-deficient.
O Maruts, full of wrath against the hater of the seer, hurl your hatred like an arrow!
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati; seeking the gods, we entreat you.
May the bounteous Maruts come forward; O Indra, be swift with us.
For indeed, O Son of Strength, the mortal calls upon you when the prize is set.
O Maruts, may he who longs for you obtain great heroic power and noble horses.
Let Brahmaṇaspati go forth; let the goddess Sūnṛtā go forth.
May the gods lead our sacrifice toward the hero, the manly one who bestows fivefold wealth.
He who gives excellent riches to the singer gains imperishable fame.
For him we offer the *iḷā*—rich in heroes, victorious, and free from blemish.
Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati utters the hymn worthy of praise,
in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman— the gods— have made their dwelling. Let us recite that very hymn, O gods, which brings well-being and is free from blemish, in our assemblies.
And if you, O heroes, welcome this speech, may it obtain all desirable things from you.
Who has reached the person seeking the gods? Who has reached the one for whom the sacrificial grass is spread? The donor has stepped forth with his dwellings; he has established a secure home within.

He bestows abundance upon his domain; with kings he slays [the foe] and establishes a secure dwelling even in the midst of fear. There is no one to obstruct or overcome the wielder of the thunderbolt, whether in a great battle or a small one. He whom the wise Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman protect—
Never indeed is that person harmed, whom they carry across as if with their arms; who protect the mortal from injury,
he thrives entirely unharmed.
The kings of these [Maruts] strike down the difficult passes, the enemies, and the fortresses; they lead them across all misfortunes.
O Ādityas, the path is easy to traverse and free from thorns for him who walks according to the *ṛta*.
There is no devouring here for you;
O heroes, O Ādityas, whatever sacrifice you lead by the straight path,
may that reach you for your favor.
That mortal, possessing jewels and all wealth, and his offspring himself,
goes unassailed toward [his goal].
O friends, how may we accomplish the hymn of praise for Mitra and Aryaman?
Great is the power of Varuṇa.
I do not speak back to you who strike nor to him who curses, if he seeks the gods; with hymns of praise alone I strive to win your favor.
One should fear even one who bestows fourfold wealth, until he has laid it down;
one should not long for ill-spoken words.
O Pūṣan, son of liberation, traverse the paths and the distress.
Go forth, O God, and lead us forward. O Pūṣan, whatever wicked wolf, ill-disposed toward us, lies in wait,
strike him away from our path.
Drive far away from the path that robber who lies in wait, the thief who plots with deceit.
You [drive him] far from the track of the one who harms, that double-dealing evildoer, whoever he may be.
Tread down with your foot the burning one.
O wondrous Pūṣan, rich in wisdom, we choose that aid of yours by which you urged on our ancestors.
Then, O possessor of all prosperity, you who are most richly endowed with golden axes, make our riches easy to win.
Lead us beyond those who attack us; make our paths fair and easy to travel.
O Pūṣan, find the will for us here;
lead us toward good pasture, not toward a new affliction on the path.
O Pūṣan...
Be able; fill us full; bestow gifts; sharpen our wits; open wide your belly.
O Pūṣan, we do not revile you; we celebrate you with hymns of praise.
We pray for treasures from you, the wondrous one. What [words] may we speak to Rudra, the wise, the most bountiful, the most powerful,
that are most pleasing to his heart?
So that Aditi may grant us Rudra’s favor for our cattle, for our men, and for our kine; so that it may be granted for our offspring;
and so that Mitra, Varuṇa, and Rudra may take heed of us.

So that all [the gods], being of one accord, [may favor us]— we pray for that auspicious favor and well-being from Rudra, the lord of songs, the lord of the sacrifice, whose healing medicine is refreshing.
He who shines like the bright sun, who glows like gold,
the most excellent Vasu among the gods—
may he grant well-being to our horse, and a good path for our ram and ewe.
For men, for women, and for cattle—
O Soma, bestow upon us the glory of a hundred heroes, great renown, and abundant manly strength.
May those who obstruct our Soma, may the enemies, not deceive us. O Indu, grant us a share in the prize.
Those offspring of yours, of the immortal, in the highest abode of Truth—

O Soma, you are the head; O Soma, you know the treasures that adorn the navel. O immortal Agni, bring hither the wonderful wealth of the dawning dawn for the donor today, O Jātavedas, bringing the gods who awaken at daybreak.
For you are the beloved messenger, the bearer of oblations, O Agni, the charioteer of the sacrifices.
In union with the Aśvins and the Dawn, bestow upon us great heroic power and high renown.
Today we choose as our messenger the Vasu Agni, who is dearly beloved by many.
At the break of dawn, I praise Agni Jātavedas, whose banner is smoke, who is radiant with light, the glory of the sacrifice among rites,
the most excellent and youngest guest, well-invoked and beloved by the person who offers oblations,
so that he may go toward the gods. At the break of dawn, I praise him.

I shall praise you, O immortal sustainer of the universe, Agni, the immortal protector, worthy of the sacrificial feast, the most excellent sacrificer, and the bearer of oblations. O youngest one, be a source of good renown for the singer; you whose tongue is honeyed, you who are well-invoked with *svāhā*.
Prolonging the life of Praskaṇva so that he may live, pay homage to the divine host.
For you, the all-knowing Hotṛ, the people kindle together;
therefore, O Agni, much-invoked and wise one, bring the gods here swiftly.
Savitṛ, Uṣas, the two Aśvins, Bhaga, and Agni at the dawning of the nights—
the Kaṇvas, having pressed the Soma, kindle thee, the bearer of oblations,
O performer of the fair sacrifice; for thou, O Agni, art the lord of sacrifices and the messenger of the people.
O Agni, awakened at dawn, bring hither today the gods who behold the light of heaven, so that they may drink the Soma.
O Agni, rich in luster, you have shone throughout the former dawns, visible to all. You are the protector within the settlements; as a man, you are the domestic priest at the sacrifices.

O Agni, we establish you as the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ priest, the officiating ṛtvij— like Manu, O God, the wise, the swift, the immortal messenger. When, O you of Mitra-like splendor, acting as the domestic priest of the gods, you go on your mission as their intimate envoy.
Like the roaring waves of the ocean, the flames of Agni flash forth.

Hear us, O Agni, you whose ear is quick to listen, together with the gods who are your fellow-travelers and bearers of the sacrifice. Let Mitra and Aryaman, who go forth at dawn, sit upon the sacred grass (*barhis*) for the rite.
May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, whose tongue is Agni and who increase the Truth, hear our hymn of praise.
May Varuṇa, the upholder of the sacred law, drink the Soma together with the Aśvins and Uṣas.
O Agni, bring hither the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas.
Sacrifice to the people of well-performed rites, born of Manu, who sprinkle the clarified butter;
for the wise gods, O Agni, are quick to listen to the donor.
O lover of songs, bring here those thirty-three deities whose horses are ruddy.
O Jātavedas, like Priyamedha, Atri, Virūpa, and Aṅgiras, O you of great vows, hear the call of Praskaṇva.
The Mahikerus and the Priyamedhas have invoked you for protection.
Agni, who reigns over the sacrifices with his bright flame—
O you who are invoked with clarified butter, O Holy One, truly hear these songs by which the sons of Kaṇva call upon you for protection.
The people among the tribes invoke you, O Agni, most rich in glorious fame,
the flame-haired one, much beloved, to carry their oblations. They have established you as the Hotṛ priest, the officiant, the best finder of wealth.

O Agni, the inspired poets call upon you at the sacrifices of the gods—you who have ears that hear, who are most far-reaching. The inspired ones, having pressed the soma, have drawn you toward the offerings.
Bearing great light as an oblation for the mortal who gives, O Agni.

O Bounteous One, O Son of Strength, worthy of trust, seat here today upon the sacred grass the divine host who come at dawn to drink the Soma. O Agni, with our joint invocations, worship the divine host so that they turn hitherward.
RV 1.45.10: O you of liberal gifts, here is the Soma; drink it, for it has been pressed on the previous day.
RV 1.46.1: This unprecedented Dawn, the beloved of heaven, shines forth.
I praise you both, O Aśvins, with a lofty hymn.
O wonder-workers, sons of Sindhu, discoverers of riches,
O gods who find wealth through inspired thought;
your lofty steeds are urged forward upon the ancient summit.
When your chariot flies with its winged steeds,
the lover of the waters fills [the vessels] with the oblation, O heroes; he is the filler, the father of the cloud, the one who observes all people.
O Nāsatyas, you who are praised in song, you are the upholders of our prayers;
through your inspired words, drink boldly of the Soma.
O Aśvins, may that luminous power carry us across the darkness.
Bestow upon us that nourishment. Come to us in the ship of our prayers so that we may reach the further shore; O Aśvins, harness your chariot.
Your oar is broad as heaven; your chariot is at the ford of the rivers. With prayer the drops have been yoked.
O Kaṇvas, the drops are at the place of heaven, the wealth at the station of the rivers.
Where will you two place your own covering?
Light has indeed come for the sake of the ray; the sun shines forth like gold, and with his dark tongue he has looked abroad.
A path has come into being for crossing to the further shore, leading straight by the way of Truth; the track from heaven has been made visible.
The singer honors each and every one of those aids of the Aśvins.
RV_01.046.12.2: O you two who have drunk of the Soma and are exhilarated;
RV_01.046.13.1: Dwelling with Vivasvat through the drinking of Soma and by means of our song; RV_01.046.13.2: O you two who bring welfare, come hither as you did for Manu.
Uṣas has approached according to the splendor of you two who move all around;
you win the cosmic order through the nights.
O both Aśvins, drink [the soma] and grant us protection.
With your unimpaired aids, [O Aśvins]—this most honey-sweet Soma has been pressed for you, O increasers of *ṛta*.
Drink it, O Aśvins, which has stood overnight; bestow treasures upon the donor.
Come hither, O Aśvins, on your chariot with its triple seat, threefold and well-adorned.
The Kaṇvas offer prayers for you at the sacrifice; hear their invocation well.
O Aśvins, increaseers of Truth, drink the most honey-sweet Soma.
Now today, O wonder-workers (*dasrā*), bearing wealth upon your chariot, come to the donor.
O possessors of all knowledge (*viśvavedasā*), sprinkle the sacrifice with honey upon the three-seated sacred grass (*barhis*).
The Kaṇvas, having pressed the Soma and looking toward heaven, call upon you both, O Aśvins.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, with those aids wherewith you protected Kaṇva, protect us as well; drink the Soma, O you who increase the Truth!
O wonder-workers, bearing wealth on your chariot for Sudās, bring us nourishment, O Aśvins.
Bestow upon us wealth, much-desired, from the ocean or from heaven.
Whether you two Nāsatyas are in the distance or whether you abide among the Turvaśas,
come hither on your well-rolling chariot together with the rays of the sun.
May your coursers, who grace the sacrifice, bring you both hitherward to the libations.
Bestowing nourishment upon the well-doer, O bounteous ones, sit upon the sacred grass, O heroes! With that chariot of sun-bright hide, O Nāsatyas, come hither.
With that [chariot] by which you have constantly brought wealth to the donor for the drinking of the sweet Soma;
with hymns and songs of praise we call you hither for protection, O lords of many riches, for you,
O Aśvins, have drunk the Soma in the beloved dwelling-place of the Kaṇvas.
O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, dawn upon us with the left [hand] (the gift).
O radiant goddess, shine forth with great splendor, bestowing wealth upon us as a liberal giver.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, and finding all things, they move in great numbers to shine forth.

O Dawn, raise up for me the truthful words; impel the bounty of the generous patrons. The goddess Dawn has shone forth and shall shine again, she who sets the chariots in motion. Those who have placed themselves within her arrivals are like those seeking glory upon the ocean.
O Dawn, those wise patrons who yoke their minds for the sake of giving during your arrivals—
here indeed Kaṇva, the best of the Kaṇvas, sings the name of these heroes. Like a noble maiden, the Dawn comes forth, bestowing her gifts.
Wearing away the strength of all that has feet, she bestows it; she causes the birds to fly up.
She who scatters the assembly and the seekers of gain, rising up, knows not their tracks.
No living being, O lady rich in booty, remains still when you have risen in your flight.
She has yoked [her chariot] from afar, from the very rising of the sun. With a hundred chariots, this fortunate Dawn approaches the human races.
The whole world bows down before her gaze; she, the noble one, creates light.
May the wealthy Dawn, daughter of heaven, shine away our hatred and drive away our enemies.
O Dawn, daughter of heaven, shine upon us with thy radiant light,
bringing us manifold prosperity as thou dawnest at our sacrifices.
For you are the breath and the life of all, O noble lady, when you shine forth.
As such, O radiant one, with your lofty chariot, hear our call, O giver of wondrous wealth.
O Uṣas, win for us booty that is brilliant among the human race.
With him, bring the well-performed sacrifices to us—the priests who praise you.
Bring all the gods from the mid-air for the drinking of Soma, O Dawn!
Bestow upon us wealth in cattle, wealth in horses, praiseworthy strength, and heroic vigor, O Dawn!
She whose radiant, auspicious beams have appeared—
may that Uṣas grant us wealth, possessing all desirable things, well-fashioned, and easy to attain.
For even the seers of old invoked you, O Great One, for protection and for aid.
O Dawn, accept our hymns with your bounty and your bright radiance!
O Dawn, as you today open wide the two doors of heaven with your light,
grant us a broad, secure shelter, and, O Goddess, bestow upon us food rich in cattle.

Sprinkle us with great wealth, adorned with all forms, and with refreshing draughts; O Uṣas, mighty one, victorious over all, sprinkle us with splendor and with strengths, O thou rich in booty! O Uṣas, come hither with auspicious things from the very light of heaven.
Let those whose appearance is ruddy bear you toward the house of the Soma-presser—
that well-adorned, easy-moving chariot which you, O Uṣas, have mounted. With that, O Daughter of Heaven, protect the people of noble fame this day.
Even the winged birds, the bipeds and quadrupeds, O bright one, have awakened at your coming,
O Uṣas, according to the seasons, from the very ends of heaven.
