For as you shine forth with your rays, you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
The Kaṇvas, desiring wealth, have invoked you, O Dawn, with their songs.
His rays bear aloft that god Jātavedas,
the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.
Those stars depart with the nights like thieves,
for the Sun who beholds all.
His banners, his rays, have become visible among the people.
Shining like fires,
O Sūrya, you are the one who crosses over, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
Facing the clans of the gods, facing men, you rise up;
facing all, so that we may behold the light of heaven. O Purifier, with that eye wherewith you look upon the active folk.
O Varuṇa, you behold;
O Sūrya, you traverse the sky and the broad mid-region, measuring out the days with your rays as you survey all living beings.
O divine Sūrya, seven bay horses carry you in your chariot,
O far-seeing one with flaming hair. The Sun has yoked the seven bright mares, the daughters of his chariot.
With those [mares] yoked by himself, he goes.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness,
we have gone up to Sūrya, the god among gods, the highest light.
Rising today, O Sūrya, you who possess the luster of Mitra, ascending to the highest heaven, destroy my heart-disease and my jaundice. We transfer my jaundice onto the parrots and the thrushes.
And so, we deposit my yellowness upon the *hāridrava* birds. This Āditya has risen with all his power;
subjecting to me whoever hates me, may I not be subject to him who hates me.
Exhilarate with songs that ram, Indra, who is invoked by many, worthy of praise, and a surging ocean of wealth;

him whose [powers] spread abroad like the heavens among men, the most generous, you—sing to that inspired sage. The aids, seeking him who is most effective in assistance, have reached him who fills the mid-air and is encompassed by his own powers.
The skillful *Ṛbhus* mounted Indra, the one who stirs with joy, the lord of a hundred powers; swift and true speech has ascended him.
You opened up the cow-stall for the *Aṅgirases*; you were the deliverer for Atri among the hundred-doored [fortress], finding the way.
Even with his army, you brought wealth to Vimada; in the contest for the prize, you made the mountain dance for the one who clothes himself in light.
You threw open the lid of the waters; you held the moisture-bearing wealth within the mountain.

When you, O Indra, by your might slew Vṛtra the dragon, you caused the sun to ascend to heaven so that it might be seen. By your wondrous powers, you blew away the sorcerers who, following their own ways, offered oblations upon the sleeping ground.
O you whose mind is set on manly deeds, you shattered the fortresses of Pipru; you protected R̥jiśvan in the slayings of the Dasyus.
You protected Kutsa in the slayings of Śuṣṇa; you delivered Śambara over to Atithigva. Even the great Arbuda you trampled underfoot; from of old you were born for the slaying of the Dasyus.
In you all powers are gathered together; your bounty rejoices for the drinking of Soma.
Your thunderbolt, placed within your arms, is renowned; shatter all the manly strengths of the enemy.
Distinguish between the Aryas and those who are Dasyus; subjecting the lawless ones, bring them under the control of the one who has spread the sacrificial grass.
Be a helper and an instigator for the sacrificer; I delight in all those deeds of yours during our joint revelries.
Subduing the lawless for the one who follows the Law, Indra with his powers has struck down the powerless.
Though he was already grown, he reached even higher as he increased; being praised, Vamra shattered the obstructing barriers.
When Uśanas fashioned for you power with forceful might, your strength pressed apart heaven and earth with its greatness.
O hero-minded one, the horses of the wind, yoked by thought, bore you toward glory as you were being filled.
When Indra was exhilarated in the company of Uśanas Kāvya, he mounted his two swift, most swiftest steeds.
The fierce one sent forth the waters with their current; he shattered the strongholds of Śuṣṇa and cast down his fortresses.
O you who hold the rain-giving thunderbolt in your hand, you mount your chariot among the offerings of Śāryāta; you take delight in these presented gifts.
O Indra, just as you have always found pleasure in those who press the Soma, may you ascend to unassailable glory in heaven.
O Indra, you gave Vṛcayā to the great and eloquent Kakṣīvat, who was pressing the soma for you.
O wise one, you became the consort of Vṛṣaṇaśva; all these deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the libations.
Indra has been established in the presence of the pious, like a sacrificial post among the Pajras, while the hymn of praise is fixed as if in a dwelling.
Seeking horses, seeking cattle, seeking chariots, and seeking wealth—Indra alone is the lord of riches, the bestower of them.
This homage has been spoken for the bull, the self-ruling one, whose strength is true and who is powerful.
O Indra, in this assembly, may we, with all our heroes and together with the patrons, abide under your protection.

That ram, the finder of light, whom a hundred well-formed ones accompany together—him I would turn hither for aid with my hymns of praise, like a prize-winning steed, like a chariot that hastens to the call, even Indra.
He is immovable like a mountain upon its foundations; he whose aids are a thousandfold has grown mighty in his powers.
When Indra, exulting in the soma-juice, slew Vṛtra who encompassed the rivers, he cast down the floods.
For he is the opener among openers, the one who has burst the udder; he whose foundation is radiant is strengthened by exhilaration through the prayers of the wise.
I invoke that Indra with a prayer of skillful action, for he is the most liberal giver; indeed, he is the fulfiller of the soma-juice.
Him whom those seated on the sacred grass in heaven fill full—like the ocean with their own well-being, so do his own aids flow toward him.

His protections stood by him in the slaying of Vṛtra; his powers, unassailable and of undeviating form, accompanied Indra. Toward his own rain-streams as he fights in the exhilaration of this [Soma], his protections have sped forth like swift waters down a slope.
When Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, boldly drinking the soma-juice, split the enclosures of Vala as Trita did;
he moves about with fervor, his power blazes forth, and having encompassed the waters, he has laid down his foundation at the bottom of the mid-air.
When, O Indra, you struck the thunderbolt between the jaws of Vṛtra, whose arms were difficult to seize, on the slope of the mountain.
For the waves do not overwhelm you, O Indra, like those entering a lake—those prayers of yours which are your means of strengthening.
Even Tvaṣṭṛ increased your fitting power; he fashioned the thunderbolt of overwhelming force.
Having slain Vṛtra with your bay steeds, O Indra of gathered wisdom, you opened a path for the waters for the sake of man.
You two took up the iron thunderbolt in your arms; you established the divine sun so that it might be seen.

When they performed the great, self-luminous, and praiseworthy deed, they caused the ascent to heaven out of fear. When the Maruts, the helpers of Indra who seek men in the battle for light, rejoiced after winning the sun.
Even the heaven itself, O Indra, trembled in fear at the roar of this impetuous serpent when your thunderbolt struck.
When you, in the exhilaration of the pressed soma, shattered with your might the head of Vṛtra as he hemmed in the two worlds,
O Indra— if indeed the earth were tenfold and all the peoples were to spread out for all days...
Here, O Maghavan, your renowned power has come forth; by your might and your greatness, it has reached even unto heaven.
On the far shore of this mid-air and sky, you of self-born strength, bold in spirit, have made yourself ready for our aid.
You have made the earth the measure of your power; encompassing the waters, the sun, and the heavens, you move beyond the sky.
You have become the counterpart of the earth; you have become the lord of the lofty, great hero.
You have filled the entire mid-air with your greatness. Truly, indeed, there is none other like you.
Neither heaven and earth nor the rivers have reached the limit of his expanse within the realm of space.
Do not withhold your own rain during his exhilaration; while he fights, you alone have performed all other deeds for the sake of humanity.
Here the Maruts sang their praise in that battle; all the gods rejoiced after you, O Indra, when with your sharp-edged weapon you struck down Vṛtra’s army.
We bring forth this speech as an offering to the Great One; we offer songs to Indra at the dwelling-place of Vivasvat.
For never indeed has one found wealth among those who sleep like the ill-praised man; a poor hymn of praise is not valued among the givers of riches.
Thou art the master of the stall of horses, O Indra, the master of the stall of cattle, the master of the stall of barley, the powerful lord of wealth.
The one who aids men from of old, who does not weary those who desire him, the friend of friends—to him we sing this song.
O Indra, powerful one, doer of many deeds, most resplendent, all this wealth around us is known to be yours alone.
Therefore, as a conqueror, gather it from there and bring it to us; do not frustrate the desire of the singer who seeks you.
With these days, with these drops, being well-disposed and warding off want with cattle, O Aśvins;
with Indra, shattering the Dasyu through the drops, may we, freed from hatred, seize abundance with food.
O Indra, may we seize wealth, may we seize food, and may we seize spoils that are many-glittering and resplendent.
May we obtain the divine *pramati* (insight), which is full of heroic vigor, preceded by cattle, and accompanied by horses.
Those exhilarations intoxicated you, those manly powers, O Lord of Beings, when the Soma juices were pressed in the slayings of Vṛtra.
When, for the singer who spread the sacrificial grass, you irresistibly struck down ten thousand Vṛtras.

With boldness you go forth from battle to battle; with your might, you shall utterly destroy fortress after fortress. When, O Indra, through your friendship, you struck down the guileful one named Namuci in the distance with your bow.
You slew Karañja and Parṇaya with the most piercing path of Atithigva.

You shattered the hundred forts of Vaṅgr̥da, who offered no resistance, when he was hemmed in by R̥jiśvan. You, O famous one, with your chariot wheel, crushed those sixty thousand and ninety-nine [men] of Janarāja, who had come against you unaccompanied by kinsmen.
You protected Suśravas with your aids, and with your protections, O Indra, you helped Tūrvayāṇ.
You made Kutsa, Atithigva, and Āyu subject to this great, youthful king.
May we, O Indra, be your most auspicious friends, guarded by the gods at the height of our prosperity.
We shall praise you, through you possessing excellent heroes, prolonging our life for a longer duration.
O Maghavan, do not abandon us in this distress amidst the battles; for the limit of your power cannot be encompassed.
You made the rivers roar and the forests resound; how did the earth not collapse with fear?
Sing praise to Śakra, the powerful and lord of might; magnifying Indra, who hears us, celebrate him.
He who, as a bull through his virile power, subdues both heaven and earth with his bold strength. Sing forth a strengthening word to the lofty sky, for he whose mind is bold possesses bold dominion.
The Asura of great renown was made mighty by his own power; for he is a bull, a chariot drawn by two bay steeds.
You stirred the ridge of the vast heaven; with your own bold self, you shattered Śambara.
When, O bold one, you assailed the magic-working, treacherous foe with your exhilarating, sharp-edged bolt from your outstretched hand.

When you strike down upon the head of the snorting [demon], even as you shatter the woods of the groaning Śuṣṇa with your forward-striving and mighty mind—even if you do this today—who can restrain you? O Lord of a hundred powers, you have protected Narya, Turvaśa, and Yadu; you have protected Turvīti and Vayya.

You made Etaśa a chariot for the decisive prize; you destroyed the ninety-nine fortresses. He indeed, the king, the lord of the virtuous, has become preeminent among men—he who, having been offered oblations, carries out the command.
Or he who welcomes the hymns with bounty—Dānu, for him, makes the lower regions of heaven overflow.
Unequaled is their dominion, unequaled their wisdom; let these Soma-drinkers excel through their skillful work.

O Indra, those who increase your great dominion, your steadfast, and your virile power—[for them] these abundant juices, milked by the stones, resting in the vessels, are for you, O Indra, to drink from the chalices.
Pervade them; satisfy their desire, and then direct their minds toward the giving of wealth. The obstructing darkness stood firm within the belly of Vṛtra like a mountain.
Indra struck down all the rivers held back by the obstructor, as they rushed down the slopes.
May he bestow upon us glorious splendor that increases our welfare; O Indra, conqueror of men, grant us great and powerful dominion.
Protect our patrons and guard our wise leaders; establish us in wealth, in noble offspring, and in nourishment.
Even the vastness of heaven has spread itself wide, yet neither heaven nor earth can equal Indra in greatness.
Terrible and most mighty, a burner for the sake of the people, he whets his thunderbolt for brilliance like a bull.

Like the ocean receiving the rivers that flow toward it, Indra receives [the offerings] spread out over the wide expanses; for the drinking of the Soma, the bull exerts himself, and from of old, as a warrior, he is praised for his power.
O Indra, you possess that mountain-like [strength] for enjoyment; by the law of great manliness, you rule as sovereign.
You are distinguished among the gods by your heroic power; as the fierce one, you are placed at the forefront for every deed.
He alone is celebrated among the people with reverent words in the forest, proclaiming his lovely Indra-power among men.
The bull becomes desirable and lovely; as the bountiful lord, he stirs the lowing cows with security. He, the warrior, by his might and power, brings about great battles for the sake of men.
And even then, they have no faith in the radiant Indra as he repeatedly hurls the thunderbolt, his weapon of slaughter.
For he, seeking glory, increasing upon the earth with his might, destroys the man-made dwellings;
creating secure lights for the sacrificer, the one of noble wisdom released the waters to flow.
O drinker of Soma, let your mind be intent on giving; make your two bay steeds turn hitherward, you who hear our praise.
Those who are the best at sacrificing and the most skillful charioteers for you, O Indra—your restless intentions do not deceive you.
You carry in your hands wealth that is never exhausted; you, the famous one, have placed invincible power within your own body.
Like wells surrounded by those who dig them, O Indra, many thoughts are centered upon your person.

He has risen up from the many ladles like a steed toward a maiden, he the active one. He causes the skillful one to drink from the golden, skillful chariot yoked with bay horses. Him the songs of praise, seeking gain, have led around—the abundant offerings—like those desiring wealth at the gathering of the ocean.

Now, like longing birds ascending a mountain with their brilliance, [we approach] the lord of the skillful assembly, the conqueror through his might. He is the victorious one, great in manly power; his strength shines with impetuous force like the peak of a mountain.
By him, in the exhilaration of the Soma, the iron-strong [Indra] cast down the guileful Śuṣṇa, binding him fast among the restless ones.
O Goddess, if thy power has increased thee, it follows Indra as the sun follows the dawn.
He who with bold strength drives away the darkness, stirs up the dust, roaring loudly as he rushes forward.
When thou didst establish the firm and unshakable expanse across the atmosphere, by thy great impetus, thou didst reach to the heights of heaven.
When in the exhilaration of the Soma, O Indra, you were gladdened by the light, you struck down Vṛtra and released the flood of waters.
By your might, O Indra, you established the support of heaven and the greatness upon the seats of earth.
In the intoxication of the pressed juice, you set the waters flowing; you shattered the flanks of Vṛtra right through his joints.
I offer a hymn to the most generous, the lofty one of vast wealth, whose strength is true and who is powerful—

the one whose irresistible bounty, like waters on a slope, is opened for all life and for power. And then, following you, all shall come for the sake of sacrifice, as the waters flow downward to the libations of the one who possesses the oblation.
When, like a mountain, the beloved vajra of Indra settled down, the golden one was ready to strike.
To this formidable one, bring [the oblation] with reverence at the sacrifice, as you would to the radiant Dawn, for he is to be approached.
His domain has been made a name for glory; his Indra-power has become light, like bay horses for the journey.
O Indra, praised by many, we here are yours—those who move about having taken hold of you, O Lord of abundant wealth.
For none other than you, O lover of songs, can sustain our hymns; as the two worlds sustain all, so do you graciously accept this our speech.
Great is your heroic power, O Indra; we belong to you. O Maghavan, fulfill the desire of this singer.
The vast heaven has yielded to your heroic power, and this earth has bowed before your might.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you shattered that great and wide mountain into pieces with your bolt;
you released the obstructed waters so they might flow, and you have truly established all conquering strength as your own alone.
Never indeed does the immortal one, born of strength, shrink away, since he has become the Hotṛ-priest and the messenger of Vivasvat.
With the most effective paths, he traverses the mid-air; at the assembly of the gods, he seeks to win them with the oblation.
Grasping his own food, the ageless one stands among the dry wood, eager to consume it.
Like a horse, his back shines with moisture; like the ridge of heaven, he has thundered and roared.
Acting together with the Rudras and Vasus, the immortal Hotṛ, seated as the one placed in front, is the winner of wealth.
Like a chariot moving swiftly among the people, the god distributes desirable treasures in succession to the living.
Impelled by the wind, he spreads through the dry brushwood; with his tongues as sickles, he roars loudly.
When you, O Agni, the bull, thirstily desire the trees, O ageless one with radiant waves, your path becomes black.
With burning jaws, driven by the wind, he rushes through the forest like a victorious bull among the herd.
Advancing with his inexhaustible splendor through the mid-air, he causes fear to the stationary, the moving, and the winged birds.
The Bhr̥gus established you among men like a lovely treasure, easy to invoke for the people—
the Hotr̥, O Agni, the excellent guest, as dear as a friend to the divine race.

The Hotṛ-priest, the most skilled in sacrifice, whom the seven sacrificial ladles and the officiating priests choose for the rites— Agni, the steward of all treasures— to him I offer oblations and seek wealth.
O Son of Strength, you who are great as Mitra, grant today to us, your praisers, a flawless protection.
O Agni, son of strength, protect the one who praises you from distress with your iron fortresses;
O radiant one, be a shelter for the singer, and be a protection, O bounteous lord, for those who offer gifts.
O Agni, protect the singer from distress; may he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
O Agni, these others are indeed thy branches; in thee all the immortals rejoice.
O Vaiśvānara, thou art the navel of the settlements; like a pillar, thou supportest the people. Agni is the head of heaven, the navel of the earth; thus he has become the messenger of both worlds.
The gods have generated you, O divine Vaiśvānara, as a light for the Āryan.
As rays are firmly fixed in the sun, so have treasures been placed within Agni Vaiśvānara.
You are the king of that which is in the mountains, in the plants, in the waters, and among men.

Like the two great worlds (*rodasī*) for their son, the human *hotṛ* priest, skillful as Manu, offers songs of praise to you— those many youthful hymns to Vaiśvānara, the most heroic one who possesses the light of heaven and true strength.
O Jātavedas Vaiśvānara, even from the vast sky your greatness has surpassed all bounds.
You are the king of the human tribes; through battle, you have created wide space for the gods.
Now I shall proclaim the greatness of the Bull, whom the Pūrus follow as the slayer of Vṛtra.
Agni Vaiśvānara, having struck down the Dasyu, shook the barriers and shattered Śambara.
Vaiśvānara, who belongs to all people by his greatness, the worshipful and radiant one among the Bharadvājas;
Agni, rich in true speech, is praised with hundreds of songs by Śātavaneya at the many festivals.
(He is) the glorious bearer of the oblation, the banner of the assembly, the excellent messenger, the one who swiftly attains his goal.
Mātariśvan brought him, the twice-born, like celebrated wealth, as a gift to Bhr̥gu.

Both his instructors attend upon him—the *uśij* who possess oblations and those who are mortals. Even before [the gods of] heaven, the invoker has sat down; he is the question-worthy lord of the people, the wise one among the clans.
May our newest hymn of praise, born from the heart, reach him whose tongue is honey-sweet;

him whom the human priests, the Āyus, providing sacrificial food, have brought forth in the assembly. The longing, purifying, and beneficent one has been established among the people as the most excellent invoker among men.

The domestic one, the lord of the house, Agni has become the master of riches within the home. As such, we the Gotamas praise you, O Agni, the lord of riches, with our hymns—grooming you like a swift prize-winning horse. May he, the possessor of wealth through prayer, come quickly in the morning.

To him, the truly powerful and swift one, I offer this hymn of praise like a refreshing draught—for the magnanimous Indra, who is worthy of the song. To him, the irresistible one, I present these most excellent prayers, O Ṛcīṣama.
To him indeed, as if offering a gift, I extend my song of praise; I bring forth this hymn with perfect skill for his protection.

For Indra, the ancient lord, they have purified their prayers with the heart, the mind, and inspired thought. To him indeed I bring this most excellent, light-winning hymn of praise with my own mouth; with the most abundant invocations of our thoughts and well-fashioned songs, I shall exalt the patron.
For him alone I fashion this hymn of praise, as a carpenter fashions a chariot for its owner;
and I offer songs and well-crafted prayers to Indra, the bearer of songs, the all-impelling, the wise.
For him alone, as one anoints a steed, I with my ladle anoint the song of praise for Indra, the seeker of glory.
To praise the hero who dwells among the bounteous, the breaker of forts whose glory is celebrated;
for him indeed Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the thunderbolt, most skillful and resonant for the battle.
With it, the lordly one, striking at will, found even Vṛtra’s vital spot, he who is of boundless power.
At the libations of his mother, he has immediately drunk the great draught and the choice food;
the mighty Viṣṇu has carried off the cooked offering, pierced the boar, and cast aside the mountain.
For him indeed, even the divine wives, the consorts of the gods, have woven a song of praise for Indra after his great deed.
He has encompassed heaven and earth, the two wide worlds; they do not encompass his greatness.
His majesty indeed exceeds that of heaven, earth, and the intermediate space.
Indra, the self-ruling lord praised by all, the sovereign of light, has grown strong for the battle within the home.
By his very might, Indra shattered with his thunderbolt Vṛtra who was swelling in strength;
like penned-up cows, he released the rivers, being mindful to bestow glory upon us.
Indeed, by his brilliance the rivers were stayed when he hemmed them in on all sides with his thunderbolt.
Acting as lord for the donor, bestowing gifts, the victorious one made a ford for Turvīti.
To him indeed, the lord of vast power, bring forth the thunderbolt with haste against Vṛtra.
Like the joints of an ox, rend him across; hurling [the bolt], let him pass through so that the floods of water may flow.
Proclaim now with new hymns the ancient deeds of this swift one;
when, eager for battle, he brandishes his weapons, he, roaring in his wrath, destroys the enemies.
Out of fear of him, even the firm mountains and heaven and earth tremble at his very birth.
Approaching the dwelling of the longing one with his cry, Nodhas instantly became ready for heroic valor.
To him indeed was this granted among these [men]: that he alone, as lord of abundance, chose it.
Indra helped Pr̥itaśa, who contended for the sun and for the prize of the beautiful horses, as he pressed the soma.
Thus have the Gotamas fashioned for you, O Indra, these well-crafted prayers suitable for the yoking of the bay steeds.
Bestow upon them a thought adorned with every beauty; may he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
We proclaim a hymn of praise like that of the Aṅgirases to the powerful one, the lover of songs, who delights in song.
With well-fashioned hymns, let us sing a song of praise to the one worthy of praise, the far-famed Hero.

Bring forth great homage to the Great One; offer a chanted hymn of praise to the Mighty One, by which our ancient fathers, the Aṅgirases, who knew the tracks, found the cattle while singing their praises.
At the impulse of Indra and the Aṅgirases, Saramā found nourishment for her offspring.
Bṛhaspati split the mountain and found the cows; the men lowed together with the kine.
He, the one who utters the cry, with the Navagvas, using the seven seers and their resonant song, shattered the mountain with his voice.
O powerful Indra, with the Saraṇyu steeds and the ten Gu’s, you shattered the enclosure and Vala with a roar.
Praised by the Aṅgirases, O wonder-worker, you disclosed the darkness with the dawn, the sun, and the kine.
You spread out the surface of the earth, O Indra, and you propped up the intermediate region of heaven.
That deed of his, the wonder-worker, is most manifest and most beautiful; it is a wondrous work, that in the secret place he caused the four rivers of honey-colored flow to swell.
Dvitā, the one born of old and dwelling in the same nest, unwearied, was praised with hymns by those who laud him.
Like Bhaga, the doer of wondrous deeds has sustained the two worlds, heaven and earth, in the highest firmament. From of old,
the two young maidens of different forms, ever-renewed and born again, move one after the other by their own inherent ways—
the Night with her dark limbs and the Dawn with her radiant bodies.
Seeking to perform noble deeds, he, the son of wondrous power, has by his might established a friendship that reaches to the furthest limit.
Even within the raw cows you have placed the cooked milk—white milk within the black and the ruddy ones.
From of old, the immortals, the sisters who are ever blue-black, protect their laws with their powers like winds.

Many thousands, like wives and sisters, serve the one who is free from shame; O Wondrous One, the ancient thoughts, seeking wealth and desiring you with reverence and new hymns, have run forth. O Lord of Might, these inspired prayers touch you, as longing wives touch their longing husband.
From of old, O Wondrous One, the riches in your hand have neither diminished nor failed.

You are brilliant, O Indra, wise and full of power; O Lord of Might, aid us with your powers. For the one who honors the ancient, Gotama has fashioned a new prayer for you, O Indra, for the yoking of the bay steeds.
May the powerful Nodhas, rich in inspired thought, come quickly to us at dawn for our well-guided leadership.
O Indra, you are great, you who at birth by your vital powers established heaven and earth.
For when all the mountains, even those vast and firm, trembled before you in fear like scattering dust.

When you, O Indra, drive hither your two bay steeds of different courses, your singer places the thunderbolt in your arms—by which, O Lord of unyielding will, you, invoked by many, hurl forward your many fortresses against the enemies.
You, O Indra, are the true one, the bold; you are the Lord of the Ribhus, the benefactor of men, the conqueror.
You slew Śuṣṇa in the contest for nourishment at the impulse of the youthful, illustrious Kutsa.

You, O Indra, O wielder of the thunderbolt, O performer of manly deeds, did indeed then incite and strike down Vṛtra as your friend. When, O hero of virile power, you, the victorious one, cast the Dasyus far away from their dwelling.

O Indra, you indeed, when seeking to overcome the enemy, shattered even the firm fortresses of mortals that were displeasing to you; O wielder of the thunderbolt, strike down our foes like a chariot-horse crossing over a boundary at full speed.
O Indra, men call upon you in the struggle for waters, in the contest for light, and in the battle.
O self-dependent one, may this aid of yours be swift to reach us in battles for booty during the assembly of men.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you indeed shattered those seven fortresses for Purukutsa while fighting;
just as you effortlessly spread the sacrificial grass for Sudās, O King, you created wide space for Pūru.

O Indra, O God, you have made swell for us that wondrous nourishment, like waters flowing all around, by which, O Hero, you may grant us back our own self, so that it may flow forth at all times like vital strength.
These prayers have been fashioned for you, O Indra, by the Gotamas; they have been spoken with reverence for your two bay steeds.
Bring us well-fashioned strength; may he who is enriched by our prayer come quickly in the morning.
O Nodhas, bring forth a pure hymn to the Maruts—the vigorous host, the noble sacrificers, the wise ordainers.
Like a skillful craftsman with a steady hand, I, the sage, fashion these songs with my mind, which are present at the assemblies.

They were born from heaven, lofty bulls, the youths of Rudra, the Asuras free from blemish; they are purifying, bright like suns, like warriors dripping with blood, terrible in form. The youthful Rudras, ageless, slayers of those who do not give, have grown irresistible like mountains.
They cause even all the firm earthly beings and those of heaven to tremble by their might.
They deck themselves for beauty with wondrous ornaments; they have fastened golden plates upon their chests for splendor.
Upon their shoulders the spears rest firmly; these heroes were born together from heaven by their own inherent power.
The masters, the shakers, the destroyers of enemies, have created winds and lightnings by their powers.
Shaking the heavens, they milk the udders; wandering all around, they swell the earth with milk.
The bounteous Maruts pour forth the waters, providing butter-like milk at the sacrificial assemblies.
Like a steed for rain, they lead forth the prize-winning racer; they milk the thundering, inexhaustible spring.
Mighty, possessing wondrous power, with brilliant luster, self-strong like mountains, they rush swiftly along.
Like wild elephants you devour the forests when you have harnessed your strength among the ruddy dawns.
Like lions they roar, the wise ones; like boars, well-furred, they are all-knowing.
Stirring the nights with spotted deer and spears, they gather together in their impetuous haste, possessing the fury of serpents through their might.
O you who are the glory of the host, speak to heaven and earth; you heroes, seekers of men, possess the fury of serpents through your might.
Like a brilliant vision upon a chariot-seat, like lightning, O Maruts, has your splendor mounted upon your chariots.
O possessors of all wealth, dwelling together with riches, you who are mighty and overflowing with strength have mingled yourselves with your powers.
These heroes, whose impetuosity is infinite and who wear the thunderbolt as their crest, have taken up their arrows in their hands as archers.
With their golden fellies, swelling with milk, they strike up like mountain-rivers;

the Maruts—sacrificial, tireless, self-moving, shaking the firm, makers of the storm, armed with glittering spears. We invoke with our call the son of Rudra, the impetuous, purifying, forest-consumer, and all-seeing one.
Follow for the sake of glory the host of Maruts, which crosses the dust, which is powerful, which possesses the *ṛjīṣa*, and which is vigorous.
O Maruts, that mortal whom you protect with your aid stands preeminent in strength above other men.
With his horses he wins the prize; with his heroes he brings home wealth; he dwells in prosperity and possesses a plan worthy of inquiry.
O Maruts, bestow upon our patrons a glorious strength that is worthy of praise, invincible in battles, and radiant.
May we nourish for a hundred winters our offspring and progeny—wealth-seekers, praiseworthy, and lords of all people.
Now, O Maruts, grant us stable wealth consisting of heroic sons, which overcomes the onset of calamities.
May he who is rich in prayer come quickly in the morning, increasing his wealth a hundredfold and a thousandfold.
Like a thief hiding with his cattle, you move in secret; you harness yourself through homage and carry it away through homage.
The wise, acting in unison, have followed your footsteps; all the worshipful ones have sat down near you.
The gods have followed the decrees of *ṛta*; there has been an encompassing presence like that of heaven over the earth.
The waters have nourished him with praise—the well-formed infant, well-born in the womb, the seat of *ṛta*.
Like delightful prosperity, like the broad earth as a dwelling, like a mountain providing enjoyment, he is a source of bliss like the flowing flood.
Like a steed urged forward in the race, like the flood of a river— who can restrain him?
Kinsman of the rivers, he devours the forests like a brother his sisters, like a king his subjects.
When, impelled by the wind, Agni has spread through the woods, he indeed shears the hair of the earth.
He breathes in the waters like a swan, never resting; by his mental power he is the most wise among the people, the awakener at dawn.

Like Soma, he is a wise ordainer born of Truth; like a young animal, he is far-reaching and radiant from afar. He is like wonderful wealth, like the sun to behold; he is like life, like the vital breath, like an ever-present son.
Like a swift, restless deer he hastens to the woods; like a cow with milk, he is bright and radiant.
He maintains security, delightful as a home; like ripened grain, he is the conqueror of men. Like a praising seer, he is lauded among the people; like a beloved steed, he bestows vital strength.
Difficult to look upon, his radiance is like the eternal will; he is like a wife in her dwelling, dear to everyone.
When he has shone forth, brilliant as a white horse among the people, he is like a golden chariot, impetuous in battles.
Like a released army, he bestows vigor; like an archer’s arrow, he is of terrible aspect.
Yama was born; Yama is the progeny of birth. He is the lover of maidens and the husband of wives.
May we approach him with our chariots for his dwelling, as cows reach their home when he is kindled.
Like the flood of a river, they have rushed downward; the cows lowed at the sight of the light of heaven.

Born in the forests, a friend among mortals, he chooses obedience like an unaging king. Like security, he is good; like a ritual act, he is auspicious. He becomes a well-disposed invoker and a bearer of oblations.
Holding all manly powers in his hand, he established the gods while sitting in the secret place.
There the men, performers of sacred thought, find her as they recite the hymns fashioned in their hearts.
Like the Unborn, he has supported the earth and propped up the sky with true mantras.
O Agni, guard the dear places of the cattle; you, whose life is all-encompassing, have entered every secret cave.
He who has perceived him dwelling in the secret cave, he who has sat down at the stream of Order—
those who discern and honor the laws of Order have proclaimed riches for him.
He who, by his greatness, has spread through the plants, and likewise among offspring and those about to bring forth.
The all-encompassing thought, dwelling in the home of the waters, the wise have fashioned together like a seat.
Mixing [the offerings], the swift one has approached heaven; he uncovers the nights for all that stands and moves.
For he alone, as a god among all the gods, encompasses them by his greatness.
From the very beginning, all have delighted in your wisdom, O God, when you were born living from the dry wood.
All have partaken of your divinity, honoring the Name and the Eternal Law with their immortal ways.
Through the impulse of the Eternal Law and the thought of the Eternal Law, they who possess all life have performed all their works.
Whoever shall offer gifts to you, or whoever shall serve you—be mindful of him and bestow wealth upon him.
Seated as the Hotṛ-priest among the offspring of Manu, he is indeed the lord of these riches.
Desiring seed within their bodies, they have come to a common understanding through their own innate powers, being free from delusion.
The sons of the father took pleasure in his will, they who, being swift, heeded his command.
He of many cattle threw open the doors of wealth; the friend of the house adorned the firmament with stars.
Bright and blazing like the lover of the Dawn, he has filled the two worlds together like the light of heaven.
Born forth, you have surpassed all by your wisdom; though being their son, you have become the father of the gods.
Agni is the wise and unerring ordainer, who knows the udder of the cows and the sweetness of the foods.
Like a beloved guest among men, he sits in the midst, the joyous one within the dwelling.
Like a son born in the house, delightful, like a prize-winning steed well-pleased, he has crossed over the clans.
When I, together with the men of common origin, call upon the clans, may Agni attain all things through his divinity.
No one violates these laws of yours, since you have granted obedience to these men.
That indeed is your wondrous deed, that you, joined with your peerless men, have rent asunder the fortresses.
Like the lover of the Dawn, the radiant one, he has shone forth; he of well-known form has made himself known to him.
Carrying him by their own power, they have thrown open the doors; all have shouted aloud at the sight of the heavenly light.
May we win many riches through our inspired thought; may Agni, the beautifully radiant, pervade all things.
He, the wise one, has taken notice of the divine ordinances and of the birth of the human race.
He who is the embryo of the waters, the embryo of the forests, the embryo of all that is stationary, and the embryo of all that moves.
Even upon the rock, within the dwelling, he is like the immortal one among the people, well-disposed.
For he, O Agni, is the lord of riches through the night; let him who serves him well with hymns be blessed.
O wise one, protect these many beings, you who know the generations of the gods and mortals alike.

Him whom many nights have strengthened, who is manifold in form, who is the breath of life for both the stationary and the moving, and who is impelled by the *ṛta*—the Hotṛ-priest has been successful, seated in the light, performing all true deeds.
You bestow renown upon the cattle and within the forests; all bring tribute to you, O Lord of the Light.
Men have worshipped you in many places, bringing forth your wisdom as one brings forth the wealth of a living father.
Like a successful seeker, like a greedy hero, like a warrior, like a formidable traveler, you are fierce in battles.
The longing ones have stirred him who longs, as wives of the same dwelling stir their own husband.
The sisters have taken pleasure in the dark one and the ruddy one, as cows do in the brightly shining Dawn.
With their hymns, our fathers, the Aṅgirases, shattered even the firm and solid rock with their roar.
They made for us a path to the great heaven; they found the day, the light, and the rays of the dawn.
They have established the cosmic order and furthered his inspired thought; from then on, the noble ones, worthy of honor, have been distributed abroad.
Unthirsting, the active fingers move toward the gods, strengthening their generation with the sacrificial food.
When Mātariśvan churned him out, he was borne away; he became the bright, noble one in every house.
Then, as if for a more powerful king, he who belongs to the Bhrigus undertook the office of messenger.
When he prepared the juice for his great father Dyaus, the wise one moved toward Pr̥śni. The archer boldly released the missile at him; the god bestowed his brilliance upon his own daughter.

He who shines within his own house for you, or who offers homage day after day according to his devotion—O Agni, increase his strength twofold; may he whom you urge forward travel in the same chariot with wealth. All nourishments attend upon Agni, just as the seven mighty rivers flow toward the ocean.

Our strength is not distinguished by our kinsmen; may he who knows find favor among the gods. When the brilliance reached the lord of men for nourishment, the pure seed was poured down from heaven in the encounter. Agni brought forth and perfected the blameless, youthful, and well-intentioned host.
He who, like thought, traverses the paths instantly—alone, the Sun, rules over all wealth.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, the two kings with beautiful hands, you who guard the beloved nectar within the cows.
O Agni, being a wise seer, do not forget our ancestral friendships.

Old age impairs the form like a cloud; before that curse reaches you, speak for us. Holding in his hand many manly wisdoms and the works of the eternal ordainer, Agni has become the lord of riches, accomplishing all immortal deeds.
The all-wise immortals, seeking him, did not find the calf who was hidden from us;

exhausted, following his tracks and meditating on the prayer, they stood at the highest station of the beautiful Agni. When, O Agni, the pure ones had worshipped you, the pure one, with clarified butter for three autumns.
They assumed names worthy of sacrifice; the well-born ones brought their bodies to perfection.
Finding the two vast worlds, the worshipful sons of Rudra have raised themselves up.
The mortal, discerning in the distribution of the sacrificial portions, has found Agni stationed in the highest place.
Coming together, they sat down facing one another; accompanied by their wives, they paid homage to him who is worthy of homage.
Casting off their bodies, they made them their own, as friend protects friend, keeping watch with the blink of an eye.
When the worshipful ones discovered the thrice-seven secret places hidden within you, they found the tracks.
With them, being of one accord, they guard the immortal nectar; protect the cattle, and guard that which stands and that which moves.

O Agni, knowing the pathways of the peoples, you have distributed the nourishments in succession; grant us life. Knowing the paths within, you have become the tireless messenger and the bearer of the oblation for those who travel to the gods.
The wise ones, knowing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), have opened wide the seven mighty doors of heaven and the gates of wealth.
Saramā found the firm stall of cattle, by which the human race now enjoys its sustenance. Those who have established all noble offspring, creating a path toward immortality— 1.72.8–9.1.
By her greatness, the great Earth has spread herself out; Aditi, the mother, with her sons, for the nourishment of the bird.
The immortals have bestowed beautiful splendor upon him when they fashioned the two eyes of heaven.
Then, like rivers set free, they flow downward; the ruddy dawns have recognized Agni.
Like wealth inherited from his father, he bestows vitality; like the instruction of one who knows, he is a perfect guide.
Like a guest at a pleasant meal, he is gratifying; like a Hotṛ-priest, he has traversed the dwelling of the worshipper.
Like the god Savitṛ whose thoughts are true, he protects all strongholds by his wisdom.
Praised by many, true like the Immortal One, he has become dear as one’s own self, worthy of being cherished.

Like a god who sustains all, he dwells upon the earth; like a king with loyal friends, he is well-disposed. Like heroes seated in their strongholds for protection, he is blameless, like a woman beloved by her husband.
Thee, O Agni, ever-kindled in the house, men serve in their firm-set dwellings.
Upon thee they have bestowed abundant splendor; become the sustainer of all life and of riches.
O Agni, may the liberal patrons obtain nourishment; may the wise givers attain a full span of life.
May we win booty in battles against the enemy, establishing our portion among the gods for the sake of glory.
For the lowing milch-cows of Truth, distributed by Heaven, have swelled with full udders;
seeking favor from afar, the rivers have flowed across the mountain.
O Agni, seeking thy favor, the worshipful ones have established glory in heaven;
they have made Night and Dawn of different forms, and have joined together the dark color and the ruddy.
O Agni, may we and our patrons be those mortals whom thou hast impelled toward wealth.

Like a shadow you accompany the entire world; having filled the two worlds and the mid-air, O Agni, may we, protected by you, conquer steeds with steeds, men with men, and heroes with heroes. May our wise patrons, being masters of wealth inherited from their fathers, attain a hundred winters.
O Agni, O Ordainer, may these hymns of praise be pleasing to you, to your mind and to your heart.
May we be able to control the reins of your wealth, bestowing upon ourselves the glory allotted by the gods. As we approach the sacrifice, let us address a prayer to Agni.
Far from us, yet hearing us—
He who, being the foremost, protected the household of the donor when the peoples had come together in their longings.
And let the people say, "Agni has arisen as the slayer of Vṛtra,
the winner of wealth in every battle. In whose house you are the messenger, you go to his oblations for their enjoyment.
You make the sacrifice wondrous.
Him, O Angiras, the people call one to whom offerings are well-presented, a good god, O son of strength, and one for whom the sacrificial grass is well-laid.
And bring those gods here for our praise,
O bright one, so that they may enjoy the oblations.
Not even the slightest sound of the chariot or its horses is heard when you are moving.
Since you, O Agni, have performed the office of messenger— Under your protection, the prize-seekers, free from shame, one after another, The donor, O Agni, has stepped forward.
And, O divine Agni, you win for the donor of oblations great splendor and abundant heroic strength from among the gods.
Accept this most extensive speech, which is most pleasing to the gods as a celestial banquet.
Offering oblations into your mouth,
O Agni, best of the Aṅgiras and most skilled in ritual, we shall now speak to you a beloved prayer that wins the prize.
Who among men is your kinsman, O Agni? Who is the one who offers the sacrifice? Who indeed are you, and upon whom do you rest?
You, O Agni, are the kinsman of men; you are their dear friend.
A friend to be praised by his friends. Sacrifice for us to Mitra and Varuṇa; sacrifice to the gods and to the great *Ṛta*.
O Agni, perform the sacrifice within your own home.
RV_01.076.01.1 What approach of the mind would be most pleasing to you for your choice, O Agni? What inspired thought [would be so]?
RV_01.076.01.2 Or who has attained your skill through sacrifices? Or with what mind might we serve you?
RV_01.076.02.1 Come, O Agni; sit down here as the Hotṛ-priest. Being undeceivable, be our excellent leader.
May Heaven and Earth, who pervade all things, protect you; I sacrifice to the gods for their great goodwill.
O Agni, burn away all the Rakṣasas; become the protector of our sacrifices against curses.
Then, with your two bay steeds, bring hither the Lord of Soma; we have prepared hospitality for this bountiful giver.

With speech that brings offspring, and with my mouth as the bearer [of the oblation], I invoke you; sit down here together with the gods. Perform the office of the *hotṛ* and the *potr*, O worshipful one; be the giver and the progenitor of riches.
Just as you, being a seer yourself, sacrificed to the gods with the oblations of the wise Manu and with the help of the seers.
Thus, O most truthful Hotṛ, O Agni, perform the sacrifice today with your joyous ladle.
How shall we offer to Agni? What song, beloved by the gods, is recited for him, the radiant one?
He who is the immortal among mortals, the observer of Truth, the Hotṛ, and the best of sacrificers—he thus brings the gods hither.
Him who is most peaceful at the sacrifices, the observer of *ṛta*, the Hotṛ—bring him hither with prostrations.
When Agni goes for the sake of the mortal, he awakens the gods; he shall perceive them and worship with his mind.
For he is the will, he is the hero, he is the effective one; like Mitra, he has become the charioteer of the wondrous.

To him, the first among those worthy of sacrifice, the god-seeking clans of the Āryas address their words, he who is wondrous. May that Agni, the most heroic of men, the destroyer of enemies, accept our songs, our prayer, and our protection. And may he, the most powerful one, together with those who are liberal givers, impelled by strength, further our inspired thought.
Thus has Agni, the observer of Truth, Jātavedas, been praised by the inspired Gotamas.
May he cause splendor to swell for them; may he, being wise, go toward their strength and prosperity according to his pleasure.
O Jātavedas, most observant one, the Gotamas have addressed you with their song.
We praise you aloud with splendors.
Gotama, desiring wealth, honors you with his song— with splendors...
As such, we invoke you, the greatest winner of booty, like Aṅgiras, with splendors...
As such, we invoke you, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, who has shaken off the Dasyus.
RV_01.078.04.2: With splendors...
RV_01.078.05.1: We, the Rahūgaṇas, have spoken a honeyed word to Agni; RV_01.078.05.2: With splendors...
Golden-haired in the expanse of the mid-air, he is like a roaring serpent, impetuous as the wind;
with pure radiance, he is mindful of the dawns, glorious and true like industrious women.
Your well-winged birds have measured out the spaces with their courses; the black bull has bellowed when this [world] came into being.
Like auspicious, smiling women he has come; the mists fall and the clouds thunder.
When he comes, swelling with the milk of *ṛta*, leading along the straightest paths of *ṛta*, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Parijman moisten the skin in the womb of the lower realm.
O Agni, lord of wealth consisting of cattle, O young son of strength, bestow upon us great renown, O Jātavedas!
Being kindled, he is the Vasu, the sage; Agni is to be praised with song.
O you of many aspects, shine forth wealth upon us!
O King Agni, by your own power, burn away the demons at night, at dawn, and throughout the day— O you with sharp teeth, consume them!
O Agni, protect us with your aids during the chanting of the Gāyatra hymn,
you who are to be praised in all our prayers. O Agni, bring to us wealth that is all-conquering and most excellent.
Most difficult to overcome in all battles.
O Agni, with your gracious favor, bestow upon us wealth that nourishes for a full lifespan and grant us mercy so that we may live.
O Gotama, bring forward purified words and songs to Agni of the sharp radiance, seeking his favor. O Agni, may he who seeks to harm us fall down, even though he be far away.
Be for our prosperity!
The thousand-eyed Agni, who observes all people, drives away the demons;
as the Hotṛ priest worthy of praise, he is glorified.
For thus, O Soma, in thy exhilaration, the priest has fashioned this strengthening hymn.
O mightiest wielder of the thunderbolt, by thy power thou hast driven the serpent from the earth, praising thy own sovereign dominion.
That bull-like exhilaration, the pressed Soma brought by the falcon, has taken hold of thee.
With which [strength] you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, struck down Vṛtra from the waters by your might—praising [you]...
Go forth, advance, be bold; your thunderbolt shall not be stayed.
For your manly power, O Indra, is strength; slay Vṛtra, win the waters—praising [you]...
O Indra, you struck Vṛtra down from the earth and from the sky.
Release these life-sustaining waters, accompanied by the Maruts; [we shall] sing praises...
Indra, incensed, struck the back of the violently shaking Vṛtra with his thunderbolt.
Advancing, he strikes down, impelling the waters to flow, chanting...
He strikes down upon the ridge with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt;
Indra, exhilarated by the soma-juice, seeking a path for his friends, chants...
O Indra, wielder of the stone, O wielder of the thunderbolt, yours alone is this unyielding heroic power.
For when you struck down that illusory beast with your own magic, you were chanting [this praise].
Your thunderbolts have spread out across the ninety navigable rivers.
Great is your heroic power, O Indra; strength has been placed within your two arms—let us sing praises!

(RV 1.80.8) Sing praises together by the thousands; let twenty chant around him. Let a hundred follow after him with songs; let them sing praises as the sacred prayer (*brahman*) is raised up for Indra. (RV 1.80.9)
Indra struck down the power of Vṛtra with his overwhelming force;
great indeed was that manly deed of his, when, having slain Vṛtra, he released the waters while chanting.
Even these two great worlds tremble before your wrath out of fear.
When you, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, accompanied by the Maruts, slew Vṛtra with your might, [the seers] sang...
Neither by his trembling nor by his roar did Vṛtra terrify Indra;
against him the iron thunderbolt with its thousand points was hurled, as [the seers] sang...

When you, O Indra, with your thunderbolt, struck Vṛtra and his lightning-bolt together; when you, desiring to slay the serpent, exerted your power in heaven— while you were chanting, O wielder of the stone,
at your shout both that which stands and that which moves trembled.
Even Tvaṣṭṛ himself trembles with fear at your wrath, O Indra; chanting, he bows down in awe.
For there is no one who can surpass Indra in heroic deeds, as we acknowledge.
In him the gods have concentrated manly strength, wisdom, and power—chanting, they bow down in awe.
The prayer which Atharvan, Manu’s father, fashioned with his mind—that prayer, as of old, Indra has gathered together; in him the sacred words and hymns have met, and they have sung praises.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been strengthened by men for exhilaration and for power.
In great battles and even in small ones, we invoke him; may he further us in our quests for booty.
For you, O Hero, are worthy of the army; you are the one who bestows abundant wealth.
You are the increaser of even the meager; you grant riches in abundance to the sacrificer who presses the soma for you.
When battles arise and booty is set before the bold one—yoke your two bay steeds that flow with exhilaration! Whom will you slay? To whom will you grant wealth? O Indra, grant us wealth!
By his great wisdom, the terrible one has increased his power according to his own will.
Exalted in glory, the fair-cheeked one, lord of bay horses, has taken the iron thunderbolt in his two hands.
He has filled the earthly realm and pressed against the luminous spheres in heaven.
O Indra, no one like you has ever been born, nor will there ever be; you have grown beyond all.
He, the noble one, who bestows upon the donor the food of mortals—may Indra grant us his aid; distribute your abundant wealth, and may I partake of your bounty.
For in every exhilaration, he of upright intellect has given us herds of cattle.
Gather in both hands many hundreds of riches; sharpen us and bring wealth hither.
Rejoice in the pressed juice, O Hero, for the sake of strength and bounty;
for we know you as the possessor of abundant wealth, and so we have poured forth our desires—therefore, be our protector.
These people here, O Indra, nourish for you every desirable thing. Look among the peoples for the wealth of those who do not offer; bring that wealth to us.
Listen well to our songs, O Maghavan, just as a mother [listens] to her sons.
When you will truly act for us who possess true wealth, then, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds.
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; the dear ones have shaken themselves free.
The self-luminous inspired singers have praised you with their newest hymn; now, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds.
O Maghavan, we would worship you, who are so beautiful to behold.
Now, O you whose chariot-seat is full, being praised, go according to our desires; yoke the horses... He indeed shall mount that bull-like chariot which finds the cattle.
O Indra, he who understands the full vessel of the *hāriyojana*—yoke it...
O Lord of a hundred powers, let your right horse be yoked, and also your left.
With that, being exhilarated by the soma-juice, go toward your beloved wife—yoke it...
I yoke for you with a sacred prayer your two long-maned bay steeds; come hither, for you have taken them into your hands.
The impetuous pressed juices have exhilarated you; O wielder of the thunderbolt, accompanied by Pūṣan, you have rejoiced together with your wife.
O Indra, the mortal man whom you protect with your aids becomes foremost among those possessing horses and cattle, being well-favored.
Thou fillest him with even more abundant wealth, as the waters flow from all sides into the ocean, each knowing its own course.
The divine waters approach the place of the Hotṛ-priest; they look down upon the sacrifice as if looking toward the vast expanse of space.
The gods lead forward the one who seeks the gods; like suitors, they take pleasure in the lover of sacred prayer.
Upon the two [stones] you have bestowed the hymn-worthy word, they who, as a pair with uplifted ladles, perform worship together.
Unrestrained, he dwells and prospers within your ordinance; auspicious is the power for the sacrificer who presses the soma.
The Aṅgirases first assumed vital strength when the fires were kindled by those who, through their skillful work, used the sacrificial peg.

The men found all the food of Paṇi; they gathered cattle and horses as their booty. Atharvan was the first to clear the paths with sacrifices; from him Sūrya was born as the guardian of the sacred law (vrata).
Uśanas Kāvya drove forth the cows; together we worship the immortal birth of Yama.
When the sacrificial grass is strewn for the sake of good offspring, or when the hymn proclaims its fame in heaven;
where the pressing-stone speaks and the singer recites his praise, Indra delights in those arrivals.
Soma has been pressed for you, O Indra; O most powerful and bold one, come hither!
May Indra fill you with power, as the sun fills the mid-air with its rays.
The two bay steeds carry Indra, whose might is unassailable,
To the praises of the seers and to the sacrifice of men.
Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra; your two bay steeds have been yoked by our prayer.
May the pressing-stone, with its roar, turn your mind toward us.
O Indra, drink this pressed juice, the most excellent, immortal exhilaration.
The streams of the bright [Soma] have flowed toward you at the seat of the Eternal Order. Now sing praises for Indra and proclaim your hymns;
the pressed Soma-drops have exhilarated him; pay homage to his supreme might.
No one is a better charioteer than you when, O Indra, you guide your two bay horses.
No one has ever equaled you in might, nor has anyone with fine steeds attained your level.
He alone who bestows wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations is truly renowned.
The sovereign, the irresistible Indra—indeed!
When will he trample with his foot the miserly mortal like a mushroom?
When indeed will Indra hear our songs? Indeed!
For whoever, having pressed the Soma, desires to win you away from many [rivals]—O Indra, that fierce power indeed prevails; truly, it is yours alone.
Thus do the Gaurī cows drink of the sweet, well-flavored mead from every side.
RV 1.84.10.2: Those who, moving in harmony with the bull Indra, rejoice for the sake of splendor—those excellent ones [follow] his own sovereignty.
RV 1.84.11.1: Eager for his touch, those dappled cows mix the Soma;
RV 1.84.11.2: Indra’s beloved milch-cows impel the thunderbolt, the missile; they are excellent...
Wise, they honor his conquering power with reverence; they follow his many ordinances for the sake of primordial thought.
With the bones of Dadhyañc, Indra, unopposed, struck down the Vṛtras.
He struck down ninety-nine [demons]. Seeking the horse’s head which was hidden away in the mountains, he found it at Śaryaṇāvat.
There they recognized the secret name of Tvaṣṭṛ’s cow,
right there in the dwelling of the moon.
Who today yokes to the pole of Order the vigorous, impetuous, and ill-disposed oxen?
They have arrows in their mouths, yet they are heart-gladdening and sources of bliss; he who provides for their maintenance shall live.
Who flees? Who is pursued? Who is afraid? Who perceives Indra as being present?
Who is near him? Who will speak in favor of his offspring, or of his cattle, or of his wealth, or of his own body, or of his people?

Who kindles Agni with oblation and ghee? Who shall worship with the ladle according to the fixed seasons? To whom shall the gods bring their swift offerings? Who, as a god of goodly sacrifice, shall be considered a welcome guest?
Verily, O most powerful God, you alone shall praise the mortal man.
O Maghavan, there is no other comforter besides you; O Indra, I speak these words to you.
Let not your gifts nor your aids, O Vasu, ever fail us at any time. And bestow upon us all human riches from every side for the sake of our people.

Those who adorn themselves like wives, like coursers on their way—the sons of Rudra, doers of wondrous deeds—they have indeed made heaven and earth grow; the heroes, impetuous in the assemblies, rejoice.
Having grown strong, they have attained greatness; the Rudras have established their seat in heaven.
Chanting their hymn and generating vital power, those whose mother is Pṛśni have assumed glorious splendors.

When, O mothers of cattle, they adorn themselves with ointments, the radiant ones place shining ornaments upon their bodies. They drive away every adversary; along their paths, clarified butter flows.

Those who shine forth as great warriors with their spears, shaking even the unshakable by their might— when you, O Maruts, the hosts of bulls, yoked the spotted deer to your chariots, swift as thought;
when you yoked the spotted deer to your chariots, O Maruts, urging the thunderbolt forward for the sake of booty.
And the streams of the ruddy one burst forth; like a skin with water, they drench the earth.

Let your swift-gliding, rapid-flying coursers carry you hither; come forward with your arms. Sit upon the sacrificial grass; a wide seat has been prepared for you. O Maruts, rejoice in the sweet draught of the soma-juice.
They grew strong by their own power through their greatness; they ascended to the firmament and made for themselves a wide dwelling.
When Viṣṇu ran toward the bull who distills exhilaration, they sat down upon the beloved sacrificial grass like birds.
Like heroes eager for combat, like warriors rushing forward, like those seeking glory, they strove together in the battles.
All beings are afraid of the Maruts; these heroes are like kings, terrible to behold.
When Tvaṣṭṛ, the skillful craftsman, fashioned the well-made golden thunderbolt with its thousand points, Indra took it up to perform manly deeds; he slew Vṛtra and cast down the ocean of waters.
They pushed the well upward by their might; they split even the firmly fixed mountain asunder.
Blowing their flute, the bounteous Maruts performed deeds of joy in the intoxication of Soma. They pushed the well sideways in that direction, pouring out the fountain for the thirsty Gotama.

May they come with their protection, O you of wondrous luster; may they satisfy the desire of the sage through their powers. The protections that you have for the one who exerts himself, grant those threefold shelters to the donor.
Extend those to us, O Maruts; bestow upon us wealth, O bulls, together with heroic sons.

O Maruts, mighty ones of heaven, that man in whose dwelling you drink [the soma] is indeed the most well-guarded of people. O you who carry the sacrifice by means of sacrifices, or [you who come] through the hymns of the inspired singer—
O Maruts, hear the call! Or rather, he for whom you, O powerful ones, have fashioned a sage— such a man shall go to a stall filled with cattle.
Upon the sacred grass of this hero, Soma is pressed during the daily rites;
his hymn of praise and his exhilarating draught are recited.
May all the peoples listen to him, he who stands over all.
Even to the Sun have you flowed with nourishing streams.
For through many autumns we have worshipped you, O Maruts,
with the protections granted to all people.
O Maruts, worthy of sacrifice, may that mortal be fortunate whose offerings you carry across. O heroes of true power, [be mindful] of the sweat of him who exerts himself in worship.
You know the longing of the one who seeks you;
O you of true power, reveal that [treasure] through your greatness. Pierce the demon with your lightning bolt.
Concealing the secret darkness, drive away every devouring demon; create the light for which we long.
Exceedingly vigorous, powerful, and overflowing with strength, they are unbending, unshakable, and drinkers of the *ṛjīṣa*.
Most beloved and most heroic, they have adorned themselves with ointments, like certain rays of light with their beams.
O Maruts, when you have set your course upon whatever path, like birds flying through the hollows of the trees;
then the vessels on your chariots drip with abundance—sprinkle the honey-colored fatness for the one who praises you.
At their rushings forth, the earth trembles as if unsteady during their courses when they harness themselves for glory.
They are playful, roaring, with glittering spears; shaking all things, they themselves proclaim their own greatness.
For that youthful host, with spotted horses, moves by its own power; it is sovereign, encompassed by mighty strengths.
You are the true one, the pursuer of debts, the blameless; you are the furtherer of this prayer, and thus the bull-like host [is yours].
By the lineage of the ancient father we speak; the tongue of Soma goes forth with its vision.
When the chanters have reached Indra with their labor, they assume the names worthy of sacrifice.
For glory, they have mingled themselves with splendors; they are well-armed with rays and with singers.
Armed with axes, impetuous, and fearless, they have found the beloved domain of the Maruts.
O Maruts, come hither on your lightning-bright chariots, which are resonant with song, equipped with spears, and winged with horses.
Fly toward us with most abundant nourishment like birds, O you of wondrous power!
They go for our choice, for beauty, with their ruddy, tawny horses that hasten the chariot. Bright as a golden ornament, equipped with axes, they strike the earth with the tires of their chariot.
For the sake of glory, what axes are upon your bodies? May they, like the wisdoms, raise the woods aloft.
For you, O Maruts of noble birth and great splendor, they set the stone in motion.
Like vultures eager for days, they have come around you; [they have accepted] this prayer and the divine Vārkarī.
The Gotamas, performing the sacred prayer with their hymns, pushed open the high enclosure so that [Indra] might drink.
This very place was not perceived as a distance when, O Maruts, Gotama sang for you; he saw you as you sped along on golden wheels, like boars with tusks of iron.
RV 1.88.6: This song of yours, O Maruts, follows you like the voice of a singer; it resounds toward you like the chant of a priest.
It has spontaneously burst forth from his hands according to its own nature. RV 1.89.1:
May auspicious thoughts come to us from every side—thoughts that are undeceived, unassailable, and victorious.
May the gods always be with us for our prosperity, our guardians day by day, never failing in their care.
May the auspicious favor of the upright gods be ours; may the bounty of the gods turn toward us. We have sought the friendship of the gods; may the gods extend our life that we may live.
We invoke them with the ancient invocation: Bhaga, Mitra, Aditi, Dakṣa, and the Infallible One; Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī—may she, the auspicious one, grant us happiness.
May Vāta blow that healing medicine upon us which brings joy; may Mother Earth and Father Heaven grant it.
O pressing-stones, pressers of Soma, bringers of bliss, hear this! O Ashvins, you who are worthy of our thought, hear this!

We invoke for protection that Lord of all that moves and stands, the stimulator of the intellect. May Pushan, with his wealth, be for our increase—our protector and infallible guardian for our well-being.
May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the all-knowing, grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are unharmed, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us.
The Maruts, whose steeds are spotted and who have Pṛśni as their mother, move toward splendor; they hasten to the assemblies.
May the Manavas, whose tongue is Agni and whose eyes are the Sun, and all the gods, come here to us with their protection.

O Gods, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O Holy Ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious. With firm limbs and bodies, may we praise you and enjoy that lifespan which is ordained by the Gods.
A hundred autumns, O gods, are before us, within which you have ordained the aging of our bodies—that time when sons become fathers. Do not harm our life-span in its course.
Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-air, Aditi is the mother; she is the father, she is the son.

May all the gods, Aditi, and the five peoples—Aditi is what has been born, and Aditi is what is yet to be born. May Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise ones, lead us with straight guidance; may Aryaman, in harmony with the gods, do the same.
For they are the masters of wealth, the dispensers of riches; they are never overcome by their own greatness.
They guard the sacred laws at all times.
May they, the immortals, grant protection to us mortals.
Driving away our enemies,
may Indra and the Maruts, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and those worthy of praise, clear out our paths for our well-being.
And may our prayers, O Pūṣan, which have cattle as their foremost goal, be swift-moving like Viṣṇu;
make us possessors of well-being.
The winds blow sweetness for the one who follows the cosmic order, and the rivers flow with sweetness.
May the plants be sweet for us. Sweet be the night and the dawns; may the earthly realm be full of sweetness, and may the Father Heaven be sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Forest be honey-sweet for us; may the Sun be honey-sweet for us;
may the cows be full of sweetness for us.
May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious to us, and may Aryaman be auspicious to us.
May Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us; may Viṣṇu of the wide stride be auspicious to us.
O Soma, you are preeminent through inspired thought; you lead us along the straightest path.
By your guidance, O Indu, our wise fathers obtained their share of treasure among the gods.
O Soma, you are well-being through your mental powers; you are most skillful through your skills, the knower of all.
You are the bull by your bull-like powers and your greatness; through your splendors, you have become splendid, the beholder of men.
Your laws are indeed those of King Varuṇa; lofty and profound, O Soma, is your domain.
Pure art thou; like Mitra, thou art dear and worthy of skill, even as Aryaman, O Soma.
Those abodes of thine in heaven, those on earth, those on the mountains, in the plants, and in the waters—with all of them, O King Soma, being well-disposed and not wrathful, accept our offerings.
O Soma, you are the lord of the good, you are the king and the slayer of Vṛtra; you are the auspicious power of will. And you, O Soma, being our desire, let us not die, but live on.
The Lord of the Forest, whose praises are dear;
O Soma, you bestow great fortune upon the one who follows the *ṛta*, and you grant strength for life to the youth.
O Soma, O King, protect us on every side from the one who intends evil; let not the friend of one such as you come to harm.
O Soma, those bliss-bestowing aids of yours that exist for the donor—
With those [powers], be our protector.
Accepting this sacrifice and this speech, come hither;
O Soma, be for our increase.
O Soma, we who know the sacred words magnify you with our songs; enter into us as one who is most gracious.
Increasing the household, driving away disease, finding wealth, and augmenting prosperity.
Be a good friend, O Soma; be a source of joy.
O Soma, take delight in our heart, as cattle do in pastures, like a young man in his own home.
O divine Soma, whatever mortal delights in your friendship, him the skillful seer attends.
O Soma, protect us from reproach; guard us from distress.
Be a most gracious friend to us.
Swell up; let virile strength gather from every side within you, O Soma; be present at the gathering of the prize.
Swell up, O most exhilarating Soma, with all your rays;
become for us a most glorious friend for our prosperity.
Let your milks, your strengths, and your bull-like powers that overcome the assailants come together.
Soma, swelling for the sake of immortality, place the highest glories in heaven.
Those stations of yours which they worship with oblation—encompassing all those, protect the sacrifice.
Increasing our household, furthering us, rich in heroes and not slaying our men, O Soma, enter the dwellings.
Soma gives the milch-cow; Soma gives the swift steed; Soma gives the hero who is skillful in action.
He gives one who is fit for the household, fit for the assembly, and fit for the council—a son who brings glory to his father—to him who offers oblations to him.
[He gives] one invincible in battles, a deliverer in conflicts, a winner of light, a winner of waters, the guardian of the stronghold.
O Soma, may we rejoice after you, the conqueror who brings secure dwellings and great renown when born for battle.
O Soma, you generated all these plants; you brought forth the waters and the cattle.
You have stretched out the wide firmament and have dispelled the darkness with light.

O divine Soma, with your divine mind, O powerful one, fight for us to win our share of wealth. Let no one obstruct you; you are the master of heroic might. Provide for both sides in the quest for cattle.
These very Dawns have made their banner appear; in the eastern quarter of the mid-air, they spread their radiance.
Like bold men fashioning their weapons, the ruddy mother-cows come forth toward us. The ruddy beams of light have flown up at will; they have yoked the self-yoked ruddy cows.
The dawns have performed their works as of old; the ruddy ones have spread out their shining luster.
They sing like women active in their tasks, traveling from afar by a common path.
Carrying nourishment for the well-doer who gives good gifts, they come every day to the sacrificer who presses the soma.
She puts on ornaments like a dancing girl; she bares her breast like a cow its udder.
Creating light for the whole world, Dawn opens the enclosure like cows returning to their stall. Her radiant beam has been seen; she spreads abroad and drives away the black monster.
Adorning herself with ornaments like a sacrificial post at the rites, the Daughter of Heaven has spread her wondrous luster.

We have crossed to the further shore of this darkness; the Dawn, shining forth, makes the paths of knowledge manifest. She smiles for glory like a meter, radiant and fair of countenance; she has awakened us for well-being.
The daughter of Heaven, the bringer of light and the leader of true blessings, is praised by the Gotamas.
O Dawn, bestow upon me strengths consisting of progeny, heroes, and horses, preceded by cattle.

O Dawn, may I obtain wealth that is glorious, rich in brave sons, free from Dāsa masters, and characterized by horses. O auspicious one, impelled by strength, you who shine with wondrous fame—grant us great [wealth].
Beholding all beings, O Goddess, she shines forth widely with her gaze turned toward us. Awakening every living creature to movement, she has found the voice of every thinking mortal.
Ever ancient, being born again and again, she adorns herself in her constant form.
Like a skillful gambler who diminishes his stakes, the goddess wears away the life of mortals.
Uncovering the ends of heaven, she has awakened; she drives her sister far away.
Diminishing the generations of men, the maiden shines forth with the glance of her lover.
Like a wonderful, fortunate cow spreading her udder, she has shone far and wide like the flood of a river.
Not violating the divine ordinances, she is visible, appearing with the rays of the sun.
O Uṣas, rich in prizes, bring that wonder to us!
By which we may obtain both offspring and descendants.
O Uṣas, rich in cattle and horses, resplendent one, shine here today upon us with wealth, O you who are full of joy.
Yoke, O possessor of mares, your ruddy horses today at dawn;
then bring to us all auspicious fortunes. O Aśvins, wonder-workers, come to our dwelling, bringing cattle and gold.
With one mind, bring your chariot hither!
O you who have thus brought forth the fame from heaven and light for mankind,
O Aśvins, bring nourishment to us!
O Gods, the wonder-workers who bring bliss, whose paths are golden— may they, awakening at dawn, bring you here to drink the Soma.
O Agni and Soma, you bulls, graciously hear this my invocation.
Accept these hymns with favor; be a source of joy to the donor.
O Agni and Soma, to him who honors you today with this speech, bestow heroic strength, an abundance of cattle, and wealth in horses.
O Agni and Soma, whoever offers an oblation or presents a prepared sacrifice to you, he shall enjoy full life,
with offspring and great heroic strength. O Agni and Soma, that heroic power of yours is well known, by which you seized the cattle from the Pani as he fled for protection.
You two struck down the offspring of Bṛsaya; you found the single light for many. O Agni and Soma, acting with one will, you two placed these luminous realms in heaven.
O Agni and Soma, you released the rivers from reproach and from disgrace when they were seized.
Mātariśvan brought one from heaven; the falcon churned the other from the mountain.
