O Agni and Soma, strengthened by the sacred prayer (*brahman*), you have made wide space for the sacrifice.
O Agni and Soma, partake of the presented oblation; accept it with pleasure, O bulls, and enjoy it.
Be indeed good protectors and good helpers; then bestow well-being and security upon the sacrificer.

O Agni and Soma, whoever honors you with an oblation and with a mind directed toward the gods, and whoever honors you with clarified butter—protect his sacred vow, guard him from distress, and grant great shelter to the people and the folk.
O Agni and Soma, who possess common wealth and are invoked together, accept our songs; you have both become present among the gods.
O Agni and Soma, he who honors you with this [oblation] or with clarified butter—
Shine forth mightily for him, O Agni and Soma; may you both enjoy these our oblations;
come together unto us.
O Agni and Soma, protect our horses; let the cows that yield the oblation swell with milk.
Bestow strength upon us and upon our patrons, and make our sacrifice full of success.
With our inspired thought, we fashion this hymn for the worthy Jātavedas, as one constructs a chariot.
For auspicious is his providence in the assembly; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
He for whom you sacrifice prospers; he dwells free from enemies and possesses great heroic strength. He thrives, and no calamity reaches him, O Agni.
May we be able to kindle thee; may our prayers accomplish their purpose. In thee the gods eat the offered oblation. Bring hither the Ādityas, for we long for them, O Agni...
Let us bring fuel and prepare offerings for thee, mindful of thee at every joint of the sacrifice.
RV_01.094.04.2: Further advance our prayers for the sake of life, O Agni...
RV_01.094.05.1: The protector of the people, his creatures move about by night—both those that are two-footed and those that are four-footed.
RV_01.094.05.2: Wondrous is his manifestation; great is he at the break of dawn, O Agni...
You are the Adhvaryu and the ancient Hotṛ; you are the Praśāstṛ, the Potṛ, and by birth the Purohita. O wise Agni, knowing all priestly duties, you cause them to flourish.
You who are beautiful on every side and uniform—though far away, you shine forth like lightning from heaven.

O God Agni, you see even beyond the darkness of night... May the chariot of the one who presses the soma be foremost, O Gods; may our prayer prevail over the evil-minded. Then recognize this word and let it prosper, O Agni...
Strike down with weapons those of evil intent and the malevolent; destroy all devourers, whether they be far away or near at hand.
And then, O Agni, make the path easy for the sacrifice and for the one who praises you.
When you have yoked to your chariot the two ruddy, red steeds, impelled by the wind, they rush forward like the bellowing of a bull.
O Agni, with your smoke-bannered flame, you bestow wealth upon the forest trees. And at your roar, even the winged birds are struck with fear when your sparks, devouring the grass, fly abroad.
That is a path easy for your chariots and for those who ride in them, O Agni.
This [offering] is for the sustenance of Mitra and Varuṇa; it is the wondrous appeaser of the wrath of the Maruts. O Agni, being gracious, turn their minds toward us again.
You are the god of gods, a wondrous friend; you are the Vasu of the Vasus, beloved at the sacrifice.
May we be under your most extensive protection, O Agni...
That is your auspiciousness, that when kindled in your own abode and invoked with Soma, you awaken as the most merciful one;
you bestow jewels and wealth upon the donor, O Agni...
To whomsoever you, O possessor of beautiful wealth, grant sinlessness and wholeness from Aditi—
whomsoever you impel with auspicious power, may we be those who possess your wealth consisting of progeny.
O Agni, you who are the knower of good fortune, do you, a god, extend our lifespan here.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this as a great gift.
Two of different forms move toward their common goal; one after the other, they suckle the calf.
In the one, he becomes golden-hued and self-sustaining; in the other, he is seen bright and full of splendor.
The tireless young women have brought forth this widely-sustained embryo of Tvaṣṭṛ.
They lead him around, he who has sharp-edged weapons, self-glorious, and shining brightly among the people. They honor his three births: one in the ocean, one in heaven, and one in the waters.

Following the eastern direction of the earthly realms, he has established the seasons in their proper order, presiding over them. Who among you has perceived this secret? The calf has brought forth his mothers by his own inherent powers;
as the embryo of many, the great seer, possessing self-sustaining power, emerges from the lap of the active waters.
The lovely one, worthy of invocation, grows within them; upright in their lap, he is self-glorious among those who lie prostrate.
Both [worlds] were afraid of Tvaṣṭṛ as he was being born; turning toward him, they wait upon the lion with delight.
Both auspicious ones wait upon him like two women; like lowing cows, they have approached him with their ways.
He has become the Lord of skill among the skilled, he whom they anoint from the right with oblations.
Like Savitṛ, he stretches out his arms; as he rushes forward in his dread, he strives toward both sides.
He raises up his bright, glittering [form] from himself alone; he leaves new garments for his mothers.

He assumes a brilliant form, even higher, when he mingles with the waters and the rays of light in his dwelling. The seer’s prayer cleanses the foundation; that assembly has become a gathering among the gods.
Your wide expanse encompasses the foundation, the shining domain of the Mighty One.
O Agni, kindled with all your own glories, protect us with your infallible guardians.
In the desert he creates a stream, a path, and a wave; with his bright waves he reaches the earth.
He places all ancient things within his bellies and moves within the newly born plants.
Thus, O Agni, increasing by our fuel, shine forth with wealth for our glory, O Purifier!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and also Heaven grant this to us.
He, being born by strength as of old, has immediately assumed all wisdom and poetic insights.
The waters and the *dhiṣaṇā* (the sacrificial vessel) furthered the rite; the gods established Agni as the bestower of wealth (*draviṇodās*).
By means of the ancient invocation and his wisdom, he brought forth these offspring of men.
With Vivasvat as his eye, the gods beheld the heavens and the waters.

Praise him, the first accomplisher of sacrifice, whom the Āryan tribes invoke as he hastens forward— the son of strength, Bharata, whose gifts flow abundantly, whom the gods... He, Mātariśvan, who nourishes many boons, has found the path for his offspring, discovering the light of heaven.
The guardian of the people, the progenitor of heaven and earth—the gods...
Night and Dawn, alternately changing their colors, suckle the one infant together;
between heaven and earth the golden disk shines—the gods...
The foundation of wealth, the gatherer of treasures, the banner of sacrifice, the fulfiller of thought, the bird—
guarding him as immortality, the gods [have established] him. Now and of old, he is the seat of riches, the dwelling-place of what has been born and what is being born.
May he be the guardian of what exists and of what shall be abundant; may the gods...

The Giver of Wealth bestows the wealth of the swift one; the Giver of Wealth bestows the wealth of the manly one. May the Giver of Wealth grant us food accompanied by heroes; may the Giver of Wealth grant us long life.
Thus, O Agni, increasing by our fuel, shine forth with wealth for our glory, O Purifier!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
May the sin be burned away from us; O Agni, shine forth wealth upon us.
May he burn away our sin.
With a desire for good fields, for a good path, and for wealth, we sacrifice.
May he burn away...
When he who is the most excellent among these is praised, and when our wise patrons are praised—
may we, O Agni, through thee, be born as thy patrons; may we, through thee, be born.
When the rays of the powerful Agni go forth in all directions... [apah]... when the rays of the powerful Agni go forth in all directions... [apah]...
For you, O you whose face is turned everywhere, encompass all things on every side. ...
[ward off] our enemies, O you whose face is turned everywhere; carry us across as if with a boat.
[He] shall carry us across for our well-being, as one carries a ship across the river. ... [He] shall carry us across.
May we abide in the good graces of Vaiśvānara; for he is the King, the glory of all beings.
Born from here, he beholds this entire universe; Vaiśvānara strives in union with the Sun.
Sought in heaven, sought on earth, Agni, being sought, has entered into all plants.
RV 1.98.2: May Agni Vaiśvānara, who has been sought with power, protect us from harm by day and by night.
RV 1.98.3: O Vaiśvānara, let that be true for you: may riches and liberal patrons attend to us. May that [be] ours...
Let us press the Soma for Jātavedas; may he burn away the wealth of the one who acts with hostility.
May Agni carry us across all difficulties, as a boat carries one across a river, beyond all misfortunes.
He who is the bull, united with manly powers, the sovereign ruler of the great heaven and of the earth.
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts—worthy of invocation in battles and possessing true strength—be our protector with his aid.
He whose course is unassailable like that of the sun, and who in every battle possesses the power of a slayer of Vṛtra; he who is most virile among his own friends through his own movements...
Whose paths go forth, unassailable by might, like the milking streams of the seed of heaven;
he who overcomes hatreds, victorious through his manly deeds— He, the best of the Aṅgiras, became one with the Aṅgiras; a bull among bulls, a friend among friends.

With hymns, he is the singer of hymns, the eldest through his paths... He, like a son with the Rudras, is skillful; in the battle for men, he has overcome the enemies... Surpassing those of common origin, he attains glorious deeds...
He, the subduer of wrath, the maker of the battle-cry, may he win the sun with our men;
on this day, the lord of the virtuous, much-invoked— Him his helpers gladdened in the struggle for heroes; him the people have made the protector of their security.
He alone is the lord of all that is created; ... Men sought him, the Hero, for aid at the festivals of power; they sought him for wealth. He found light even in the blinding darkness; ...
With his left hand he restrains even those who are swelling with pride; with his right hand he gathers all achieved deeds.
Even through the humble, he wins riches;
he is the winner with the hosts and with chariots; may he be known today by all the peoples.
He, by his manly deeds, overcomes those who revile us...
When he, O much-invoked one, gathers together with kinsmen or with strangers at the sacrifice according to his wonts,
for the winning of waters, of offspring, and of progeny...
He, the wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of the Dasyus, terrible and fierce, possessing a thousand insights and a hundred hymns, is skillful;
like the Soma-draught, he belongs to the five peoples by his might.
His thunderbolt roars along with him as he wins the light of heaven; like the sky, his roar is brilliant and impetuous.
To him cling enduring gains and treasures... Whose hymn of praise, through his unceasing power, encompasses both heaven and earth on every side—
he, rejoicing in his sacred rites, shall protect us...
Neither gods, nor mortals, nor even the waters have reached the limit of his power;
he, by his might, has overspread both earth and heaven.
The ruddy, dark-brown, and spotted mare, the bright one, brings wealth to R̥jrāśva.
Bearing the chariot yoked with stallions at the pole, the joyous one has been noticed among the tribes of the Nahuṣas.
O Indra, bull-like hero, the Vārṣāgiras sing this hymn to you for the sake of bounty.
Ṛjrāśva with his side-horses, Ambarīṣa, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna, and Surādhās [have come].
Having slain the Dasyus and Śimyus by his own powers, O much-invoked one, he has struck them down upon the earth with his arrow.
With his bright companions, he won the land; the wielder of the excellent thunderbolt won the sun and won the waters.
May Indra be our advocate every day; unassailed, may we win the prize.
May that [favor] of yours be ours...
Sing forth a word rich in nourishment for the exhilarated one, he who with Ṛjiśvan struck down those whose womb was black.
Seeking aid, we invoke for friendship the bull who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, accompanied by the Maruts.
He who with exultant fury struck Vyaṃsa, he who slew Śambara and the lawless Pipru;
Indra, who overthrew the insatiable Śuṣṇa—
[he is the one] for whom heaven and earth possess great manly power, in whose ordinance Varuṇa and Sūrya abide.
Whose ordinance the rivers follow, Indra’s— He who is the master and lord of horses, the lord of cattle, who is honored and firm in every deed; Indra,
He who is the lord of all that moves and breathes, he who first found the cows for the Brahman;
Indra, who cast down the Dasyus beneath his feet.
He who is to be invoked by the brave and by the timid, who is called upon by those who flee and by those who conquer.
RV_01.101.06.2: Him whom all beings have united toward Indra...
RV_01.101.07.1: By the direction of the Rudras, the far-seeing one goes; with the Rudras, the maiden extends her broad course.
RV_01.101.07.2: The inspired thought honors the renowned Indra...

Whether, O Marut-possessor, you rejoice in the highest dwelling place, or whether you delight in the lowest assembly, come from there toward our sacrifice; desiring you, O you whose gifts are true, we have prepared the oblation.
For you, O Indra, we have pressed the Soma, O most skillful one; desiring you, O you who are borne by prayer, we have prepared the oblation.
Then, O Lord of the teams, together with your troop of Maruts, rejoice upon the sacred grass at this sacrifice.
Rejoice with your bay steeds, O Indra; unbind your jaws and open wide your lips.
Let your bay horses, O fair-jawed one, bring you hither; desiring our offerings, graciously accept them.
We, the guardians of the Marut-praising host, would win booty through Indra. May he grant us that...
I offer this great prayer to you, the Great One; my mind is directed toward his praise and is adorned for him.
The gods have followed with power that Indra, the victorious, in battle and in procreation.
The seven rivers bear his glory; heaven and earth, and the broad world, bear his visible form. For us to behold, O Indra, the sun and moon move in their alternating course for the sake of faith.
O Maghavan, protect that victorious chariot of yours for our gain, which we shall cheer on in the encounter.
O Indra, praised by many, in this battle grant us protection with your mind, O Maghavan, to us who are devoted to you.
May we, with you as our ally, conquer the opposing host; in every fray, raise up our portion.
O Indra, grant us wide space and an easy path; O Maghavan, shatter the manly strength of our enemies.
For these people, competing for wealth and eager for your favor, invoke you from various sides, O Sustainer of riches.
Ascend our chariot for the sake of victory; for your mind, O Indra, is ever intent on triumph.
His arms win cattle; he is the peerless one of boundless power, providing a hundredfold aid in every deed, the stirrer of the fray.
Indra is incomparable in his might; thus do people invoke him when they desire to gain their prize.
O Maghavan, your fame among the peoples has surpassed a hundred, it has surpassed even a thousand. It has exceeded all bounds.
The measureless you, the Dhiṣaṇā has made radiant; thus, O Purandara, you strike down the Vṛtras.
O Lord of men, your counterpart in power is threefold: the three earths and the three luminous realms.
You have grown beyond this entire world; O Indra, by birth you have been without an enemy from of old.
We invoke you first among the gods; you have become the conqueror in battles.
May Indra place this singer of ours, Upamanyu, at the forefront in the impulse of the chariot, as one who breaks through the enemy.
You have won the prize and have not withheld wealth, O Maghavan, in small contests and in great ones alike.
We sharpen you, the fierce one, for protection; therefore, O Indra, impel us in our invocations.
Every day, Indra...
That supreme *indriya* power of yours, the seers maintained in the distance long ago, before this [present world].

One part of this [world] is earthly, another is divine; they are joined together like a banner in battle. He supported the earth and spread it out; having struck with his thunderbolt, he released the waters.
He slew the serpent, he split Rauhiṇa asunder; Maghavan, by his powers, struck down Vyaṃsa.
Bearing his innate strength and full of faith, he advanced, shattering the fortresses of the Dāsas.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, knowing the way, hurl your weapon at the Dasyu; O Indra, increase the Aryan power and the glory.
To him who spoke thus, through these human generations, Maghavan has borne a name worthy of praise.

Approaching for the slaying of the Dasyus, the wielder of the thunderbolt—when indeed the Son assumed his name for the sake of glory—behold now this vast abundance of his; place your faith in the heroic power of Indra. He found the cattle; he found the horses; he found the plants, the waters, and the forests.
For the bull, the showerer of benefits, the performer of mighty deeds, for him whose strength is true, let us press the Soma.
He who, like a hero lying in wait on a path, goes about distributing the wealth of the non-sacrificer as he pleases.
O Indra, you have truly performed that heroic deed when you awakened the sleeping Ahi with your thunderbolt.
The wives and all the gods rejoiced after you as you were exultant; they rejoiced after you.
O Indra, when you struck down Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava, and Vṛtra, and shattered the fortresses of Śambara—do that for us...
An abode has been prepared for you to sit upon, O Indra; sit down there like a neighing steed.
Unharness your birds, unyoke your horses that carry you more swiftly than the wind at evening and at dawn, as you approach the sacrifice.
These men have come to Indra for protection; may he truly come to them this very day from his journeys.
O gods, may you suppress the fury of the Dāsa; may they bring our people to a state of well-being.
He himself casts down the foam of the waters, he himself casts it down, knowing the intent.
Bathed in milk, the two wives of Kuyava have been slain; let them lie in the swift current of the Śiphā.
The kinship of the lower Ayu has perished; the hero prevails and rules by means of his ancient [deeds].
Añjasī, Kuliśī, and Vīrapatnī, swelling with milk, bring forth water with their floods. When that path of the Dasyu was revealed, she went toward the dwelling as one who knows her own home.

And now, O Maghavan, remember us; do not cast us away like a wealth-seeker who has fallen asleep. As such, O Indra, grant us a share in the sun, in the waters, and in sinlessness, that we may have a good report while living.
Do not harm our inner enjoyment; faith has been placed in your great Indra-power.
Now, therefore, I place my trust in you; as a bull, rouse yourself for the sake of great wealth.
O Indra, invoked by many, do not leave us in an unprepared dwelling; give food and drink to those who hunger.
Do not strike us down, O Indra, nor abandon us; do not steal away our beloved enjoyments.
O Maghavan, O Śakra, do not shatter our eggs; do not break our vessels that have grown together from of old.
Come hither; they say you long for Soma—here it is pressed, drink of it for exhilaration.
Widely-capacious, pour it down into your belly; being invoked, hear us like a father.
The moon runs within the waters; the fair-winged bird flies in the sky.
O you whose rims are gold, the lightnings do not find your track; mark this for me, O Heaven and Earth!
Seeking their goal, they indeed go toward their goal; the wife embraces her husband.
They two strike together; having bestowed the virile milk, he milks out the essence. Be aware...
Do not, O God, let that light fall from heaven. May we never be in want of the blissful Soma-offering. Be aware...
I ask about the sacrifice; as the messenger, he shall declare it. Where has the ancient *ṛta* gone? Who maintains it now?
... O you gods who abide in the three luminous realms of heaven!
Where is your *ṛta*, and where is untruth? Where is your ancient oblation?
What is the support of your *ṛta*, and what is the vision of Varuṇa?
How may we, free from malice, pass along the path of the great Aryaman?
I am he who, in the past, used to speak something [of value] when the soma was pressed. Those anxieties pursue me, as a wolf pursues a thirsty deer...
The ribs pain me on all sides, like rival wives.
Like rats gnawing at their own tails, they gnaw at me, your praiser, O Śatakratu.
Those seven rays—there my navel is extended. Trita Āptya knows that; he utters his cry because of kinship.
Those five-eyed ones who stand in the midst of the great heaven— worthy of being proclaimed among the gods— they have turned back together toward the same goal.
These beautiful-winged ones sit in the middle of the ascent of heaven.
They ward off the wolf from the path as it crosses the swift-flowing waters.
This new hymn is worthy of praise and well-proclaimed, O Gods;
the rivers flow according to *ṛta*, and Sūrya has spread the truth far and wide.
O Agni, that which is yours among the gods is worthy of praise and is to be attained through fellowship.
Seated like Manu, as the most wise one, sacrifice to the gods for us.
Seated like Manu, as the most wise Hotṛ-priest, [sacrifice] toward the gods.
Agni, the wise god among the gods, prepares the oblations. ... Varuṇa acts as the priest; we pray to him who knows the way. He uncovers the thought within the heart; may a new truth be born. ...
That path of the Āditya which has been made manifest in heaven— O gods, mortals do not see it, for you cannot overstep it.
Trita, cast down into the well, calls upon the gods for help.
Bṛhaspati heard that, making wide space from the narrow strait.
Indeed, the ruddy wolf once saw me as I was going along my path.
Having perceived it, he rises up like a carpenter working on a back-ache.
Through this hymn of praise, may we, accompanied by Indra and with all our heroes, prevail in the assembly.
May that [favor] be ours...
For protection, we invoke Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, the host of Maruts, and Aditi.

Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you who are bounteous givers, rescue us from every distress. O Ādityas, come hither for our complete well-being; O Gods, be our benefactors in the battles against Vṛtra.
[The chariot...]
May the Pitṛs, worthy of high praise, and the two goddesses, mothers of the gods and increasers of cosmic order (*ṛta*), protect us.
[We invoke] the chariot...
Seeking strength, we pray here with blessings to Narāśaṃsa, the vigorous one, to Pūṣan, who dwells among heroes.
O Bṛhaspati, make for us ever an easy path; we beg for that health and prosperity which was ordained by Manu. [The chariot...
[The chariot...]
The seer Kutsa, having hidden in the pit, called upon Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of power, for aid.
May the divine Aditi protect us with the gods; may the god, the protector, guard us without ceasing.

May that [favor] of yours... The sacrifice approaches the goodwill of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious. May your benevolence turn toward us, for it is the best finder of wide space even out of distress.
May the gods come to us with their protection, being praised by the *sāmans* of the Aṅgirases. May Indra with his powers, the Maruts with the Maruts, and Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Agni, Aryaman, and Savitṛ bestow that upon us, which we recognize.
May that [favor] be ours...
O Indra and Agni, your most wondrous chariot surveys all living beings. Come hither on that, standing together upon the same car; then drink of the pressed soma.

As far as this entire world extends—vast in its breadth and deep in its extent—so much Soma be for you to drink, O Indra and Agni, according to your own desire. For you two have made for yourselves a blessed name that is shared in common; indeed, you two are united as slayers of Vṛtra.

O Indra and Agni, sitting together as the two bulls, rain down the bull-like Soma. When the fires are kindled, having anointed yourselves and spread the sacrificial grass with uplifted ladles, come hither, O Indra and Agni, for our goodwill, having been sprinkled with the potent Somas.
O Indra and Agni, those heroic deeds which you have performed, those forms and powers that you possess—by virtue of those ancient and auspicious friendships of yours, drink of this pressed soma.
When I first spoke to you while choosing, saying: "This soma is to be invoked by us against the Asuras."
Come hither toward that true faith; then drink of the pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you rejoice in your own dwelling, or with a priest, or with a king, O worshipful ones—come hither from there, O bulls; then drink of the pressed soma.

O Indra and Agni, whether you are among the Yuṣus, the Turvaśas, the Druhyus, the Anus, or the Pūrus— come from there [to us]. O Indra and Agni, whether you are in the lowest earth, in the middle earth, or in the highest, come from there [to us].
From there... RV_01.108.10.1{27} O Indra and Agni, whether you are in the highest earth, in the middle one, or even in the lowest; from there...
O Indra and Agni, whether you are stationed in heaven, on earth, among the mountains, in the plants, or in the waters—
from there [come to us].
O Indra and Agni, when the sun has risen, if you two rejoice in your own power in the midst of heaven.
From there...
Thus, O Indra and Agni, having drunk of the pressed juice, win for us all riches.
May that [favor] be ours...

For I have looked with my mind, O Indra and Agni, desiring what is better—whether kinsmen or brothers; no other youthful providence exists for me. Therefore, I have fashioned this hymn for you that seeks the prize.
For I have heard that you two are the greatest givers, whether from a brother-in-law or even from a sister's husband.
Now, as the Soma is being offered, O Indra and Agni, I generate for you two a new hymn of praise.
Praying, "May we not sever the reins," and following the powers of the Fathers, the vigorous ones rejoice in Indra and Agni; for those two are the pressing-stones in the lap of Dhiṣaṇā.
For you two, O Indra and Agni, the divine Dhiṣaṇā presses the Soma for exhilaration with longing.
O Aśvins, you who have auspicious hands and beautiful arms, come hither; mingle [the Soma] with honey in the waters.
O Indra and Agni, I have heard that you two are the most powerful in the distribution of wealth and in the slaying of Vṛtra.
May those two sit upon the sacrificial grass at this sacrifice; O leaders of men, rejoice in the pressed juice!
You surpass all people in the calls to battle, and you exceed both the earth and the heavens in greatness.
You surpass the rivers and the mountains in majesty; O Indra and Agni, you transcend all other beings.
Bring hither, bestow your gifts, O you who wield the thunderbolt in your arms; Indra and Agni, protect us with your powers.
These indeed are the rays of the Sun, by which our fathers attained companionship. O shatterers of forts, wielders of the thunderbolt, bestow your gifts; Indra and Agni, protect us in battles.
RV_01.109.08.2: May that [favor] of ours...
RV_01.110.01.1: My work was stretched out; it is being stretched out again. This most sweet prayer is recited for the sake of praise.
RV_01.110.01.2: This ocean here belongs to all the gods; O *Ṛbhus*, satisfy yourselves with this which has been consecrated with the cry of *svāhā*.
When they came forward desiring enjoyment, some of my kinsmen turned westward while others turned eastward.

O sons of Sudhanvan, you arrived at the house of the liberal Savitṛ by means of the abundance of your journeying. Savitṛ bestowed immortality upon you—that which is unhidden—when you went forth proclaiming your glory.

That very chalice, the vessel for the Asura’s draught, which was but one, you made fourfold. Having performed the labor with skill and swiftness, the worshipers, though being mortals, attained immortality.
The R̥bhus, sons of Sudhanvan, with the eyes of the sun, were united with their sacred thoughts after a year.
Like a field, the Ṛbhus measured out with a measuring-line that single vessel which was gaping open;

they, being praised, seeking the highest, and desiring glory among the immortals, [acted]. With our inspired thought, we offer to the heroes of the mid-air, as if pouring clarified butter with a ladle, through our knowledge.

The *Ṛbhus*, who by their skillful crossing followed the path of this Father, ascended to the realm of heaven for the sake of booty (*vāja*). Like the *Ṛbhu*s, O Indra, you are most new in your power; like the *Ṛbhu*s, you are a giver of wealth through your riches and treasures.
O Gods, through your protection on the day of our beloved [sacrifice], may we overcome the battles waged by those who do not press the Soma.
O Ṛbhus, you fashioned the cow from the hide; you reunited the mother with her calf once more. O sons of Sudhanvan, by your skillful work, you made your aged parents young again.
With your strengths, aid us in the winning of booty; O Indra, accompanied by the Ṛbhus, bestow upon us wondrous wealth.
RV_01.110.09.2{31} Grant us that...
RV_01.111.01.1{32} They fashioned the well-rolling chariot; the skillful workers fashioned the two bay steeds that carry Indra, O you who possess bull-like wealth.
RV_01.111.01.2{32} The Ṛbhus fashioned vital strength for their parents; they fashioned for the calf a mother who stays by its side.

Fashion for our sacrifice a strength endowed with skill; for wisdom and power, fashion food accompanied by noble progeny. So that we may dwell with a clan consisting of all heroes, grant that same vital power to our host.
Fashion for us, O Ṛbhus, the means of success; O heroes, fashion success for the chariot and success for the steed.
May he ever bestow upon us victorious gain, the subduer of both kin and stranger in battles.
I invoke Indra, the lord of the *Ṛbhus*, for our aid; I call the *Ṛbhus*, the *Vājas*, and the Maruts to drink the Soma.
May both Mitra and Varuṇa, and now the Aśvins, urge us toward gain, toward prayer, and toward victory.
May Ṛbhu sharpen our gain for the contest; may Vāja, the winner of the prize, protect us.
May he [grant] this to us...
I invoke Heaven and Earth for the first thought, Agni, the Gharma, and the radiant one, for the sacrifice upon the journey.
With those aids wherewith you quickened Kāra for Aṃśa in battle—come hither with those very succors, O Aśvins.

For your gift, the well-borne, unfailing [sacrificers] have mounted the chariot, as if to deliberate upon a word. With those aids wherewith you favor prayers for the successful completion of the rite—[with those come hither].
By your power, you two rule over those divine clans under the command of immortality.
O heroes, with those [powers] by which you cause the barren cow to swell with milk—[with them...
By those [powers] by which Parijman, through the might of his offspring, the son of two mothers, hastens across the waters and displays his splendor.
With those [powers] by which Trimantu became far-sighted, with those...
With those by which you raised up Rebha, who was confined and bound within the waters, and Vandana, so that he might behold the sun;
With those by which you protected Kaṇva as he strove for gain—with those [powers]...
With those [helps] by which you quickened Antaka as he was wasting away in battle, and with those unerring aids by which you revived Bhujyu;
with those by which you quickened Karkandhu and Vayya—[with those come hither].
With those [helps] by which you granted to Atri the pure Śucanti, the winner of wealth, the one worthy of fair praise, and the heated *gharma* offering that is full of sweetness.
With those aids by which you protected Pṛṣnigu and Purukutsa—with those [aids]...
With those powers, O bulls, by which you made Parāvṛj whole, and gave sight to the blind and the lame so that he might walk—with those [powers]...
With those [powers] by which you released the swallowed Vartikā—with those [powers]...

With those [powers] by which you made the Sindhu river full of honey, and with which you, O undecaying ones, quickened Vasiṣṭha; With those by which you protected Kutsa, Śrutarī, and Narya—with those [powers, come to us].
With those by which you quickened Viśpalā, the winner of wealth, and Atharvan’s daughter, when she had been seized as a thousandfold prize in the race.
With those [helps] by which you protected Vaśa Aśvya and Preṇi—with those [helps]...
With those by which, O bounteous ones, the cask flowed with honey for the merchant Dīrghaśravas, the son of Uśij;
with those by which you protected Kakṣīvat the praiser—with those [helps]...
With those [powers] by which you caused the Rasā river to swell with its flood of water; with which you aided the horseless chariot for victory;
with which Triśoka drove forth the cows—by those [powers, O Aśvins, come hither].
With those [powers] by which you encompassed the sun in the distance; with which you aided Mandhātṛ in his contests for the lordship of lands.
With those [aids] by which you protected the sage Vāja when he was being carried away— [with those, O Aśvins...
With those by which you protected the great Atithigva Kaśoju, Divodāsa, in the slaying of Śambara—
With those by which you protected Trasadasyu at the breaking of the forts— [with those, O Aśvins...]
With those [helps] by which you honored Vamra when he was drinking deeply and receiving praise, and with which you favored Kali who had won a wife;
with those by which you protected Vyaśva and Pṛthi—[with those come to us].
With those [helps] by which, O heroes, you sought a path for Śayu and for Atri, and with which in ancient times you found a way for Manu.
With those [powers] by which you made Śārīra silver for Syūmaraśmi—with those [powers]...
With those [powers] by which Paṭharvā, through the greatness of his belly, shone like Agni when piled and kindled on his course—with those [powers]...
With those [powers] by which you protected Śaryāta in the great contest for wealth—with those [powers]...
With those [powers] by which, O Aṅgiras, you two went forth in spirit and reached the forefront of the flood of cattle in the opening;
with those by which you protected the heroic Manu with nourishment—with those [powers]...
With those by which you brought the wives to Vimada, or those by which you bestowed the ruddy cows—those [powers]...
With those [powers] by which you brought divine favor to Sudās, with those...
With those by which you become sources of peace for the donor, with which you protect Bhujyu, and with which you protect Adhrigu;
With those [powers] that are full of grace, well-bearing, and praising the *ṛta*, with those...

With those aids wherewith you honored Kṛśānu on his seat, and wherewith you helped the young man’s steed in its speed; with those wherewith you bring the dear honey for the seekers—[with those aids come hither].
With those aids wherewith you quicken the hero who fights for cattle in the conquest of men, and in the winning of land and offspring—[with those aids come hither].
With those aids by which you protected the chariots and by which you protected the horses—with those [aids]...
With those aids by which you, O Śatakratus, protected Kutsa, the son of Arjuni, and Turvīti and Dabhīti—with those [aids]...
With those aids by which you protected Dhvasanti and Puruṣanti—with those [aids]...

O Aśvins, make our speech effective; O wonder-workers, bulls, grant us inspired thought. In this non-gambling [contest], I invoke you for protection; be with us for our increase in the winning of the prize.
O Aśvins, protect us day and night with unimpaired blessings of good fortune.
May that [grant] us...
This most excellent light among lights has come; the brilliant, far-reaching sign has been born.
Just as she was impelled by the impulse of Savitṛ, so has Night yielded her womb to Dawn.
Bright with her white calf, the radiant one has come; the black one has entered her dwellings. Of common kinship, immortal, following one another, the two heavens move along, changing their colors.
Common is the path of the two sisters, endless; instructed by the gods, they travel it, each by her own way.
They do not clash, nor do they stand still; well-established, Night and Dawn, of different forms yet one in mind, move together.
The radiant leader of true blessings has been perceived; wonderful, she has thrown open the doors for us.
Stretching forth the world, she has revealed our wealth; Dawn has awakened all living beings.
O Bountiful One, you are for the crooked-eyed one to move about, for enjoyment, for sacrifice, and for wealth;
O Uṣas, you are for those who see even a little to look out over the wide expanse.
You are for dominion, you are for glory, you are for greatness, you are for sacrifice, and you are for the attainment of purpose.
The Dawns, whose appearances are diverse, have looked upon our lives...
This daughter of heaven has appeared, shining forth, a young woman clothed in radiant raiment. Ruling over all earthly wealth, O auspicious Dawn, shine here today!
She follows the path of those who have departed, the first of the endless mornings yet to come.
Dawn, shining forth, stirs the living, though she awakens no one who is dead. O Dawn, you have caused the fire to be kindled; you have revealed all things with the eye of the sun.
That you have awakened the men who were about to sacrifice—that you have performed a glorious service for the gods.
How great is the distance between those dawns that have already shone, those that are now shining, and those yet to shine?
Yearning after the former ones, she gazes longingly and goes gladly with the others.
Those mortals who beheld the earlier dawns as they broke forth have passed away;
now she has become visible to us, and those who shall behold her in future ages are yet to come.
Driving away hatred, guardian of Truth, born of Truth, the bringer of bliss, she stirs up the joyous song of praise.
Bringing auspicious blessings and the feast for the gods, may the most excellent Dawn shine forth here today.
Again and again the goddess has shone forth from of old; and so today, the wealthy one, she has shone upon this place.
And so she shall shine through the days to come; ageless and immortal, she moves by her own inherent powers.

With her bright ornaments she has shone across the expanse of heaven; the goddess has cast off the black mantle of night. Awakening all with her ruddy horses, Dawn approaches on her well-yoked chariot.
Bringing nourishing and desirable boons, she displays her wondrous banner as she shines forth.
The first of the many dawns that have passed away has shone forth.
Arise! The breath of life has come to us; darkness has departed and light approaches.
She has cleared the path for Sūrya to travel; we have arrived where they prolong their span of life.
With the shuttle of speech, the singer, being praised, raises up the shining Dawns.
O bounteous ones, shine forth today upon the one who sings your praises; bestow upon us a life-span rich in progeny.
Those Dawns that shine forth for the mortal worshipper, bringing cattle and all-heroic strength—may they dawn upon us.
Like the outburst of the winds, may the presser of Soma obtain those gifts of truth that bestow horses.
Mother of the gods, face of Aditi, banner of sacrifice, shine forth as the great one!
Arising, bring us praise for our prayer; O possessor of all boons, give birth to us among the people.
Whatever wonderful wealth the Dawns bring as auspicious for the one who has performed the rite and exerts himself—
that, may it come to us... These hymns we offer forth to the powerful Rudra, the one with matted hair, the ruler of heroes.

So that it may rest well for bipeds and quadrupeds, so that everything in this village may be nourished and free from disease—be gracious to us, O Rudra, and grant us joy; we shall worship you, the lord of heroes, with homage. Whatever health and prosperity our father Manu won through sacrifice, may we attain that under your guidance, O Rudra.
May we obtain your favor through sacrifice to the gods, O bounteous Rudra, ruler of heroes.
Approaching us with goodwill, come to our people; with our heroes unharmed, let us offer the oblation to you.
We invoke for protection the brilliant Rudra, the fulfiller of the sacrifice, the swift and wise one.
May the divine wrath be cast far away from us; we choose for ourselves his goodwill.

We invoke with reverence the ruddy boar of heaven, the one with braided hair, the brilliant form. Holding in his hand the most excellent medicines, may he grant us protection, armor, and a secure shelter.

This speech is spoken for the father of the Maruts, sweeter than the sweet, a strengthening for Rudra. And grant us, O Immortal One, that which is the food of mortals; [grant it] for ourselves and for our offspring.
Do not [strike down] our great one, nor our small one; do not [strike down] our growing one, nor our grown one.
Do not slay our father, nor our mother; O Rudra, do not harm our dear bodies.
Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our life, nor in our cattle, nor in our horses.
O Rudra, do not slay our heroes in your wrath; bearing oblations, we ever invoke you.
Like a herdsman, I have brought these hymns of praise near to you; O Father of the Maruts, grant us your favor.
For your benevolence is auspicious and most compassionate; therefore, we choose only your protection.
Keep far from us your bolt that slays cattle and men, O Lord of Heroes; let your favor abide with us.
Be gracious to us and speak for us, O God; then, you of vast power, grant us protection.
Seeking your aid, we have uttered our homage to him; may Rudra, accompanied by the Maruts, hear our call. May he [grant] this to us...
The brilliant array of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya, the soul of all that moves and stands, has filled the heavens, the earth, and the mid-air.
Like a youth approaching a maiden, Sūrya comes toward the radiant goddess Uṣas from behind.
Where god-seeking men extend the ages for the sake of auspiciousness upon the auspicious one.
Auspicious are the bay horses of Sūrya, bright, dappled, worthy of praise;
paying homage, they have mounted the back of heaven and traverse heaven and earth in an instant.

That is the divinity of Sūrya, that is his greatness: in the midst of his work, he withdraws what was spread out. When he has unyoked his bay horses from their station, Night spreads her garment over all this. That form of Mitra and Varuṇa, Sūrya assumes for the sake of being beheld in the lap of heaven.
One part of his power is infinite and bright; the other, dark, the green-hued ones bring together.
O gods, at the rising of the sun today, deliver us from distress and from the man’s way of sin.
Grant us that...
To the Nāsatyas I offer up my hymns like sacred grass; I release them as the wind drives the clouds.
You two, with your swift chariot, brought a wife to Vimada, who was seeking fortune, by means of your rapid vehicle.
Or, boasting with your firm-winged, swift-gliding steeds, or through the incitements of the gods, you have come.
O Nāsatyas, that donkey won a thousand [cows] in the contest of Yama’s prize. Tugra, indeed, O Aśvins, when the clouds were withheld, was carried away like wealth by no one who had died;
you carried him away with self-propelled ships that glide through the mid-air and exclude the waters.

O Nāsatyas, with winged steeds that traverse three nights and three days, you carried away Bhujyu across the ocean, on the dry land and at the edge of the wet. With three chariots, hundred-footed and drawn by six horses,
you performed that heroic deed in the ocean, which offers no support, no standing place, and no hold.
O Aśvins, when you carried Bhujyu home, who had boarded a ship with a hundred oars;
When you gave a white horse to Aghāśva as a perpetual blessing— That gift of yours was great and worthy of praise: the horse of Pedu, the swift steed, who is to be invoked even by the noble foe.
O Heroes, you bestowed abundant wisdom upon Kakṣīvat, the son of Pajra, who praises you.
From the hoof of the stallion horse at the *kārotara* press, you poured out a hundred jars of *surā*. With snow you warded off the burning heat of the fire; you provided him with nourishing strength.
O Aśvins, you brought forth Atri, who had been cast into the pit, together with all his followers, in safety.
O Nāsatyas, you raised him up from afar; you turned the well upside down and made its opening upward.
Thus the waters flowed for the sake of Gotama’s thirst, like a stream for the sake of wealth and for a thousand thirsty ones.
O Nāsatyas, you released the aged Cyavāna from his confinement, like a garment, as he grew old.
O Dāsras, you prolonged the life of the abandoned man and made him the husband of young maidens.
That deed of yours, O Heroes, Nāsatyas, is worthy of praise, successful, and a protective shelter for those who seek your aid.

When you two, as knowers, brought forth from the visible [place] that which was hidden like a treasure for Vanda— that mighty deed of yours, O heroes, I bring to light for the sake of gain, like the roar of thunder bringing rain. For Dadhyanc, the son of Atharvan, declared this honeyed secret to you both by means of the horse’s head.
O Nāsatyas, the far-sighted Purandhi invoked you both with her hands for the great journey;
O Aśvins, you heard that call like the Āsurī Vadhrimatī and gave her a golden-handed son. O heroes, O Nāsatyas, you released the quail from the jaws of the wolf in the encounter.
And you two, O lords of many blessings, made the lamenting seer capable of seeing clearly.
For in the decisive struggle, like the wing of a bird that has been cut off, Viśpalā’s leg was severed in the fray for Khela’s sake.
Immediately, you two restored an iron shank to Viśpalā so that she might run when the prize was set.
To the wolf he gave a hundred rams; his father made Ṛjrāśva blind.
To him, O Nāsatyas, you two physicians, O wonder-workers, bestowed eyes that see clearly, O lords of the forest.
The daughter of Sūrya mounted your chariot, as if upon a plowshare, winning it with her swift course.

All the gods approved with their hearts; you, O Nāsatyas, are united with glory. When you went on your circuit for Divodāsa, O Aśvins, speeding for Bharadvāja, your accompanying chariot brought wealth; a bull and a porpoise were yoked to it.
O Nāsatyas, bringing wealth with good dominion, noble offspring, long life, and heroic strength,
you came together with vigor to the daughter of Jahnu, who offered you your portion three times a day.
You carried Jāhuṣa, who was besieged on all sides, through the dust by easy paths during the night.
O Nāsatyas, with your piercing chariot, you two who do not grow old, you went through the mountains.
On one morning, O Aśvins, you protected Vaśa for battle so that he might win thousands.
Aided by Indra, O powerful ones, you drove away misfortune and the hostilities of Pṛthuśravas.
From the very low place you raised the waters for Śara Ārcatka to drink;
indeed, O Nāsatyas, by your powers, you made the barren cow swell with milk for the exhausted Śayu.
To the seeker of aid, the praising, the upright Kṛṣṇiya, O Nāsatyas, you granted [his wish] through your powers.
Like a lost animal, you restored Viṣṇāpū to the sight of Viśvaka. For ten nights and nine days he had been bound and pierced within the waters;
Rebha, who was submerged and cast away in the flood, you brought forth like Soma with a ladle.
I have proclaimed your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins; may I be the lord of this [wealth], possessing good cattle and noble sons.
And beholding and attaining long life, may I reach old age as if returning home.
O Aśvins, the ancient Hotar-priest invites you both for the exhilaration of the sweet Soma.
The gift is spread upon the sacred grass; O Nāsatyas, come hither with your songs and with strengths.

O Aśvins, that chariot of yours, swifter than thought, drawn by noble horses, which visits the people— with that chariot by which you go to the dwelling of the doer of good deeds, come, O Heroes, to our abode.
O Heroes, with your host you released the seer Atri, who belongs to the five peoples, from the narrow pit of distress.
O Bulls, you destroyed the magic powers of the malevolent Dasyu, driving him away in succession.
O Aśvins, O Heroes, O Bulls, you rescued the seer Rebha, who was hidden like a horse by the evil-doers, within the waters.
You two restored him who was shattered by your wondrous deeds; your ancient exploits do not grow old.
Like one fallen into the lap of Destruction, or like the sun dwelling in darkness, O wonder-workers—like a beautiful golden ornament buried for splendor—you two, O Aśvins, raised up Vandana.

O Nāsatyas, O Heroes, that deed of yours is worthy of praise by Kakṣīvat, the son of Pajra, as you traveled around: from the hoof of a swift horse, for the sake of the people, you poured out a hundred jars of honey.
O Heroes, you gave Viṣṇāpū back to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, who praised you.
To Ghoṣā, who dwelt among her ancestors in her own home and was growing old, O Aśvins, you gave a husband.
You gave a bright wife to Śyāva, the son of Kaṇva, of the great clan, O Aśvins.
That deed of yours, O mighty ones, is worthy of proclamation: that you bestowed glory upon the descendant of Nṛṣad.
O Aśvins, assuming many forms, you brought to Pedu a swift horse—a winner of thousands, a prize-winning steed, irresistible, a slayer of serpents, glorious, and a conqueror.
O bounteous givers, these are your glorious deeds; this is the prayer, the hymn of praise, and the dwelling place between the two worlds.
O Aśvins, when the Pajras call upon you, come with nourishment and grant strength to the wise man.
O Aśvins, being praised according to the measure of the son, you who are swift, bestow strength upon the inspired singer;
having grown great through the prayer of Agastya, O Nāsatyas, you restored Viśpalā.
Where were you two going when you found the excellent praise of Kāvya, O sons of Heaven, O bulls, in his dwelling?
On the tenth day, O Aśvins, you dug him out like a buried vessel of gold.
O Aśvins, by your wondrous powers, you made Cyavāna, who was growing old, young again.
The daughter of Sūrya chose your chariot, O Nāsatyas, together with glorious splendor.
You two, O youthful ones, became mindful again for Tugra by means of your ancient ways. You carried Bhujyu out from the ocean, from the midst of the waters, with your swift, reddish-brown horses.
The son of Tugra invoked you, O Aśvins, having been cast into the sea and traveling without wavering. You two, O Bulls, carried him out safely on your well-yoked chariot, swift as thought.
The quail invoked you, O Aśvins, when you released her from the mouth of the wolf.
With victory, you two traversed the ridges of the mountain; you slew Viṣvāc with poison at his very birth.

To him who offered a hundred rams to the she-wolf, and was led away into darkness by his malevolent father— O Aśvins, you restored sight to the son of R̥jrāśva; you created light for the blind man so that he might see.
"Success! To the blind man you brought a burden, O Aśvins, bulls among men, saying, 'Come, O Vṛkī!
Like a youthful lover who carves up his prey, Ṛjrāśva [offered] one hundred and one rams. Great is your aid, O Aśvins, bringing bliss; indeed, O wise ones, you heal even the cripple."
Then Purandhi invoked you; O bulls, come to her with your aids.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, you made the barren cow swell with milk for Śayu, though she was dried up and parched.
By your powers, you brought back the wife for Vimada—you led forth the young woman of Purumitra.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, you plow barley with the wolf, milking nourishment for mankind;
with the *bakura* [reed], you blew away the Dasyu and created wide light for the Ārya.
O Aśvins, for Dadhyac the son of Atharvan, you restored the horse’s head.
He, observing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), proclaimed the honeyed [soma] to you two, O wonder-workers (*dasrau*), that which belongs to Tvaṣṭṛ and is hidden in your girth-bands.
O sages (*kavī*), I have always desired your favor; O Aśvins, further all my prayers.
O Nāsatyas, bestow upon us great wealth that brings progeny and is worthy of renown.
O Aśvins, bestowing gifts, you gave a golden-handed son to Vadhrimatī, O heroes.
O Aśvins, givers of good gifts, you raised up the three-severed Śyāva from his mangled state.
O Aśvins, men have proclaimed these ancient heroic deeds of yours.
Performing sacred prayer for you two, O Bulls, may we, possessing brave sons, speak at the assembly.
O Aśvins, let your chariot, flying like a falcon, most gracious and well-provided, come hither—
your chariot which is swifter than the mind of a mortal, three-seated, O Bulls, and fleet as the wind.
Come hither on your well-rolling, three-wheeled chariot, with its triple seat and triple framework;
O Aśvins, swell our cows, quicken our steeds, and increase our heroic strength.
With your well-rolling chariot that travels through the air, O wonder-workers, hear this hymn of praise from the Adra.
O Aśvins, why do the ancient sages say that you are the ones most swift to return?
O Aśvins, let the falcons, yoked to your chariot, swift-flying birds, bring you hither—
those who cross the waters like divine eagles, carrying you, O Nāsatyas, toward the offerings.
May the youthful daughter of Sūrya mount your chariot here, O heroes, having found it pleasing. May your beautiful, winged, red horses carry you around at the encounter.
By your wondrous deeds, O wonder-workers, you raised up Vandana; by your powers, O mighty ones, you raised up Rebha.
You brought Tugrya safely across the ocean; you restored Cyavāna to youth once more.
O Aśvins, you bestowed nourishment and protection upon Atri when he was cast down into the heat.
Delighting in his beautiful hymn of praise, you restored sight to Kaṇva when he was blinded.
O Aśvins, you caused the cow to swell for Śayu who was in distress, for his ancient sake.
You released the quail from calamity; you restored the leg to Viśpalā.
O Aśvins, you gave the white horse, impelled by Indra, to Pedu for the slaying of the dragon.

To the one who is to be invoked repeatedly, the conqueror of enemies, the fierce, the winner of thousands, the bull with firm limbs— to you two, O heroes, well-born Aśvins, we call for protection as we cry out in need.
Come to us on your chariot laden with wealth, enjoying our songs of praise, for our well-being.
Come to us with the fresh swiftness of a hawk, O Nāsatyas, being of one mind;

for I, having offered oblations, call upon you both at the dawning of every most recent dawn, O Aśvins. I invoke your wondrous, mind-swift chariot, drawn by vigorous horses and worthy of sacrifice, so that we may live.
Toward him who has a thousand banners, the forest-dweller, the possessor of a hundred riches, the prompt listener, the bestower of wide space, toward him [I go] for the sake of enjoyment.
His upright prayer has been established at his departure upon the sacrificial grass; the quarters of the sky come together.
I sweeten the hot offering; the protections approach; the nourishing *ūrjānī* has mounted your chariot, O Aśvins.
When they have come together, vying with one another for glory— those vigorous, immeasurable,
and swift ones in the fray— your chariot, O Aśvins, is seen on the slope when you bring the patron a boon.
You two went to Bhujyu as he was struggling, carrying him back by means of your self-yoked birds to his ancestors.

O powerful ones, you have gone to the dwelling that is to be won; for Divodāsa, your great favor has been manifest. O Aśvins, two voices have guided your wondrous, self-yoked chariot toward its strength. Having come to you for friendship, the noble maiden chose you as her husbands, she who possesses the power of flight.
You rescued Rebha from his confinement; for Atri, you quenched the burning heat with cold.
You caused the cow of Śayu to swell with milk; Vandana was prolonged in his long life.
O wonder-workers (dasrā), you restored Vandana, who was seized by old age, as a craftsman repairs a chariot.

From the field you have brought forth the sage through your wondrous power; let your marvelous deed be manifest here for the one who honors you. You two went to him who was lamenting in the distance, oppressed by the abandonment of his own father.
Truly, your aids were full of light; your brilliant assistances were present in the encounter.
And for you two, the honey-bee hums a sweet song; in the exhilaration of Soma, the son of Uśij calls upon you.
You won over the mind of Dadhyañc, and then the horse’s head spoke to you both.
O Aśvins, you bestowed upon Pedu the white steed, the fulfiller of many desires and the conqueror of enemies.
With arrows, [he strikes] the one who shines upon the sky, invincible in battles, worthy of praise, like Indra, the subduer of peoples.
What offering will satisfy you, O Aśvins? Who is pleasing to both of you? How can the one lacking wisdom worship you?
The wise one may ask the two knowers at the doors; thus another is ignorant and lacks understanding.
Indeed, there is none among mortals who is not subject to decay.
Therefore, we invoke you two as the knowers; as such, O knowers, declare our prayer to us today.
The youthful one, feeling compassion, has raised his voice toward you both.
Out of simple-mindedness, I question the gods regarding the wondrous oblation consecrated with the *vaṣaṭ* call, O wonder-workers:
protect us from the stronger foe and guard us from the more impetuous.
The speech which shone forth like [the song] of Ghoṣa Bhr̥gavāṇa— the very speech with which the son of Pajra worships you both—
[that speech] has been sent forth by the one who knows,
like a messenger. O Aśvins, I have indeed sung this Gāyatra hymn of Takavāna for you both.
O Lords of Splendor, look upon us with your eyes;
for you two were present at the great [sacrifice], whether you have extended it or have withdrawn it.
As such, O Vasus, be our good protectors; guard us from the wolf, from the one who intends evil.
Do not deliver us over to any enemy; let not our milch-cows stray from our homes anywhere.
Let them yield their udders for you, O youthful ones, even though they have no calves, so that we may form a bond of friendship with you. And measure out for us wealth consisting of booty.
Measure out for us nourishment consisting of milch-cows;
[measure out] the chariot of the Aśvins, which is without horses yet possesses swift steeds. Through that, I have great delight.
May this chariot, which brings happiness at the Soma-drinking, carry me along with the people. Now, enough of the sight of sleep and of the wealthy man who does not enjoy his riches!
Both of them reach us swiftly.

How indeed has he, the vessel of those devoted to the gods, heard the songs of the Aṅgirases, hastening forward? When he has come to the people of the house, the worshipful one strides widely at the sacrifice.
He propped up the sky and sprinkled the foundation; as a *ṛbhu*, he created wealth for the prize-winning hero from the cow.
The buffalo beheld his own kindred host; he looked upon the mate of the horse, the mother of the cow.
The ruddy one reached the ancient dwelling, the sovereign lord of the tribes, swift through the days of the Aṅgirases.
He fashioned the thunderbolt and harnessed his team; he propped up the sky for the four-footed and the two-footed man.

In his exhilaration, he gave the resounding host of the sun-beams to the one who upholds the cosmic order (*ṛta*), when, at the onset, he turned back the triple-peaked mountain and threw open the doors of the human oppressors.
For you [is that milk] which the two parents brought, a gift of excellent seed, they who hasten and stir;
that pure heritage of yours which they offered as the milk of the ever-yielding cow.
And now he has been born, the one who carries us across; may he exhilarate us, like the sun at the dawning of this light.
The moon-like Soma, by whom the one who offers sweat as oblation has reached his stations, pouring with the ladle into the vessels;

when the wood-pile, well-fueled, performs its work at the sacrifice, the hero [Soma] is encompassed within the enclosure of the cow. When you shine forth through the days for the sake of the decisive ones, you bring wealth to the non-impetuous man who seeks cattle.

From the great eight [quarters] of heaven, bring hither the two bay steeds, the subduers of splendor, for the sake of battle. When they have pressed with stones the exhilarating, tawny juice for your increase— the juice that is mixed with milk and is stirred by the wind—
then you, the skillful one, turned back the iron stone brought down from heaven by the cow.
RV 1.121.9: When, O much-invoked one, you were winning for Kutsa, you encompassed Śuṣṇa with endless weapons of death.

RV 1.121.10: Before the sun was swallowed by darkness, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you cast his weapon, Phaliga, away; even that power of Śuṣṇa which was arrayed around him, well-fastened as it was, you took from heaven.
The two great wheelless expanses, heaven and earth, rejoiced in your deed, O Indra.
With your mighty thunderbolt, you sent Vṛtra—the one who lay upon the rivers—to sleep, the one with the broad jaw.
O Indra, mount the manly, swift steeds that are well-yoked and most effective carriers of the wind; mount them, O hero, for the sake of men.

The exhilarating Vajra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the one that carries us across, which Kāvya Uśanas fashioned for you— With it, O Indra, you made the bay horses of Sūrya rest for the sake of men; Etaśa brought back the wheel.
You cast the godless ones into the abyss beyond the ninety navigable rivers.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us from this malevolent assault and from misfortune in the encounter.
Bestow upon us riches borne on chariots, with horses as their foremost prize, for our sustenance, glory, and abundance.
May that benevolence of yours never fail us; O you who are great through strength, may the sacrificial offerings encompass us.
O Maghavan, grant us a share of the wealth in cattle; may we be your most liberal companions at the feast.
O you of swift thought, bring forward the pressed juice for your drink; offer the oblation to the bounteous Rudra.
I have praised the heroes of the divine Asura with the sons of Heaven—the Maruts—desiring their favor from both worlds.
Like two wives eager for the first invocation, Dawn and Night, appearing in many forms, have increased [our strength].
Like a barren woman wearing a loosened garment, she is beautiful to behold with the golden splendors of the Sun.
May the wanderer who strikes at dawn delight us; may the wind, the bull of the waters, delight us.
O Indra and Parvata, sharpen us; may all the gods grant us wide space.
And those two glorious ones, who hasten to the bright dawn, the sons of Uśij call upon them for protection.
Bring forward the offspring of the waters; bring forward the two parents of the yearning Āyu.
The descendant of Uśij calls upon your roaring one, as Ghoṣā did in the winning of the prize for Arjuna’s praise.
May I proclaim to you the abundance of wealth belonging to Pūṣan and Agni at the place of giving.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, hear my invocation; hear it also from every side in this assembly.
May the listener, the giver who hears us well, the one with good ears, and the Sindhu with its waters grant us fair fields.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, that gift of yours is praised—a hundred cattle bestowed upon the Pajras at the *pṛkṣayāma* festivals.
Bestowing wealth upon Śrutaratha and Priyaratha, they have come, instantly securing full prosperity.
I praise the bounty of this one whose wealth is great; may we, together with brave sons, win the favor of Nahuṣa.
He who is a patron for the Pajras, possessing strength, a lord of horses and chariots for me—he is a true patron.
That person who, seeking to harm you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, presses the Soma for you with guile, like one who seeks to steal water—may he be struck down by his own crookedness.
May he himself lay the consumption deep within his heart, since the upholder of *ṛta* has come with our oblations.

Impelled by wondrous deeds, the mighty son of Nahuṣa, the subduer of hosts, whose fame is celebrated among men— He who bestows gifts proceeds with rapid strides; the hero is ever victorious in all battles.
Now come to the call of Nahuṣa, the patron; hear us, O kings of immortality, you who are delightful.

When the gift of Nabhojū, the protector, is bestowed for the sake of praise upon the one with the great chariot, they have said: "Come to this host, the support of that patron, at the distribution of the tenfold wealth."
In whom the splendors and the granting of wealth delight—may they all win booty in the contests. We rejoice in the tenfold nourishment, when those who bear the fivefold foods come twice.
What is it that these men, masters of good horses and good reins, strive for as they urge on their rivals?

May all the gods grant us wide space—[the god] with golden ears and jeweled neck—who has come swiftly to the songs of the noble one; may both [the gods and the dawns] take pleasure in our offerings. Four sons of Maśarśāra, three of King Āyavasa, the victorious, [have honored me].
Your chariot, O Mitra and Varuṇa, has long-reaching reins and well-extended poles; it has shone like the sun.
The broad chariot of Dakṣiṇā has been yoked; the immortal gods have mounted it.
From the darkness has arisen the noble, far-extending one, discerning for the dwelling of mankind.
She has awakened before all the world, the Great One, winning booty and bestowing gain. The young woman, born again, has looked out from on high; Dawn has come first at the morning invocation.
O well-born goddess Dawn, whatever portion you shall distribute today among men and mortals.
May the divine Savitṛ, the friend of the home, proclaim us sinless here before Sūrya.
Day after day she goes toward every house, bestowing her names upon them. Seeking to win, the radiant one has come repeatedly; she enjoys the very best of riches.
Sister of Bhaga, kinswoman of Varuṇa, O Dawn, you who are full of joy, be the first to be awakened.
May he who is the establisher of evil be left behind; may we conquer him with the chariot of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Let the true words rise up, let the inspired thoughts rise up; the brightly shining fires have ascended.

The radiant Dawns, shining forth, reveal desirable treasures that were hidden by darkness. One part departs and another arrives; the two days of diverse forms move in succession. One conceals the darkness within the dwelling, while Uṣas shines forth on her brilliantly glowing chariot.
Similar today, similar indeed tomorrow, they follow the long-lasting ordinance of Varuṇa.
Blameless, each one traverses thirty leagues in a single day, according to his will.
Knowing the name of the first day, the bright and white one has been born from the black.
The maiden of *ṛta* does not violate the ordinances, coming day after day to the appointed place. Like a maiden displaying her body, O Goddess, you go toward the god who desires to worship.
Smiling, the young woman, shining brightly, reveals her breasts before us.
Like a woman beautifully adorned and groomed by her mother, you make your body visible for all to see.
O Auspicious Dawn, shine forth even more widely; no other Dawns have attained what you possess.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, and possessing all desirable things, you strive in harmony with the rays of the Sun.
They go away and they come back again, the Dawns bearing auspicious names.
Following the rein of *ṛta*, bestow upon us every kind of auspicious resolve.
O Uṣas, easy to invoke, shine forth for us today; may riches be with us and with our patrons.
As the Dawn shines forth while the fire is kindled, and as the Sun rises, he has spread his light far and wide.
Here, may the divine Savitṛ impel our two-footed and four-footed creatures toward their goals for the sake of the Goddess Earth.
Unfailing in her divine ordinances, she diminishes the human generations.
The first of the eternal dawns that have passed away has shone forth, the foremost of those yet to come.
This daughter of Heaven has appeared, clothing herself in light, always in the same manner toward the east.
She follows the path of *ṛta* perfectly; like one who knows her way, she does not confuse the directions.
She has appeared like the breast of a bright woman; like Nodhas, she has revealed her dear delights.

Like one who awakens those lying at the feast, she has come again as the most constant of those who return. On the eastern side of the unattainable realm, the mother of the cows has raised her banner.
She spreads herself out further and wider, filling both the laps of her parents. Thus she is most manifold to behold; she avoids neither the stranger nor the kinsman.
Displaying herself with a stainless body, she does not shrink from the small nor from the great as she shines forth.
Like a brotherless maiden, she goes forth toward men; like one ascending the chariot-seat for the winning of riches, Dawn approaches.
Like a loving, well-dressed bride for her husband, Dawn bares her breast like a smiling woman.
The sister yields her place to the elder sister; she departs from her, as if to look back upon her.
Shining forth with the rays of the sun, she anoints herself like women going to a gathering.
Of these sisters, the later one follows after the earlier as it has departed. May those Dawns, newer than the ancient ones, shine upon us now with wealth and auspicious days.
Awaken, O wealthy Dawn, those who bestow gifts; let the stingy misers sleep on, never waking.
Shine forth with riches for the generous patrons, O wealthy one; shine forth with wealth for the singer, O bountiful one, as you bring the day to light.
This young woman has been seen from the east; she yokes her team of ruddy cows.

Now indeed the light shall break forth; Agni shall take his station in every house. Even the birds have flown up from their nests, and the men who partake of food [arise] at the breaking of dawn. O Goddess Dawn, you bring much wealth to the mortal who dwells at home and offers oblations.

You have been praised with my prayer, O you who are worthy of praise; you, the longing Dawns, have increased our wealth. Through your divine protection, O goddesses, may we win booty consisting of hundreds and thousands.
The early traveler bestows treasure at dawn; he who is wise accepts it and takes possession of it.

By that [gift], increasing his progeny and his life, he, possessed of good heroes, partakes in the increase of wealth. May he be well-provided with cattle, well-endowed with gold, and well-served by horses; to him Indra bestows great vital strength— to him who, O *prātaritvan*, as you approach, releases you with wealth like one untying a tethered animal.
Today at dawn we seek the well-performed deed; may he come with his wealth-bearing chariot, the son of *iṣṭi*.
Make him drink the pressed juice of the exhilarating *aṃśu* plant; increase the hero who dwells among men with our truthful hymns.
The rivers flow toward us, bringing refreshment; like milch-cows, they approach the one who has sacrificed and the one who is about to sacrifice.
Seeking glory, streams of clarified butter flow from every side toward him who bestows gifts and fulfills them.

Resting upon the ridge of the firmament, he who bestows gifts indeed goes among the gods. For him the waters and the rivers flow with clarified butter; for him this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) ever overflows.

For those who give sacrificial gifts, these wondrous things belong; for those who give sacrificial gifts, the suns are in heaven. Those who give sacrificial gifts partake of immortality; those who give sacrificial gifts prolong their life.
May the liberal givers not fall into sin or distress; may the wise patrons, firm in their vows, never suffer decay.
Let there be some other enclosure for them; let sorrows fall upon the one who does not give.
With inspired thought, I offer these unflagging hymns of praise for Bhāvya, who dwells by the river. He, the unconquered king, seeking glory, measured out a thousand libations for me.
A hundred gold coins from the king who entreated me, and a hundred horses presented at once—I have accepted them.
Kakṣīvat has received a hundred cattle from the lord; he has extended his undecaying fame to heaven.
Ten chariots, drawn by dark bay horses and accompanied by brides, given by Svanaya, have come to me.
Sixty thousand followed after the cattle; Kakṣīvat won them at the close of days.
Forty bay steeds of Daśaratha lead the line at the head of a thousand. The Kakṣīvats and the Pajras have groomed the intoxicating, pearl-adorned coursers.
I have accepted the former offering: three yoked horses and eight cows that provide abundance.
Those Subandhus, like common folk in a crowd, with their wagons, sought renown—the Pajras.
That which is clung to, closely adhered to, which wriggles like a creeping insect...
The Yāduri gives me hundreds of swift, well-fed mares to enjoy.
Come close and touch me; do not think that my hairs are few.
I am covered all over with hair, like the sheep of the Gandhāris.
I honor Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, the bountiful, the Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas— the wise one like a sage, Jātavedas— who,
as a god with his upright form, performs the sacrifice well for the gods, and who, with his flame, desires the brilliance of the clarified butter, of the offered fatness.

We, the sacrificers, invoke you, the best of sacrificers, the eldest of the Aṅgirases, the inspired sage with our prayers, O radiant one, with the hymns of the sages; you who, like the sky that encompasses all, are the invoking priest of the people—
the flame-haired bull whom these clans shall favor for their impulsion, these very clans.

For he, shining with manifold splendor through his power, becomes the subduer of the malicious; like an axe, he is the subduer of the malicious. At whose onset even that which is firm yields like wood when it is struck; prevailing, he holds his ground and does not yield, like one who endures on the battlefield.
Even firm things yield to him, as is well known; with the most brilliant kindling-sticks, one offers to Agni for his protection, one offers for his protection.
He who plunges into many [woods] hews them like trees with his flame; even solid foods he consumes by his might, even solid things he destroys by his might.
Let us place that nourishment of his within our reach, he who is more clearly visible by night than by day, more visible by day than for one whose life is spent;
from him [we take] a grasp of life, as firm protection for a son.
The undecaying fires consume what has been shared and what has not been shared; the undecaying fires consume it all.
For he, roaring loudly like the host of Maruts, is the bestower of wealth upon fertile fields; he is the bestower of wealth in battle-cries.
He has taken up the oblations; he has taken them up as the worthy banner of the sacrifice.
And now, as he rejoices, full of joy, all men delight in his path, as in a path for glory.

When the *kīstas*, seeking heaven, offered worship and the Bhr̥gus invoked him with reverence—the Bhr̥gus churning [the fire]—then Agni took possession of the riches; he who is the pure sustainer of these.
May the wise one win the dear treasures; may the wise one win them.
We invoke you, the lord of all people, the common lord of all for our enjoyment; we invoke the one borne by true songs for our enjoyment.
He is the guest of men, by whose presence—as by that of a father—the immortals here and all those elsewhere come as vital strength to the gods, as food to the gods.

O Agni, you are born as the most powerful through your might, the most vigorous for the sake of the divine assembly, like wealth for the sake of the divine assembly. For your exhilaration is most vigorous, and your wisdom is most splendid.
And so, O undecaying one, they attend upon you, like obedient servants, O ageless one.

Let your hymn of praise go forth to the great Agni, who by his might overcomes the mighty, who awakens at dawn, and who bestows cattle—let it go forth to Agni. When the bearer of oblations has called out to him in all lands, he, like a singer at the head of the flames, awakens; the Hotṛ priest, the consumer of the flames, awakens.

O Agni, appearing most near to us, bring hither with the gods and with good wisdom, with great wealth and with good wisdom; O mightiest one, make for us a great vision for the enjoyment of this [earth],
O Maghavan, as a fierce one churns forth great heroic power for the singers by his strength.
This Agni was born for the support of man, the most excellent sacrificer, following the will of the *uśij*—Agni, following his own will.
All-hearing, he is like wealth to one who seeks friendship, like glory to one who seeks renown.
The undeceived Hotṛ has sat down in the place of *iḷā*, encircled in the place of *iḷā*.
We send him forth, the accomplisher of sacrifice, by the path of Truth (*ṛta*) with reverent offerings; we send him to the assembly of the gods with oblations.
Through his bringing of nourishment for us, he does not grow old, for his form is like that of a swift steed.
He whom Mātariśvan brought from afar for Manu—the god who brought light from afar.
By his even path, he instantly traverses the earthly realm; the bull, bellowing repeatedly, bestows the seed as he bellows.
Beholding with a hundred eyes, the god, victorious in the woods, establishes his seat upon the lower ridges and upon the highest ridges—Agni.

He, the wise one, the domestic priest, Agni, takes heed of the sacrifice and the rite in every house; by his mental power he takes heed of the sacrifice. By his mental power the ordainer is impelled; he has looked upon all created beings.
From whence the guest adorned with ghee was born, from whence the bearer and ordainer was born.
When they unite with his power through his will within his strengths—like the roar of Agni, like the bounty of the Maruts—for the impetuous one there is no withholding of gifts;
for he indeed stirs up the giving of wealth by his own greatness.
May he protect us from misfortune and from assault, from the curse and from assault.

All-pervading, far-reaching, and wealthy, he has placed the sacrificial ladle in his right hand; like one who crosses over, he has not relaxed his effort, nor does he relax through his desire for glory.
For every one who strives toward him, you carry the oblation among the gods.
To every doer of good he grants a boon; Agni opens wide the doors.
He has been established as the most auspicious one among the human community; Agni is the noble lord of the people at the sacrifices, the beloved lord of the people at the sacrifices.
